1.description_en:
A road is an area open to the movement of pedestrians, animals and vehicles.
It may be one-way or two-way.
It may be divided into several carriageways where there is a central median.
It includes:
- the carriageways, reserved for vehicles and animals
- the road shoulders and sidewalks, reserved for pedestrians
- the cycle paths, reserved for bicycles

2.description_en:
The carriageway is the part of the road intended for vehicle traffic.

It can be one-way or two-way.

It can be divided into several lanes.

The following are part of the carriageway:

- all lanes, except the emergency lane

- pedestrian crossings

- cycle crossings

The following are not part of the carriageway, but they can run alongside it:

- sidewalks, road shoulders or pedestrian promenades

- cycle paths

- parking bays

3.description_en:
A lane is a part of the carriageway that allows a single line of vehicles to travel.

It is bounded by solid or dashed lines and has a minimum width of 2.80 metres and a maximum width of 4 metres.




A lane is always one-way and may be:

- a travel lane: for the movement of vehicles

- an acceleration lane: to allow vehicles to enter the carriageway

- a deceleration lane: to allow vehicles leaving the carriageway to slow down

- an emergency lane: for emergency parking in case of breakdown or illness

- a reserved lane: used exclusively by a particular category of vehicle (e.g. taxis or buses)

- a specialised lane: intended for specific manoeuvres (e.g. overtaking, parking, turning)




Lanes may be prohibited to certain types of vehicles.

The owner of the road may require that vehicles travel in a lane at a mandatory minimum speed.

It is not true that it can never be crossed by pedestrians, or that two motorcycles or two mopeds can travel side by side in the same lane.

4.description_en:
An acceleration lane is used to increase the speed of vehicles entering a carriageway (on motorways or main extra-urban roads).

For example, when coming from another road or from a service area.

Parking and overtaking are prohibited in an acceleration lane.

5.description_en:
The deceleration lane is used to slow down vehicles that leave a carriageway or a priority road.

For example, it is used to exit the motorway carriageway and enter a secondary road or a service area.

Parking and overtaking are prohibited in the deceleration lane.

6.description_en:
The road shoulder is a part of the road located outside the carriageway, that is, beyond the continuous white edge line of the carriageway.

It is intended for pedestrians. As a rule, it does not allow vehicles to travel on it, and therefore vehicles may not park on it either.

7.description_en:
The sidewalk is a part of the road, outside the carriageway, that is raised or otherwise delimited and reserved for pedestrians.

Vehicles may park on it only where specific parking markings are present.

It is not true that it is reserved for pedestrians and parked vehicles when it is not raised, or that mopeds may be parked on it.

8.description_en:
A pedestrian crossing is a part of the carriageway (and therefore of the road) marked with parallel white stripes (zebra crossing), where vehicles must yield to pedestrians who are crossing.

Stopping (and therefore also parking) of vehicles on it is prohibited.

9.description_en:
A traffic island is a part of the carriageway (and therefore of the road), marked with white diagonal hatching and bordered by continuous white lines.

It helps channel vehicles in different directions.

It can be flush (painted on the road surface) or raised. If raised, it is preceded by white diagonal hatching.

Driving on it and parking on it are prohibited.

10.description_en:
The refuge island is a raised part of the road. It is intended to shelter pedestrians crossing the road, or to serve as a waiting area for them, at pedestrian crossings or at stops for public transport vehicles.

It makes it easier for passengers to get on and off trams, trolleybuses or buses.

It can be marked by fixed yellow light posts.

11.description_en:
An at-grade intersection is an intersection of two or more roads located on the same level.

It requires attention to vehicles coming from the intersecting roads.

It may be controlled by traffic lights.

12.description_en:
A grade-separated intersection is an intersection of two or more roads located at different heights.

The connection between these roads is made through infrastructure such as ramps, overpasses or underpasses.

It makes traffic flow easier, because it eliminates direct crossing between vehicles.

It is not true that the general maximum speed limits do not apply.

13.description_en:
A limited traffic zone is an area where access and circulation are restricted to predetermined hours or days, or to particular categories of users and vehicles.

It is marked by specific road signs at its beginning and end.

It is not true that it is always prohibited to motor vehicles.

14.description_en:
A pedestrian area is a zone intended for pedestrian traffic and is marked by specific road signs at its beginning and end.

In addition to pedestrians, the following may travel:

- bicycles

- vehicles serving persons with disabilities

- emergency, police, fire brigade and ambulance vehicles, with siren and flashing blue light switched on

- other categories of vehicles, if expressly permitted; e.g. zero-emission (electric) vehicles

15.description_en:
It is a section of road that allows vehicles to access private properties alongside the road (garages, courtyards, etc.).

It must be marked by a specific sign showing the issuing authority and the authorization number.

At a driveway access, a brief stop is permitted but parking is not (not even for the owner).

16.description_en:
A railway level crossing is an at-grade crossing between a road and a railway line.

A railway level crossing may have:

- barriers or half-barriers

- panels showing the distance

- an acoustic signalling device with a bell

- red lights

- St Andrew's cross

17.description_en:
A main extra-urban road has separate carriageways, or carriageways separated by a central median. Each carriageway has at least two traffic lanes. In addition:

- it is marked by specific road signs at its start and end

- junctions (intersections) may be grade-separated, but not at grade

- it has acceleration and deceleration lanes for vehicles entering and leaving, and dedicated rest and parking areas

- only certain categories of motor vehicles may use it (bicycles, mopeds and light quadricycles are not allowed)

- the general maximum speed limit is 110 km/h

- the signs are blue

It is not true that there are no bends or crests.

18.description_en:
A motorway has separate carriageways, or carriageways separated by a central median. Each carriageway has at least two traffic lanes and an emergency lane. In addition:

- it is marked by specific road signs at its start and end

- junctions (intersections) may be grade-separated, but not at grade

- it has acceleration and deceleration lanes for vehicles entering and leaving

- only certain categories of motor vehicles may use it

- it has no private access points

- it must be fenced along both sides

- the general maximum speed limit is 130 km/h

- the signs are green


The following are excluded from motorway traffic:

- passenger cars that cannot reach a speed of at least 80 km/h

- vehicles with a load that is not properly arranged and secured, or with loose, uncovered material that could scatter

- vehicles that do not have a valid periodic technical inspection, or that are in poor condition in terms of use, equipment or tyres (for example: worn tyres, faulty indicators)

- mopeds

- motorcycles with an engine displacement under 150 cm3

- agricultural machinery and work machines


On motorways, the following is prohibited:

- reversing (changing the direction of travel)

- stopping, except in cases of necessity (illness or serious vehicle breakdown), on the emergency lane for a maximum of 3 hours

- asking for or offering lifts (including at service areas)

- towing other vehicles (except trailers)

- using full-beam headlights in service areas and on sections with lighting

- racing for speed

- carrying out sales or advertising activities

19.title_en: Example of lane and carriageway use: 4-lane road
19.description_en: This is a road made up of 1 carriageway and 4 lanes. Traffic runs in both directions. As a rule, the outer lanes are used for normal driving, and the central lanes are used for overtaking. Only when traffic is heavy may vehicles drive in parallel rows. Left turns and U-turns are prohibited. Overtaking is allowed even on crests or along a bend.

20.title_en: Example of lane and carriageway use: 6-lane road
20.description_en: This is a road made up of 1 carriageway and 6 lanes (three lanes for each direction of travel). Traffic runs in both directions. As a rule, in each direction, the right lane is used for ordinary driving, and the central and left lanes are used for overtaking. Only when traffic is heavy may vehicles drive in parallel rows. Left turns and U-turns are prohibited. Overtaking is allowed even on crests or along a bend.

21.title_en: Example of use of lanes and carriageways: road with 3 carriageways and 8 lanes
21.description_en:
It is a road made up of 3 carriageways (1 two-way and 2 one-way) and 8 lanes.
The side carriageways are, as a rule, one-way. If traffic is heavy, vehicles may travel in parallel rows. Left turns, reversing and U-turns are prohibited, while overtaking is permitted even on crests or along a bend.
The central carriageway is, as a rule, two-way with 4 lanes. The side lanes are therefore used for normal driving and the central lanes for overtaking. If traffic is heavy, vehicles may travel in parallel rows. Left turns and U-turns are prohibited, while overtaking is permitted even on crests or along a bend.

22.description_en:
A vehicle is defined as any machine circulating on the road that is driven by a person (excluding those intended for children or disabled persons, such as prams or wheelchairs).
Vehicles are classified into the following categories:
- hand-drawn vehicles: pushed or pulled by a person on foot
- animal-drawn vehicles: pulled by one or more animals
- cycles: bicycles, rickshaws, kick scooters
- mopeds
- motor vehicles: motorcycles, motorcycles with sidecar (motocarrozzette), quadricycles,
- motor vehicles (autoveicoli): cars, buses, trucks, road tractors, lorry-trailer combinations (autotreni), articulated vehicles (autoarticolati), articulated buses (autosnodati), motorhomes (autocaravan)
- trolleybuses
- trailers: including caravans and semi-trailers
- agricultural machinery
- work machines

23.description_en:
These are two- or three-wheeled vehicles with a combustion engine of up to 50 cm3 displacement and a maximum speed of up to 45 km/h on level road.

They may be fitted with an automatic transmission.

Mopeds must undergo a technical inspection four years after first registration, and every two years thereafter.

Note: they do not fall within the category of motorcycles.

Light quadricycles (microcars) are treated as mopeds for the purposes of road traffic.

24.description_en:
These are two-wheeled vehicles with an engine capacity greater than 50 cm3.

They may be fitted with an automatic gearbox.

They are subject to periodic technical inspection four years after first registration, and every two years thereafter.

25.description_en:
These are vehicles with three symmetrical wheels, with an engine displacement greater than 50 cm3 and a maximum speed greater than 45 km/h.

They should not be confused with the combination of a motorcycle and a sidecar (motocarrozzetta, with asymmetrical wheels).

They must undergo a technical inspection four years after first registration, and every two years thereafter.

It is not true that they can be driven without a licence.

26.description_en:
These are four-wheeled vehicles with an unladen mass of up to 400 kg (550 kg if intended for goods transport) and a maximum engine power of up to 15 kW.
As a rule, to drive a quadricycle you must be at least 16 years old and hold a category B1 licence, unless it is a light quadricycle.

LIGHT QUADRICYCLES are those with power up to 6 kW, fitted with a petrol engine (displacement not exceeding 50 cm3), diesel or electric motor, for example microcars.
For road traffic purposes they are treated as mopeds, so they may be driven from the age of 14 with a category AM licence.

On quadricycles with an open body (quads), wearing a helmet is mandatory.
All quadricycles (light or otherwise) are subject to periodic technical inspection.
It is expressly forbidden to modify or replace the engine of a quadricycle in order to increase its speed or displacement.

28.description_en:
A passenger car (autovettura) is a four-wheeled motor vehicle intended for carrying people (maximum nine, including the driver).

Therefore, the following are not passenger cars: buses (more than nine people), valuables transport vehicles (intended for transporting valuables), and trucks (intended for transporting goods).

They may have an electric or combustion engine, and front-wheel or rear-wheel drive. They may tow drawbar trailers or trailers.

They are subject to periodic technical inspection (revisione periodica) four years after first registration and, subsequently, every two years.

29.description_en:
These are vehicles with a special body, permanently equipped for carrying and accommodating people (the maximum number is indicated on the vehicle registration document).

You may not travel standing up, and it is always necessary to fasten the seatbelt.

They are subject to periodic technical inspection four years after first registration and, subsequently, every two years.

Do not confuse them with caravans, which are trailers and not motor vehicles.

30.description_en: These are trailers, fitted with a licence plate, with a special body and equipped to be used for accommodation only while the vehicle is stationary.

31.description_en:
Trailers or semi-trailers are vehicles without an engine, intended to be towed.

Light trailers are those with a maximum laden mass of up to 750 kg.

Semi-trailers are not trailers lacking a braking system.

It is not true that they are fitted with a silencer (since they have no engine).

32.description_en:
Work machines (macchine operatrici) and agricultural machines are self-propelled (able to move by themselves) or towed machines, fitted with rubber tyres or tracks.

Self-propelled ones may carry at most three workers, including the driver, but not standing (not even, and especially not, on the trailer).



AGRICULTURAL MACHINES are intended for use in agricultural and forestry activities.

They may travel on public roads for their own transfer or for transporting agricultural products, but only if they are registered.

Agricultural machines, even exceptional ones (i.e. those exceeding the size and mass limits set for motor vehicles), may be driven with a category B licence.

Agricultural machines that do not exceed the mass and size limits for motor vehicles of the motorcycle type (motoveicoli) may be driven with category A1, A2, or A licences.

WORK MACHINES are, for example, snow-clearing vehicles, snow ploughs, vehicles used for building civil or road works, and forklift trucks for moving goods.

Non-exceptional ones (i.e. with a mass of up to 3.5 t) may be driven with a category B licence; exceptional ones require a higher licence (C).

33.description_en:
The panel for protruding loads:

- must be retroreflective

- must be applied in every case where the load protrudes from the rear, even if only slightly

- signals indivisible loads that protrude from the rear of the vehicle (for no more than 3/10 of the vehicle's length)

- if the load protrudes longitudinally across the entire width of the rear of the vehicle, two panels must be used, placed transversely at the two ends of the load

- may be placed on broken-down vehicles when they are being towed and the hazard lights are not working

- warns drivers behind the vehicle on which it is applied to proceed with particular caution

34.description_en: Signals vehicles carrying dangerous goods. They must be affixed to the front and rear of the vehicle; they are supplemented with two series of numbers indicating the type of danger and the substance being transported.

35.title_en: Panel for goods vehicles with a maximum laden mass exceeding 3.5 t
35.description_en:
They must be applied to the rear of all motor vehicles for the transport of goods whose maximum laden mass exceeds 3.5 t.

They are fluorescent/retroreflective to improve the visibility of the motor vehicles to which they are applied.

36.title_en: Panel for trailers used for goods transport with a maximum laden mass exceeding 3.5 t
36.description_en:
They must be applied to the rear of all trailers or semi-trailers for the transport of goods whose maximum laden mass exceeds 3.5 t.

They therefore identify a road train or an articulated vehicle.

They are fluorescent/retroreflective to improve the visibility of the vehicles to which they are applied.

38.description_en:
They must be applied to the rear of certain vehicles and indicate their maximum permitted speeds (on motorways and on main and secondary rural roads, respectively).

No more than two may be fitted to the same vehicle.

They must be applied to:

- goods vehicles with a mass exceeding 3.5 t, motorhomes with a mass exceeding 3.5 t, and buses with a mass exceeding 8 t

- motor quadricycles (because they have special speed limits, different from the general ones)

It is not true that a sign indicating the minimum permitted speed must be affixed to the rear of buses.

39.title_en: Driver's duties when using the road
39.description_en:
It is forbidden to:

- remove, move or soil road signs, including temporary signs such as cones or barriers. This can cause serious danger to other road users

- throw objects out of the window. Cigarette butts are especially dangerous, particularly when two-wheeled vehicles are approaching or near woods and green areas where they could start fires

- dirty the road, including the road shoulder, by dropping waste or entering the road with dirty wheels (mud, soil) or with a vehicle leaking oil or fuel.

If oil or fuel is leaking, the driver must take all necessary action to avoid danger to other road users and immediately notify the road owner or the police.

In all cases where the road is significantly dirtied, an administrative fine may be imposed.

- race at speed. A driver who takes part in unauthorised speed races on public roads is punished with imprisonment. The same applies to anyone who bets on such races.

- damage road structures and installations (fences, benches, drains, etc.).

40.title_en: Proceeding in a queue or in heavy traffic
40.description_en:
When proceeding in a queue with other vehicles:

- you must still keep a safe distance, and therefore not get too close to the vehicle in front

- do not only watch the vehicle in front, but also pay attention further ahead to check the traffic situation

- to help traffic flow, it is advisable to keep the exits of side roads clear

- do not repeatedly change lane or accelerate sharply to overtake other vehicles

It is not true that you should always keep hazard lights on or move as far left as possible to create a free lane on the right.



In heavy traffic or when queues form, you must always keep clear:

- road junctions (intersections, merges, car park entrances, etc.)

- railway level crossings and tram tracks

- pedestrian and cycle crossings

41.description_en:
When entering a built-up area you must:

- bear in mind that right-of-way at junctions may change often

- bear in mind that the flow of traffic is often obstructed or interrupted by vehicles that are stopped, pulling away or changing direction

- bear in mind that other road users (such as pedestrians and cyclists) mix more with motor traffic

- be more attentive, careful and tolerant, due to the greater number of users interacting in the urban environment

- keep your concentration while driving, even though there may be more reasons to be distracted

42.title_en: Driver behaviour towards other road users
42.description_en:
Behaviour that a vehicle driver must show towards other road users:

- in addition to complying with the specific traffic rules, the driver must maintain a correct, patient and tolerant attitude towards other road users, even when traffic slows down

- must always exercise the utmost caution, even when other drivers must give way to them

- must try to anticipate the behaviour of other users, which may not be correct

- must protect their own safety and that of others

- must respect traffic officers (even if not in uniform) and cooperate with them

- must drive at low speed over puddles or on roads covered with gravel, to avoid skidding or splashing or hitting other road users.

43.title_en: Driver behaviour towards vulnerable road users
43.description_en:
The driver must exercise greater caution towards vulnerable road users, namely persons with disabilities, the elderly, children, drivers who show uncertain driving, drivers of vehicles adapted for persons with disabilities, cyclists, pedestrians, and persons with limited mobility.



The driver must stop and yield to a visually impaired pedestrian using a white cane (blind) or a white-and-red cane (deafblind), whether or not accompanied by a guide dog, who is about to cross the road, even outside a pedestrian crossing. The driver must not frighten them with a sudden braking or the use of the horn.



When a pregnant woman or a person pushing a baby stroller is present, the driver must avoid approaching too closely with the vehicle so as not to frighten them. When parking a vehicle, it is prohibited to obstruct any sidewalk ramps, so as not to prevent pedestrians pushing a baby stroller from passing.



The driver must keep in mind that elderly people are exposed to greater dangers because, due to their age, their vision and hearing are no longer excellent. They may not pay adequate attention to vehicles, misjudge the speed of approaching vehicles, stop in the middle of the carriageway, and fail to react promptly to dangerous situations. The driver must not approach too closely, so that they do not feel threatened and react with dangerous movements.





When children are present, the driver must take into account their unpredictable behaviour and be ready to stop.

They may suddenly cross the road at a traffic light without following the rules of light signals;

They may push one another, ending up in the carriageway; near a bus stop they may run across the road to board or alight from the school bus without paying attention to approaching vehicles; they may not be visible when entering the carriageway because of parked vehicles.




When the carriageway is occupied by cyclists or pedestrians, the driver must maintain an adequate lateral safety distance when overtaking them. On extra-urban roads it is advisable to sound the horn before overtaking them (it is not true that they must be overtaken without exceeding a speed of 30 km/h).




While driving, the driver must frequently check the rear-view mirror for approaching cyclists or motorcyclists. The driver must keep in mind that the interior pillars of motor vehicles reduce visibility, making it harder to see a cyclist, motorcyclist or pedestrian. The driver must also remember that an accident, even at low speed, may cause serious physical injuries to pedestrians, cyclists and motorcyclists. Before opening a door, the driver must check that no pedestrians, cyclists or motorcyclists are approaching.




Before entering an intersection after the traffic light has turned green, the driver must wait for pedestrians to finish crossing the road.




Near a pedestrian crossing, the driver must be very cautious (especially if elderly people or children are present), and consider that:

- a pedestrian crossing the road may become unsure, suddenly turn back, or suddenly stop on the pedestrian crossing

- elderly people usually cross slowly and with difficulty

- children often behave unpredictably

- pedestrians, especially children, may suddenly emerge from between parked vehicles.




Near a taxi stand, the driver must watch for pedestrians getting on or off taxis, and slow down and stop if necessary when pedestrians cross the road without taking due precautions.

The driver may not park in taxi stands.

50.description_en:
This is a danger sign warning of a deformed road, in poor condition, broken up or with an irregular surface (usually 150 metres ahead).

It may be supplemented by a panel reading 'ESTESA' (indicating the length of the stretch), 'DISTANZA' (indicating how many metres away the hazard is), or a 'MAXIMUM SPEED LIMIT' sign.

If the background is yellow, it is used where roadworks are in progress.

When this sign is present you must:

- adjust speed to the road surface conditions (especially when towing a trailer), also to avoid excessive stress and damage to the suspension

- anticipate possible skidding by vehicles coming from the opposite direction

- hold the steering wheel firmly to control possible skidding



Do not confuse it with the 'DOSSO' (bump) or 'CUNETTA' (dip) sign.

It is not true that it warns of a series of bumps, a dip, or a stretch with reduced visibility.

It is not true that you must drive in the centre of the carriageway or watch for narrowing of the carriageway.

51.description_en:
This is a warning sign that announces (normally 150 metres ahead) a hump: a rise followed by a descent. It marks a stretch of road where the change in gradient is dangerous because visibility is limited.

It may also warn of artificial speed humps.

When this sign is present:

- Reduce speed according to visibility.

- U-turns, parking and brief stops are prohibited on both the uphill and the downhill section.

- Overtaking is prohibited on the uphill section if the road is two-way with only two lanes.

Do not confuse this sign with the 'UNEVEN ROAD' or 'DIP' sign.

52.description_en:
This is a warning sign that announces (normally 150 metres ahead) a dip: a descent followed by a rise. It marks a stretch of road that may flood during heavy rain.

When this sign is present:

- Reduce speed to keep control of the vehicle and avoid damage to the suspension.

- Hold the steering wheel with a firmer grip.

- In rain, expect water, mud and debris to collect in the dip.

Do not confuse this sign with the 'UNEVEN ROAD' or 'HUMP' sign.

It is not true that overtaking is prohibited.

53.description_en:
This is a warning sign that announces (normally 150 metres ahead) a dangerous bend to the right. It marks a stretch of road that is not straight and is dangerous because visibility is reduced.

It may be combined with a panel reading TORNANTE (hairpin bend).

When this sign is present:

- Pay particular attention to vehicles coming from the opposite direction.

- If the road is two-way with only two lanes, keep as close as possible to the right edge.

- Adjust speed to visibility and to the radius of the bend, so you can stop if an obstacle appears suddenly.

- Adjust speed to the vehicle's load.

- Take the bend more carefully if the road is wet.

- Stopping, parking, reversing and U-turns are not permitted.

- Overtaking is not permitted if the carriageway is two-way with only two lanes, even if you do not cross the white line, for example to overtake a motorcycle.

- Drive at a particularly moderate pace if you are using a temporary spare wheel.

- If the road is two-way with two lanes, move as far as possible to the right edge of the carriageway.

54.description_en:
This is a danger sign that warns (normally 150 metres ahead) of a dangerous left bend, i.e. a non-straight stretch of road that is dangerous due to reduced visibility.

It may be supplemented by a panel reading TORNANTE (hairpin bend).

When this sign is present:

- particular attention should be paid to vehicles coming from the opposite direction

- if it is placed on a two-way road with only two lanes, you must keep as close as possible to the right-hand edge

- speed must be adjusted to visibility and the radius of the bend so that you can stop in case of a sudden obstacle

- speed must be adjusted to the loading conditions of the vehicle

- the bend must be taken with more care if the road is wet

- stopping, parking, reversing and U-turns are not permitted

- overtaking is not permitted if the carriageway is two-way with only two lanes (not even if you do not cross the white line, for example to overtake a motorcycle)

- you must drive at a particularly moderate speed if using a temporary spare wheel (space-saver)

- you must move as far as possible to the right-hand edge of the carriageway if the road is two-way with 2 lanes only

55.title_en: Double bend, first to the right
55.description_en:
This is a warning sign that announces (normally 150 metres ahead) a dangerous double bend, with the first bend to the right. It marks a stretch of road that is not straight and is dangerous because visibility is reduced.

It may be supplemented:

- With a panel reading TORNANTI (hairpin bends), indicating the presence of hairpin bends.

- With an ESTESA (extent) panel, showing the length of the dangerous stretch.

- With a DISTANZA (distance) panel, showing the distance to the dangerous area.

When this sign is present:

- Pay particular attention to vehicles coming from the opposite direction.

- If the road is two-way with only two lanes, keep as close as possible to the right edge.

- Adjust speed to visibility and to the radius of the bend, so you can stop if an obstacle appears suddenly.

- Adjust speed to the vehicle's load.

- Take the bend more carefully if the road is wet.

- Stopping, parking, reversing and U-turns are not permitted.

- Overtaking is not permitted if the carriageway is two-way with only two lanes, even if you do not cross the white line, for example to overtake a motorcycle.

- Drive at a particularly moderate pace if you are using a temporary spare wheel.

- If the road is two-way with two lanes, move as far as possible to the right edge of the carriageway.

56.title_en: Double bend, first to the left
56.description_en:
This is a danger sign that warns (normally 150 metres ahead) of a dangerous double bend, the first to the left, i.e. a non-straight stretch of road that is dangerous due to reduced visibility.

It may be supplemented by:

- a panel reading TORNANTI (hairpin bends) to indicate the presence of hairpin bends

- the ESTESA (EXTENT) supplementary panel, showing the length of the dangerous section

- the DISTANZA (DISTANCE) supplementary panel, showing the distance to the dangerous zone

When this sign is present:

- particular attention should be paid to vehicles coming from the opposite direction

- if it is placed on a two-way road with only two lanes, you must keep as close as possible to the right-hand edge

- speed must be adjusted to visibility and to the radius of the bend so that you can stop in case of a sudden obstacle

- speed must be adjusted to the loading conditions of the vehicle

- the bend must be taken with more care if the road is wet

- stopping, parking, reversing and U-turns are not permitted

- overtaking is not permitted if the carriageway is two-way with only two lanes (not even if you do not cross the white line, for example to overtake a motorcycle)

- you must drive at a particularly moderate speed if using a temporary spare wheel (space-saver)

- you must move as far as possible to the right-hand edge of the carriageway if the road is two-way with 2 lanes only

57.title_en: Level crossing with barriers or half barriers
57.description_en:
This is a warning sign that announces (normally 150 metres ahead) a railway level crossing with barriers or half barriers, regardless of the number of tracks.

After the pictured sign, a half-barrier crossing has flashing red lights, and a full-barrier crossing has a steady red light.

When this sign is present, reduce speed according to how well you can see the railway line. Stop if a steady red light is on (or two flashing red lights at a half-barrier crossing), if the audible bell is sounding, or if red-and-white striped trestles are blocking the tracks.

Do not enter the level crossing if heavy traffic prevents you from clearing it.

If your vehicle stops on the tracks because of a breakdown, you must take every action needed to prevent an accident.

U-turns, reversing and parking are prohibited. Overtaking is allowed if the crossing is controlled by a traffic light or by officers, and you stay in your own direction of travel (that is, you do not enter the opposite half of the carriageway).

It is not true that you must stop if the red lights beside the barriers or half barriers are off, or that the sign is placed after the DOUBLE ST. ANDREW'S CROSS sign (which is found only at level crossings without barriers).

58.description_en:
This is a warning sign that announces (usually 150 metres ahead) a railway level crossing without barriers. It is supplemented by the corresponding distance indicator panel with three red bars.

After this sign, and before the tracks, the ST. ANDREW'S CROSS sign is installed if there is a single track, or the DOUBLE ST. ANDREW'S CROSS if there is more than one track.

When this sign is present, use maximum caution and slow down (depending on the visibility of the railway line) so that you can, if necessary, come to a halt before the crossing. Then, before crossing, make sure no trains are approaching from either the right or the left.

Prohibited: overtaking, parking, U-turns and reversing.

59.description_en:
This is a warning sign placed in the immediate vicinity of a railway crossing, generally without barriers (after the RAILWAY LEVEL CROSSING WITHOUT BARRIERS sign and the distance indicator panels). It indicates that the railway has a single track.

It may be placed either horizontally or vertically.

It requires you to stop before the stop line if a train is approaching.

It may be combined with the STOP sign when visibility is sufficient only from a short distance from the track.

It is not true that it is supplemented by a green light and a fixed red light.

60.description_en:
This is a warning sign placed in the immediate vicinity of a railway crossing without barriers (after the RAILWAY LEVEL CROSSING WITHOUT BARRIERS sign and the distance indicator panels). It indicates that the railway has more than one track.

It may be placed either horizontally or vertically.

It requires you to stop before the stop line if a train is approaching.

It urges caution before crossing, because more than one train may pass.

It may be combined with the STOP sign when visibility is insufficient.

It is not true that it may have a yellow background in the case of track work.

61.description_en:
These are warning signs located near all types of railway level crossings (with barriers, half-barriers, and without barriers).

They indicate that you are approaching a railway crossing.

They are generally placed about 150 metres (3 red bars), 100 metres (2 red bars), and 50 metres (1 red bar) from the railway crossing.

62.description_en:
This is a warning sign that announces (usually 150 metres ahead) a crossing with a tram line that is not controlled by traffic lights (both inside and outside built-up areas).

It reduces the space available for vehicle traffic.

Drivers must pay greater attention so as not to obstruct the tram's movement.

When this sign is present:

- you may overtake a moving tram on the right if there is sufficient space

- you may overtake on the right a tram stopped in the centre of the road for passenger boarding and alighting, only if the appropriate traffic island exists

- you may drive on the tracks without obstructing the tram's movement

- you must watch out for any pedestrians present at the tram stop

- you must be aware of the possible reduction in wheel grip when braking on the tracks

- keep in mind that a tram requires a longer stopping distance than cars

It is not true that it applies to trolleybus traffic or that it may be supplemented by a red-light device.

63.description_en:
This is a warning sign that announces (usually 150 metres ahead) a pedestrian crossing, both inside and outside built-up areas.

When this sign is present:

- slow down so you are ready to stop if pedestrians are crossing the carriageway

- the driver must give way to pedestrians crossing on the marked crossing.

- overtaking is not permitted for vehicles that slow down or stop to let pedestrians cross, and care must be taken not to rear-end them

- do not park or make a brief stop on top of pedestrian crossings

- if you fail to give way to pedestrians crossing on the designated crossing, you will incur a deduction of points from your licence

It is not true that it is placed at the location of a pedestrian crossing; as stated, it is placed 150 metres before it.

64.description_en:
This is a danger sign that warns (normally 150 metres ahead) of a cycle crossing (both inside and outside built-up areas), i.e. a crossing for cyclists, marked by the appropriate markings on the carriageway.

When this sign is present:

- speed must be reduced so as not to endanger cyclists, and you must be ready to stop, if necessary, to give way to cyclists crossing

- overtaking vehicles that have stopped to let cyclists cross the carriageway is not permitted

- you must not stop or park at the location of the crossing

It is not true that the sign is placed at the location of a cycle crossing; as stated, it is placed 150 metres before it.

65.description_en:
This is a warning sign that announces (usually 150 metres ahead) a dangerous descent (along which the vehicle's braking distance increases) and specifies its gradient.

When this sign is present:

- use greater caution if the road is wet

- engaging a low gear allows you to make proper use of the engine's braking action

- reduce speed to avoid rear-ending vehicles that are travelling more slowly

- avoid prolonged use of the brakes so they do not overheat (which would make braking less effective)

It is not true that you must drive with the clutch depressed.

66.description_en:
This is a warning sign that announces (usually 150 metres ahead) a dangerous uphill and specifies its gradient.

You must drive up the hill with caution, using an appropriately low gear.

It is not true that you must drive with the clutch depressed, or that it announces a stretch of road along which the vehicle's braking distance increases.

67.description_en:
This is a warning sign that announces (usually 150 metres ahead) a symmetrical narrowing, meaning a reduction in width on both sides of the carriageway, with a likely difficulty in passing vehicles coming from the opposite direction.

If it has a yellow background, it is placed where there is a road works site.

It requires you to reduce speed and, if necessary, come to a stop.



After this sign you may find the sign 'RIGHT-OF-WAY IN ALTERNATING ONE-WAY TRAFFIC' or 'GIVE WAY IN ALTERNATING ONE-WAY TRAFFIC'.

It is not true that it announces alternating one-way traffic with the obligation to give way to vehicles coming from the other direction.

68.description_en:
This is a warning sign that announces (usually 150 metres ahead) an asymmetrical narrowing on the left, meaning a reduction in width on the left side of the carriageway, with a likely difficulty in passing vehicles coming from the opposite direction.

If it has a yellow background, it is placed where there is a road works site.

It requires you to reduce speed and, if necessary, come to a stop.



It is not true that it announces alternating one-way traffic with the obligation to give way to vehicles coming from the other direction.

69.description_en:
This is a warning sign that announces (usually 150 metres ahead) an asymmetrical narrowing on the right, i.e. a narrowing of the carriageway on the right-hand side, with a likely difficulty in passing vehicles coming from the opposite direction.

If it has a yellow background, it is placed where a road works site is in progress.

It requires you to moderate your speed and, if necessary, come to a halt.

It is not true that it announces alternating single-lane traffic with an obligation to give right-of-way to vehicles coming from the other direction.

70.description_en:
This is a warning sign that announces (usually 150 metres ahead) a movable bridge.

It may be supplemented by a panel showing the operating or opening times of a movable bridge, and by the three red bar distance panel (only this one, not the two- and three-bar panels).

After the sign there is a device with flashing red lights; if it is operating, it requires you to come to a halt.

It is not true that it announces a port area, or that it requires you to stop before crossing the bridge, or that it prohibits overtaking if placed on the access road to a port area.

71.description_en:
This is a warning sign that announces (usually 150 metres ahead) a road shoulder that is yielding and not passable, creating the danger of falling into the roadside ditch.

It is advisable not to approach too closely to the right-hand edge of the road.

It is not true that it announces a damaged road surface, the presence of loose gravel on the pavement, or that it must necessarily be combined with a speed limit sign.

72.description_en:
This is a warning sign that announces (usually 150 metres ahead) a stretch of road that may become slippery (where tyre grip is reduced) under particular weather conditions specified in the supplementary panels (ice, rain).

It requires you to proceed at a moderate speed, avoid sudden manoeuvres, acceleration and braking, and increase your safety distance, as braking distance increases.

Overtaking is permitted only with particular care.

It is not true that it announces the possibility of skidding due to strong crosswinds, or that you must fit snow chains.

73.description_en:
This is a warning sign that announces (usually 150 metres ahead) a stretch of road where loose gravel may be found on the road surface.

This, in addition to reducing the vehicle's grip, may be thrown up at a distance as vehicles pass, becoming dangerous for other vehicles or for pedestrians.

It therefore requires you to keep a greater distance from the vehicle ahead and to proceed with caution where pedestrians are present, even if they are outside the carriageway.

It is not true that it announces a stretch of road subject to landslides (or falling rocks), or that, if it has a yellow background, it announces a stretch of road that is impassable due to road works.

74.description_en:
This is a danger sign that warns (normally 150 metres ahead) of places frequented by children (schools, playgrounds, gardens).

It invites you to drive at a moderate speed and to expect possible unpredictable behaviour from children (even when they are on the sidewalks).

Overtaking vehicles that have stopped to let children cross is prohibited.

It does NOT indicate the brief stop of a school bus, it is NOT placed on the rear of a school bus, and it does NOT impose a speed limit of 30 km/h.

75.description_en:
This is a danger sign that warns (normally 150 metres ahead) of a road section where domestic animals are likely to cross.

It requires you to slow down or come to a halt (and not sound your horn) if animals cross the road, show signs of fright, or do not move out of the way.

76.description_en:
This is a danger sign that warns (normally 150 metres ahead) of a road section where wild animals are likely to cross suddenly.

It requires you to slow down or come to a halt (and not sound your horn) if animals cross the road, show signs of fright, or do not move out of the way.

77.description_en:
This is a danger sign that warns (normally 150 metres ahead) that a one-way carriageway becomes a two-way road, so you may encounter vehicles travelling in the opposite direction. It indicates that the one-way traffic ends and greater caution is required.

If it has a yellow background, it is placed where roadworks are in progress.

Overtaking, where permitted, must be carried out with particular care.

It does NOT warn of alternating one-way traffic, does NOT grant right-of-way in alternating one-way sections, and does NOT require you to give way to vehicles coming from the opposite direction.

78.description_en: This is a danger sign that warns (normally 150 metres ahead) of an intersection of two or more roads (urban or rural) controlled by a roundabout.

79.title_en: Road leading onto a quay or embankment
79.description_en:
This is a warning sign that announces (normally 150 meters ahead) that the road leads onto a harbor quay, a pier, the embankment of a river or canal, and therefore the danger of falling into the water.

Particular caution must be exercised, especially at night, to avoid falling into the water, especially if reversing maneuvers will have to be carried out.

It is not true that it announces a road leading onto a movable bridge or that it refers only to passenger cars.

80.description_en:
This is a warning sign that announces (normally 150 meters ahead) the danger of rocks falling from the left, with the consequent presence of them on the carriageway.

It is advisable to moderate speed to avoid hitting any rocks that have fallen onto the carriageway, avoid long stops, and be alert for possible sudden braking by vehicles ahead.

It is not true that overtaking is prohibited.

81.description_en:
This is a warning sign that announces (normally 150 meters ahead) the danger of rocks falling from the right, with the consequent presence of them on the carriageway.

It is advisable to moderate speed to avoid hitting any rocks that have fallen onto the carriageway, avoid long stops, and be alert for possible sudden braking by vehicles ahead.

It is not true that you cannot drive at more than 30 km/h.

82.title_en: Advance warning of vertical traffic light
82.description_en:
This is a warning sign that announces (normally 150 meters ahead) a traffic light with the lights arranged vertically: speed must be moderated so that you can stop if necessary.

The yellow disc may be replaced by a flashing yellow light.

If it has a yellow background, it is placed before a road works site.

It is mandatory on extra-urban roads before a traffic light.

It is not true that it may have a steady yellow light in the center or the red disc replaced by a flashing red light.

83.title_en: Advance warning of horizontal traffic light
83.description_en:
This is a warning sign that announces (normally 150 meters ahead) a traffic light with the lights arranged horizontally: speed must be moderated so that you can stop if necessary.

The yellow disc may be replaced by a flashing yellow light.

If it has a yellow background, it is placed before a road works site.

It is mandatory on extra-urban roads before a traffic light.

It is not true that it may have a steady yellow light in the center or the red disc replaced by a flashing red light.

84.description_en:
It is a danger sign that warns (normally 150 metres ahead) of areas where low-level flight of aeroplanes may occur, and therefore the possibility of sudden dazzling or loud noise.

It is placed in the vicinity of airports and runways used for the takeoff and landing of aeroplanes.

85.description_en:
It is a danger sign that warns (normally 150 metres ahead) of a stretch of road subject to sudden, strong gusts of crosswind (for example the exit of a tunnel, a viaduct, or a bridge).

It indicates to proceed with caution, holding the steering wheel firmly and anticipating possible swerving of vehicles coming from the opposite direction.

The danger is greater for two-wheeled vehicles and for all vehicles with a large lateral surface area, especially when travelling empty. This includes vehicles with canvas covers, panel vans, vehicles towing trailers, and vehicles with bulky luggage on the roof (because the wind exerts a greater overturning force). For these vehicles there is an obligation to slow down and, if necessary, stop.

It is not true that the danger is greater at the entrance to tunnels (it is greater at the exit).

It is not true that it indicates the direction from which the wind is coming.

86.description_en:
It is a danger sign that warns (normally 150 metres ahead) of the proximity of areas beside the road at high risk of fire (for example, a forest that is easily flammable).

It must be supplemented by the supplementary panel ESTESA, which indicates the length of the stretch of road affected.

If the driver or any passengers do not obey the prohibition on throwing lit cigarettes out of the window, a fire may break out.

It is advisable not to stop on dry grass or scrub with a vehicle fitted with a catalytic converter (as the catalytic converter reaches high temperatures).

It is not true that it prohibits transit to vehicles carrying explosives or easily flammable products.

87.description_en:
It is a danger sign that warns (normally 150 metres ahead) of a general danger, different from those indicated by the other danger signs.

Below the sign, a supplementary panel specifying the type of danger is mandatory (for example RAILWAY CROSSING, ICE, SNOW CLEARING IN PROGRESS, WORK VEHICLES IN OPERATION, etc.).

It may be used without supplementary panels to indicate a general danger in an emergency.

It indicates to proceed with caution.

100.description_en:
It is a prohibition sign and prohibits transit to all vehicles, therefore prohibiting traffic in both directions.

It applies 24 hours a day but may have a limited validity period, indicated on a supplementary panel.

It is placed at both accesses to the road.

It also applies to vehicles without an engine (for example bicycles) and to electric cars, but not to pedestrians. It is not true that it allows entry onto the road for parking or for loading and unloading operations.

101.title_en: Prohibition of through traffic for articulated lorries and semi-trailers
101.description_en:
This is a prohibition sign and forbids entry to the categories of vehicles shown in the figure, in particular articulated lorries and semi-trailers.

It is placed at both access points to the road.

102.description_en:
It is a prohibition sign and prohibits all vehicles from entering a road that is accessible from the other side (therefore a one-way road).

It is in effect 24 hours a day (therefore also during night hours).

It also applies to vehicles without a motor and to taxis.

103.description_en:
It is a prohibition sign and prohibits all vehicles from overtaking motor vehicles (including electric ones), except mopeds and motorcycles.

In addition, where this sign is present, you may overtake non-motorized vehicles (bicycles, hand-propelled vehicles, horse-drawn carriages, animal-drawn vehicles), motorcycles and mopeds.

Note: the no-overtaking prohibition applies to all motor vehicles, including mopeds and motorcycles.

It also applies if the maneuver could be completed within the half of the carriageway without crossing the solid line.

It is valid 24 hours and can be found on both urban and rural roads.

It may be supplemented by the supplementary panel CONTINUES, for example after an intersection, to indicate that the prohibition continues.

104.description_en:
This is an end-of-restriction sign (end of prohibition) and indicates the end of the overtaking ban previously imposed.

In practice, it means that from this point onwards overtaking is permitted, provided it is carried out without crossing any solid white line.

It is valid for 24 hours and can be found on both urban and non-urban roads.

It does not impose a particular speed limit.

105.title_en: Overtaking prohibition for lorries exceeding 3.5 t
105.description_en: This is a prohibition sign and forbids overtaking to goods vehicles with a laden mass exceeding 3.5 tonnes only. Only vehicles without an engine may overtake.

106.title_en: End of overtaking prohibition for lorries exceeding 3.5 t
106.description_en: This is an end-of-restriction sign (end of prohibition) and indicates the end of the overtaking ban previously imposed on vehicles with a laden mass exceeding 3.5 tonnes that are not intended for the carriage of passengers.

107.title_en: Compulsory minimum following distance of 70 metres
107.description_en:
This is a prohibition sign and requires you to keep a distance of at least 70 metres from the vehicle ahead (the one in front, not the one behind).

It also applies to motorcycles and when travelling at low speed.

108.description_en:
This is a prescriptive (prohibition) sign that sets the maximum speed allowed for all vehicles (in this case 80 km/h). It takes effect immediately after the sign.

It is valid 24 hours a day and can also appear on motorways. As noted, it applies to all vehicles, including motorcycles.

It does not allow overtaking at a speed above the indicated limit.

109.description_en:
This is an end-of-prohibition sign that marks the end of the maximum speed limit.

From this point on, you may drive at a speed above the indicated limit, but you must not exceed the general limit in force for that type of road.

110.description_en: This is a prohibition sign. It bans the use of any audible warning device (horn, trumpet horns), except in cases of immediate danger or when transporting seriously injured or ill people.

111.description_en:
This is a prohibition sign. It bans pedestrians from using that road.

It allows traffic by all vehicles.

It is valid 24 hours a day.

112.description_en:
This is a prohibition sign. It bans all hand-propelled vehicles (for example, handcarts) from using that road.

It allows pedestrians and all other animal-drawn or motor vehicles.

113.description_en:
This is a prohibition sign. It bans all animal-drawn vehicles (for example carriages or other vehicles pulled by horses or donkeys) from using that road.

All other vehicles are allowed to use the road (including hand-propelled vehicles and motor vehicles).

It is valid 24 hours a day.

It is not true that animal-drawn vehicles are allowed if they have tyres.

114.description_en:
This is a prohibition sign. It bans cycles (bicycles, tandems, pedal-powered quadricycles) from using that road.

Pedestrians and all other vehicles are allowed to use the road (including motor quadricycles, mopeds, and motorcycles).

It is valid 24 hours a day.

115.description_en:
This is a prohibition sign. It bans all motorcycles from using that road, even if they do not exceed 125 cm3 or have a safety cabin.

All other vehicles are allowed to use the road (including bicycles, mopeds, tricycles, quadricycles, and cars).

Be careful not to confuse motorcycles with mopeds.

116.title_en: No entry for all motor vehicles and three- or four-wheeled motor vehicles
116.description_en:
This is a prohibition sign. It bans all motor vehicles and motorized vehicles with three or more wheels from using that road: tricycles, quadricycles, cars, trucks, and buses.

It does not apply to vehicles without an engine (bicycles, carts, etc.), motorcycles, and mopeds.

It is not true that taxi cars are allowed to use the road.

117.description_en:
This is a prohibition sign. It bans all buses from using that road, including tourist and school buses.

Pedestrians and all other vehicles are allowed to use the road.

It is not true that it is valid only on weekdays.

118.title_en: Prohibition on transit for lorries exceeding 3.5 t
118.description_en:
This is a prohibition sign. It bans all motor vehicles carrying goods (lorries, articulated lorries, road trains) with a maximum laden mass exceeding 3.5 t from using that road.

It therefore allows the transit of vehicles intended for carrying people even if they exceed 3.5 t (for example buses, caravans, etc.).

It may be fitted with a supplementary panel showing a different permitted mass limit.

119.title_en: Prohibition on transit for lorries exceeding 6.5 t
119.description_en:
This is a prohibition sign. It bans all motor vehicles carrying goods (lorries, articulated lorries, road trains) or special-use vehicles (concrete mixers, etc.) with a maximum laden mass exceeding the value shown on the sign (in this case: 6.5 t) from using that road.

It therefore allows the transit of vehicles intended for carrying people even if they exceed 6.5 t (for example buses, caravans, etc.).

120.title_en: Prohibition on transit for motor vehicles towing a trailer
120.description_en:
This is a prohibition sign. It bans all vehicles towing a trailer (intended for either goods or passenger transport) from using that road.

It may be supplemented by a panel that permits towing trailers with a mass not exceeding the value shown on that panel.

It therefore bans caravans, boat trailers, road trains and articulated lorries. It allows vehicles with a drawbar trailer (considered an integral part of the vehicle) and articulated-chassis (semi-integral) vehicles.

121.title_en: Prohibition on transit for agricultural machinery
121.description_en:
This is a prohibition sign. It bans wheeled and tracked agricultural machinery, agricultural tractors and agricultural trailers from using that road.

It allows transit for all other types of vehicles, including work machines (snow ploughs, road-works vehicles, etc.) and road tractors for semi-trailers (the front part of an articulated vehicle).

It is valid 24 hours a day.

It is not true that it is found only on the road network of farms, or that agricultural machinery is permitted to use the road during fairs.

122.title_en: Prohibition on transit for vehicles carrying dangerous goods
122.description_en:
This is a prohibition sign. It bans vehicles carrying dangerous goods (petrol, toxic or radioactive materials, corrosive acids, etc.) from using that road.

The sign does not refer to the fuel (petrol, diesel, methane gas, LPG) contained in the vehicle's fuel tank.

123.title_en: Prohibition of transit for vehicles carrying flammable or explosive materials
123.description_en:
It is a prohibition sign. It prohibits transit for vehicles carrying explosive and/or easily flammable products. It also applies to trailers.

The sign does not refer to the fuel (petrol, diesel, methane gas, LPG) contained in the vehicle's tank.

It is not true that it requires caution when vehicles carrying explosives pass.

124.title_en: Prohibition of transit for vehicles carrying products that can contaminate water
124.description_en:
It is a prohibition sign. It prohibits transit for vehicles carrying substances that can contaminate water. It also applies to trailers.

It therefore does not refer to empty tanks or to vehicles carrying water, for example road water sprinklers.

125.title_en: Prohibition of transit for vehicles wider than 2.30 metres
125.description_en:
It is a prohibition sign. It indicates the maximum width of vehicles that may use the road.

In this case it prohibits transit for all vehicles (motorised and non-motorised) wider than 2.30 m.

It is placed on both urban and non-urban roads. It may be found, for example, before a narrow point. It applies 24 hours a day.

It is not true that it indicates the width of the road or of the narrow point.

126.title_en: Prohibition of transit for vehicles taller than 3.50 metres
126.description_en:
It is a prohibition sign. It indicates the maximum height of vehicles that may use the road.

In this case it prohibits transit for vehicles whose height, measured from the road surface, exceeds 3.50 metres.

It may be found both inside and outside built-up areas. It may be found, for example, where the road passes under a bridge (not over a railway). It applies 24 hours a day.

It is not true that it indicates the height of the passage.

127.title_en: Prohibition of transit for vehicles longer than 10 metres
127.description_en: It is a prohibition sign. It prohibits transit for all vehicles with an overall length greater than the figure shown (in this case 10 metres). It also applies to vehicle combinations, for example a car towing a caravan if together they exceed 10 metres, and to buses. It applies 24 hours a day.

128.title_en: No entry for vehicles with mass over 7.00 t
128.description_en:
This is a prohibition sign. It prohibits entry to all vehicles whose actual (total) mass exceeds the value shown.

With the addition of a supplementary panel, it can prohibit the simultaneous passage of several vehicles, indicating the maximum number of vehicles that may cross the bridge at the same time.

It is generally placed before a location where there may be a risk of collapse, such as a bridge. It is valid 24 hours a day.

129.title_en: No entry for vehicles with axle mass over 2.5 t
129.description_en:
This is a prohibition sign. It prohibits entry to all vehicles whose mass on the most heavily loaded axle exceeds the value shown.

It is generally placed before a location where there may be a risk of collapse, such as a bridge. It is valid 24 hours a day.

130.description_en:
This is an end-of-restriction sign. It indicates the end of the restrictions (prohibitions or obligations) previously imposed.

It does NOT indicate the end of a hazard previously signalled.

131.description_en:
This is a prohibition sign. It prohibits parking and stopping, or any voluntary temporary suspension of the vehicle's movement (applies to all types of vehicles, including buses and taxis).

An forced halt is permitted in cases of force majeure (red traffic light, traffic congestion, etc.).

Unless supplementary plates state otherwise, it is valid 24 hours a day, every day, including within built-up areas.

If the prohibition is not observed, forced towing of the vehicle is always ordered.

It prohibits parking and stopping only on the side of the road where it is placed.

When combined with the supplementary panel END, it indicates the end of the no stopping and no parking restriction (which still applies to the preceding section).

132.description_en:
This is a prohibition sign. It prohibits parking the vehicle but allows brief stops.

Outside built-up areas it is valid 24 hours a day; within built-up areas, from 8:00 to 20:00, unless otherwise indicated.

It may be supplemented by panels indicating its start, continuation, or end.

It ceases to apply after the first intersection, unless repeated.

It prohibits parking only on the side of the road where it is placed.

When combined with the supplementary panel START, it indicates the start of the no parking restriction from the section beyond the sign.

When combined with the supplementary panel CONTINUES, it indicates no parking in the section before and after the sign. (It does NOT indicate permanent no parking.)

When combined with the supplementary panel END, it indicates the end of the no parking restriction (which still applies to the preceding section).

When combined with the supplementary panel EXCEPTION, it permits parking for the vehicles listed on the panel (for example, buses).

When combined with the supplementary panel WEEKDAY TIME BAND, it prohibits parking only on working days within the indicated time band.

When combined with the supplementary panel FORCED REMOVAL ZONE, it indicates an area where no parking is in force and vehicles will be removed.

133.description_en: It is a prohibition sign. In urban areas, it prohibits parking during particular hours so that road-cleaning machinery can clean the road. (See no parking sign)

134.title_en: Flexible parking regulation in built-up area
134.description_en:
It is a composite prohibition sign that regulates parking. It allows parking only during the hours indicated and prohibits it at other times.

A brief stop is always permitted 24 hours a day.

In this case, parking is allowed from 9 to 17 and from 20 to 7, and prohibited from 7 to 9 and from 17 to 20.

135.description_en:
It is a prescription (prohibition) sign. It prohibits parking at the location where it is placed. It indicates the exit of a driveway access, meaning the area for vehicles to access adjacent properties. It is valid 24 hours a day. It allows a brief stop provided the vehicle does not obstruct access.

To be valid, it must show the name of the authority that granted the authorization, and the number and year of issue.

It may be placed on both urban and extra-urban roads.

136.description_en: It is a prescription (prohibition) sign representing an exception to the no parking prohibition. It allows parking for a particular category of vehicles (in this case, vehicles serving persons with disabilities displaying the appropriate permit) and prohibits parking for all other vehicles.

137.description_en:
It indicates an authorized parking area, meaning an equipped and organized area for parking for an unlimited time (24 hours a day), unless otherwise indicated.

It may be supplemented with a panel showing:

- the distance

- the time limitation

- the categories for which parking is reserved or those excluded

- the times and fees

- the arrangement of vehicles

It is not true that it indicates a parking area with a parking meter, or that it may be supplemented with a panel showing the available surface area.

138.description_en: The sign announces a parking area ahead, in the direction of the arrow, in this case 300 metres away.

150.description_en:
This is a mandatory sign (prescription). It indicates that the only permitted direction is straight ahead.

It is placed before an intersection (on both one-way and two-way roads). It does not allow a right or left turn and requires drivers to continue straight ahead.

It does not rule out vehicles coming from the opposite direction (it should not be confused with the one-way traffic sign, which has a rectangular base).

It does not mean that single-file traffic is required.

151.description_en:
This is a mandatory sign (prescription). It indicates that the only permitted direction is to the left.

It is placed before an intersection (on both one-way and two-way roads). It does not allow a right turn or going straight ahead, and requires drivers to turn left.

It does not mean that it is mandatory to pass to the left of an obstacle on the carriageway, nor does it signal an upcoming left-hand bend.

152.title_en: Advance notice of mandatory left turn
152.description_en:
This is a mandatory sign (prescription). It indicates that the only permitted direction at the next intersection is to the left.

It precedes a MANDATORY LEFT DIRECTION sign, so it is placed before an intersection where a right turn or going straight ahead is not allowed, and only a left turn is permitted.

It may be supplemented by a panel showing the distance to the intersection (the point where the requirement applies).

153.description_en:
This is a mandatory sign (prescription). It indicates that the only permitted direction is to the right.

It is placed before an intersection (on both one-way and two-way roads). It does not allow a left turn or going straight ahead, and requires drivers to turn right.

It does not mean that it is mandatory to pass to the right of an obstacle on the carriageway, nor does it signal an upcoming right-hand bend.

154.title_en: Advance notice of mandatory right turn
154.description_en:
This is a mandatory (obligation) sign. It indicates that the only permitted direction at the next intersection is a right turn.

It precedes a MANDATORY RIGHT TURN sign, so it is placed before an intersection where turning left or going straight is not permitted, only turning right.

It may be supplemented by a panel showing the distance to the intersection (the point where the obligation applies).

155.title_en: Advance notice of mandatory diversion for trucks in transit
155.description_en:
This is a mandatory (obligation) sign. It indicates the only permitted direction for the category of vehicles shown in the figure (in this case, right).

It applies only to the vehicles shown in the figure (trucks exceeding 3.5 t). It does not apply to trucks that do not exceed that mass.

It requires these vehicles to turn right, and prohibits going straight and turning left.

156.description_en:
This is a mandatory (obligation) sign. It indicates that the only permitted directions are right and left.

So the sign allows turning right and left, but prohibits going straight ahead.

It does not indicate a dangerous fork in the road.

157.title_en: Permitted directions straight ahead and right
157.description_en:
This is a mandatory (obligation) sign. It indicates that the only permitted directions are right and straight ahead.

So the sign allows turning right and proceeding straight, but prohibits turning left.

It does not indicate a dangerous fork in the road, nor does it indicate keeping as far as possible to the right edge of the carriageway at all times.

158.title_en: Permitted directions straight ahead and left
158.description_en:
This is a mandatory (obligation) sign. It indicates that the only permitted directions are left and straight ahead.

So the sign allows turning left and proceeding straight, but prohibits turning right.

It does not indicate a dangerous fork in the road, nor does it indicate keeping as close as possible to the centre line of the carriageway at all times.

159.description_en:
This is a mandatory regulatory sign (obligation). It obliges drivers to pass to the left of an obstacle (traffic island, refuge island, roadworks, central median, etc.), thus leaving the obstacle on their right.

It is NOT true that it can be preceded by the ROUNDABOUT sign.

It is NOT true that it obliges drivers to turn left (there is no intersection).

160.description_en:
This is a mandatory regulatory sign (obligation). It obliges drivers to pass to the right of an obstacle (traffic island, refuge island, roadworks, central median, etc.), thus leaving the obstacle on their left.

It is NOT true that it obliges drivers to turn right (there is no intersection).

161.description_en:
This is a mandatory regulatory sign (obligation). It indicates to drivers the only permitted passages for going around an obstacle (traffic island, refuge island, roadworks, central median, etc.).

You may pass on the left, leaving the obstacle on your right, or pass on the right, leaving the obstacle on your left.

It is NOT true that it obliges drivers to turn (there is no intersection).

It is NOT true that it is preceded by the ROUNDABOUT sign.

162.description_en:
This is a mandatory regulatory sign. It is placed before the entrance to an area where roundabout circulation is required (an intersection, a square, etc.).

It obliges drivers to circulate in the direction indicated by the arrows.

On extra-urban roads it is preceded by the triangular danger warning sign ROUNDABOUT AHEAD (CIRCOLAZIONE ROTATORIA).

The sign is placed before the intersection on the right-hand side.

It is NOT true that it is placed on the central illuminated column of a roundabout, or that it is combined with the MANDATORY PASSAGE ON THE LEFT sign.

163.description_en:
This is a mandatory regulatory sign. It indicates the speed limit below which driving is prohibited (minimum speed limit).

It therefore prohibits traffic to vehicles that are unable to comply with the requirement.

Although it is necessary to drive at a speed higher than the one indicated, drivers must nevertheless respect the maximum speed limits for the type of road being travelled.

164.description_en:
It is a prescription sign. It indicates the end of the minimum speed limit.

It therefore allows driving both at a speed lower than and higher than the one indicated, always within the maximum speed limits in force for that road.

165.description_en:
It is a prescription sign (obligation). It allows passage only to vehicles fitted with snow chains or winter tyres.

The sign is found on roads that, under particular conditions, are snow-covered or icy, so caution is required.

It is not true that it pre-signals the kilometre point beyond which the use of chains is compulsory, nor that it prohibits circulation to vehicles fitted with tyres whose tread depth is less than 3 millimetres.

166.description_en:
It is a prescription sign (obligation). It indicates the start of a pedestrian boulevard/area (reserved for pedestrian traffic).

Therefore it does not allow vehicles to pass.

It is valid 24 hours a day.

It does not indicate a pedestrian crossing or a pedestrian and cycle path (other signs are used for these).

167.description_en:
It is a prescription sign (obligation). It indicates the end of a pedestrian boulevard/area (reserved for pedestrian traffic).

Therefore it indicates that from this point onward pedestrians no longer travel on a reserved route.

It is not true that it prohibits pedestrians from crossing the road, nor that it indicates the end of a pedestrian crossing.

168.description_en:
It is a prescription sign (obligation). It indicates the start of a track, lane, route or itinerary reserved for cycles (bicycles).

Therefore it allows neither vehicles nor pedestrians to pass.

It does not indicate a cycle crossing (another sign is present for this).

169.description_en:
This is a mandatory sign (prescription). It indicates the end of a track, lane, path or route reserved for velocipedes (bicycles).

It is not true that bicycles (and/or pedestrians) are no longer allowed to pass, or that it indicates the end of a cycle crossing.

170.description_en:
This is a mandatory sign (prescription). It indicates the start of a path, track or lane reserved for velocipedes (bicycles), running alongside and parallel to a sidewalk, a pedestrian promenade, or any other route reserved for pedestrians.

Therefore, it does not permit the passage of motor vehicles.

It is not true that it is placed where a mixed boulevard is reserved for both pedestrians and cyclists (they are separated).

171.title_en: End of cycle track alongside the sidewalk
171.description_en:
This is a mandatory sign (prescription). It indicates the end of a path, track or lane reserved for velocipedes (bicycles), running alongside and parallel to a sidewalk, a pedestrian promenade, or any other route reserved for pedestrians.

It is not true that it prohibits all two-wheeled vehicles or pedestrians from passing.

172.description_en:
This is a mandatory sign (prescription). It indicates the start of a path, boulevard or route reserved for the use of pedestrians and cyclists.

Therefore, it does not permit the passage of motor vehicles.

It is not true that it is placed where a cycle path runs alongside a path reserved for pedestrians (the path is single and for shared use).

173.title_en: End of shared pedestrian and cycle path
173.description_en:
This is a mandatory sign (prescription). It indicates the end of a path, boulevard or route reserved for the use of pedestrians and cyclists.

It is not true that it prohibits bicycles or pedestrians from passing.

174.title_en: Route reserved for pack and saddle animals
174.description_en:
This is a mandatory (prescriptive) sign. It indicates the start of a route or passage reserved for pack and saddle animals (for example, horses).

It prohibits all vehicles (including cycles) and pedestrians from using it.

It is not true that it is placed near a riding school, that it warns of stray animals, or that it imposes an obligation to give way to crossing animals.

175.title_en: End of route reserved for pack and saddle animals
175.description_en:
This is a mandatory (prescriptive) sign. It indicates the end of a route or passage reserved for pack and saddle animals (for example, horses).

It is not true that it prohibits the passage of animals.

176.description_en:
This is a mandatory (prescriptive) sign. It indicates a customs crossing point with a country that is not part of the European Community (a non-EU country), where stopping is compulsory.

It therefore means that you must slow down and stop at the customs post even if you have no goods or items to declare.

177.description_en:
The ALT POLIZIA sign must be placed to indicate a road checkpoint set up by police forces, where stopping is compulsory.

The sign is portable (mobile use). It must be placed at an appropriate distance from the checkpoint and must be visible in good time and with safety, so that the driver can adjust their driving, taking into account the horizontal and vertical alignment of the road and the prevailing speed of vehicles on the section leading up to the checkpoint.

The sign must be repeated at the level of the stopping point. Both signs must be positioned so as not to create a danger or harm to road safety. The sign may be repeated in the language of the neighbouring state when the checkpoint is near the border.

178.description_en:
This is a mandatory (prescriptive) sign. It indicates a motorway station (controlled motorway access) where stopping is compulsory.

It therefore imposes the obligation to slow down and stop for motorway toll procedures.

200.description_en:
It is a mandatory sign (right-of-way). It requires giving way to vehicles approaching from both the right and the left on the road being crossed.

It may be found (both outside and inside built-up areas), for example:

- on a secondary road that does not have right-of-way

- on acceleration lanes for merging onto a motorway

- on slip roads connecting to a motorway

- combined with a traffic light; in that case it applies when the traffic light is flashing yellow.

It requires the utmost caution to avoid accidents, particularly reducing speed and, if necessary, stopping. It is not mandatory to stop at the junction if, by slowing down, you can see that no vehicles are approaching from either the right or the left.

It may be installed before the junction, within 10 metres in town and within 25 metres outside town.

On rural roads it is preceded by the GIVE WAY ADVANCE WARNING sign.

It is not true that it may be preceded by the RIGHT-OF-WAY sign, or that it is found on roads with right-of-way.

201.description_en:
It is a mandatory sign (right-of-way). It announces the upcoming presence of a GIVE WAY sign and indicates the distance to the junction where you will have to give way.

It indicates that you should slow down so that you can stop if there are vehicles to which you must give way.

It is placed on rural roads on which you do not have right-of-way.

202.description_en:
It is a mandatory sign (right-of-way). It requires stopping at the transverse stop line, even if no one is there, and giving way to vehicles approaching from both the right and the left.

It may be found (both outside and inside built-up areas), for example:

- generally, at junctions with poor visibility and particular danger

- at a railway level crossing

- at a junction with a road that has right-of-way

- combined with a traffic light; in that case it applies when the traffic light is flashing yellow.

It may be installed before the junction, within 10 metres in town and within 25 metres outside town.

On rural roads it is preceded by the STOP ADVANCE WARNING sign.

It is not true that it announces the obligation to stop and give way on alternating one-way traffic sections.

It is not true that it requires stopping only at a customs checkpoint, or only when other vehicles are crossing (you must always stop, even if you cannot see anyone).

203.description_en:
It is a mandatory sign (right-of-way). It announces the upcoming presence of a STOP AND GIVE WAY sign.
