You must begin to reduce speed so that you are ready to stop mandatorily at the STOP sign, and give way to traffic from both the right and the left.

204.title_en: Junction with priority to the right
204.description_en:
It is a mandatory sign (right-of-way). It announces a junction (normally 150 metres ahead) where the general rule of giving way to the right applies.

It requires proceeding at particularly moderate speed, giving way to vehicles approaching from the right, and making sure that vehicles approaching from the left are ready to give way to you.

It is not found on a stretch of road with right-of-way.

205.description_en:
It is a mandatory sign (right-of-way). It warns of a junction (normally 150 metres ahead) where you have right-of-way over vehicles entering from the side roads on the right and left (those side roads have no right-of-way).

It loses its effect when a traffic officer is directing traffic.

It may be preceded by the RIGHT-OF-WAY sign.

It still requires you to slow down, making sure that the vehicles crossing or joining from the right and left are prepared to give way.

It is not true that it is placed on motorways, where there cannot be at-grade junctions.

206.title_en: T-junction with right-of-way to the right
206.description_en:
It is a mandatory sign (right-of-way). It warns of a junction with a secondary road (without right-of-way) that joins from the right (a 'T' junction), where you have right-of-way over vehicles coming from that road.

It still requires you to slow down, making sure that the crossing vehicles are prepared to give way.

It is not true that it is placed on motorway access ramps.

207.title_en: T-junction with right-of-way to the left
207.description_en:
It is a mandatory sign (right-of-way). It warns of a junction with a secondary road (without right-of-way) that joins from the left (a 'T' junction), where you have right-of-way over vehicles coming from that road.

It still requires you to slow down, making sure that the crossing vehicles are prepared to give way.

It is not true that it is placed on motorway access ramps.

208.description_en:
It is a mandatory sign (right-of-way). It warns of a merge from the right via an acceleration lane, where you have right-of-way over the vehicles merging into your road.

It is normally placed more than 150 metres before the merging point.

The GIVE WAY sign is placed on the connecting ramp (the side merging road).

It urges extreme caution to avoid accidents, helping or at least not hindering the merging vehicles.

It is not true that it may be preceded by the GIVE WAY sign (which is instead placed on the side merging road).

It is not true that it allows a right turn at the next junction, since it is an acceleration lane, which is a one-way carriageway.

209.description_en:
It is a mandatory sign (right-of-way). It warns of a merge from the left via an acceleration lane, where you have right-of-way over the vehicles merging into your road.

It is normally placed more than 150 metres before the merging point.

The GIVE WAY sign is placed on the connecting ramp (the side merging road).

It urges extreme caution to avoid accidents, helping or at least not hindering the merging vehicles.

It is not true that it may be preceded by the GIVE WAY sign (which is instead placed on the side merging road).

It is not true that it allows a right turn at the next junction, since it is an acceleration lane, which is a one-way carriageway.

210.description_en:
It is a priority (precedenza) regulatory sign. It indicates the start of an urban or non-urban road on which vehicles have right-of-way.

It may be repeated in a smaller format before and after each intersection, and may be combined with the ANDAMENTO DELLA STRADA PRINCIPALE (main road layout) panel.

It implies that GIVE WAY or STOP signs are present on the crossing roads.

Where this sign is shown, you must still give way to vehicles with a flashing blue light and siren in operation.

You must still reduce speed near intersections and make sure vehicles coming from side roads give way.

It is not true that it is placed exclusively on busy non-urban roads, that right-of-way applies only until leaving the built-up area, or that it is placed only on state roads.

211.title_en: End of right-of-way road (Fine del diritto di precedenza)
211.description_en:
It is a priority (precedenza) regulatory sign. It indicates the end of an urban or non-urban road on which vehicles have right-of-way.

After this sign, you must generally give way to vehicles coming from the right, unless a GIVE WAY or STOP sign requires you to give way to vehicles from the left as well.

The sign tells you to proceed with greater caution because you no longer have right-of-way.

It is not true that it requires you to stop at the intersection (unless a STOP sign is present), that it announces the end of a previously imposed obligation (the RIGHT-OF-WAY sign is not a mandatory sign), or that it always announces an intersection with right-of-way from the right.

212.title_en: Give way in alternating one-way traffic (Dare precedenza nei sensi unici alternati)
212.description_en:
It is a priority (precedenza) regulatory sign. It requires you to give way to vehicles coming from the opposite direction. It is found where a two-way road has a bottleneck (for example, part of the carriageway is closed for roadworks) that allows only one line of vehicles to pass.

At the bottleneck, two-way traffic temporarily ends and alternating one-way traffic begins. In effect, this sign requires you to give way in alternating one-way traffic.

If the sign, a traffic light and a traffic officer are all present, the traffic officer takes precedence:
- You must give way if the traffic light is off or flashing yellow.
- You have priority if the traffic light is green, or if it is red but the traffic officer signals you to proceed.

It is not true that it is found before any narrowing of the carriageway.

213.title_en: Right-of-way in alternating one-way traffic (Diritto di precedenza nei sensi unici alternati)
213.description_en:
It is a priority (precedenza) regulatory sign. It indicates that you have right-of-way over vehicles coming from the opposite direction. It is found where a two-way road has a bottleneck (for example, part of the carriageway is closed for roadworks) that allows only one line of vehicles to pass.

At the bottleneck, two-way traffic temporarily ends and alternating one-way traffic begins. In effect, this sign indicates right-of-way in alternating one-way traffic.

When this sign is shown, you must still proceed with caution and pass through the bottleneck only after making sure that vehicles coming from the opposite direction have given way to you.

If the sign, a traffic light and a traffic officer are all present, the traffic officer takes precedence:
- You have right-of-way if the traffic light is green or off, or flashing yellow.
- You have right-of-way if the traffic light is red but the traffic officer signals you to proceed.
- You must give way if the traffic light is off and the traffic officer orders you to stop.

250.title_en: The line along the centre of the carriageway (La striscia lungo il centro della carreggiata)
250.description_en:
On all roads, the centre line may be solid (continua) or dashed (discontinua, tratteggiata). A solid line must not be crossed.

On a carriageway with two-way traffic, if the line is dashed, it may be crossed during an overtaking manoeuvre.

251.title_en: Dashed white line in the centre of the carriageway
251.description_en:
Divides the carriageway into two lanes; it may be crossed if all other traffic rules are respected.

It does not allow driving astride it.

On a two-way road with two lanes, it separates the directions of travel and allows:

- when wanting to overtake, to temporarily occupy the other lane of travel (sufficient visibility must still exist and it must be permitted on that stretch of road)

- making a U-turn, under safe conditions.

- a left turn (moving toward the centre of the carriageway)

It is not true that to make a U-turn it is necessary to not occupy the other lane.

On a one-way carriageway, the dashed white line serves to delimit the lanes (the left-hand lane is, as a rule, reserved for overtaking), therefore it allows:

- overtaking (also on bends and near or at humps)

- a left turn (moving to the left edge of the left-hand lane)

It is not true that you can always travel in parallel rows or make a U-turn (it is a one-way road).

It is not true that it can be replaced by a series of road studs or reflectors (these may supplement the solid line), or that it is found near a railway level crossing (generally, near a hazard such as a level crossing, there is a solid line).

252.title_en: Solid white line in the centre of the carriageway
252.description_en:
- divides the carriageway into two lanes:

- it may not be crossed

- it allows the overtaking manoeuvre without crossing it (if permitted by other rules)

- it does not allow driving astride it

- it does not allow making a U-turn

- on two-way roads it separates the directions of travel

- on two-way roads it may be found near a hazard, such as on the uphill stretch of a hump or near pedestrian or cycle crossings.

253.description_en:
It serves to separate the directions of travel on two-way roads.

For example, with four lanes (two per direction of travel): there will be a dashed line between each of the lanes in each direction of travel, and a double solid line in the centre to separate the two directions of travel.

- it may not be crossed

- it allows overtaking, if permitted, without crossing it

- it does not allow reversing the direction of travel

- it does not allow turning left

It is not true that it can be found at the edges of the road to mark the margins, or that it indicates the point where drivers must come to a halt because of a STOP sign.

254.title_en: Central solid line flanked on the left by a dashed line
254.description_en:
Found on two-way roads. The solid line on the vehicle's side indicates that it has not yet passed the hazard, and there is an obligation not to encroach on the other lane (that is, not to cross the two lines). For example, it can be found:

- before a bend - on the other direction of travel it is dashed because it is at the exit of the bend, so there is greater visibility

- on the uphill stretch of a hump - on the other direction of travel it is dashed because it is on the downhill stretch, so there is greater visibility

- before a junction

- before a railway level crossing

255.title_en: Central dashed line flanked on the left by a solid line
255.description_en:
Found on two-way roads. The dashed line on the vehicle's side indicates that it has passed the hazard and may, if necessary, encroach on the other lane (for example, to overtake). For example, it can be found:

- after a bend - on the other direction of travel it is solid because it is before the bend, so there is reduced visibility

- on the downhill stretch of a hump - on the other direction of travel it is solid because it is on the uphill stretch, so there is reduced visibility

- after a junction

- after a railway level crossing

256.title_en: Solid white lateral line separating the carriageway from the emergency lane
256.description_en:
The continuous white line separating the carriageway from the emergency lane (lane A) may be crossed only in case of necessity (vehicle breakdown, passenger illness), for a maximum of three hours.

Therefore, it cannot be occupied for overtaking manoeuvres or in heavy traffic.

The only vehicles that may use the emergency lane (lane A) are rescue vehicles on duty.

It is not true that motorcycles are permitted to travel on it.

259.description_en:
The dashed lateral lines:

- mark the edge of the main road at side-road junctions or at roads where right-of-way obligations apply

- also mark parking bays or parking areas, driveway access points, and acceleration or deceleration lanes.

260.description_en:
Guide lines at intersections (crossroads) are curved dashed white lines used to make a left turn correctly, avoiding entry into the wrong side of the road.

As a rule, they are found where the left turn is made by leaving the centre of the intersection on our right, so they must be kept on the vehicle's left when turning left.

Being made of dashed white lines, they may be crossed by vehicles (for example, to proceed straight ahead).

In the case of the figure:

- vehicle A may go in any direction

- vehicle B may turn left, but must give way to vehicle A

- vehicle C may go straight ahead

261.description_en:
Guide lines at intersections (crossroads) are curved dashed white lines used to make a left turn correctly, avoiding entry into the wrong side of the road.

As a rule, they are found where the left turn is made by leaving the centre of the intersection on our right, so they must be kept on the vehicle's left when turning left.

Being made of dashed white lines, they may be crossed by vehicles (for example, to proceed straight ahead).

262.description_en:
A traffic island is an area bounded by diagonal white stripes and indicates a stretch of road where vehicles are prohibited from entering and parking.

In the case of the figure:

- vehicle A must go straight ahead

- vehicle B must turn right

- vehicle C must turn right

263.description_en:
The solid transverse line indicates the point where drivers must stop when stop signals are present (red traffic light, traffic officer signaling HALT, STOP AND GIVE WAY sign).

It may be supplemented with the word STOP painted on the road surface.

It is not true that it indicates the point where you must stop at an unregulated intersection, or the point where you must always stop near a road intersection, or that giving way to vehicles coming from both the right and the left is mandatory (this only applies where there is a stop sign).

265.description_en:
In the absence of directional arrows, all three lanes allow you to go straight ahead. In addition:

- the left lane also allows you to turn left

- the right lane also allows you to turn right

- the center lane only allows you to go straight ahead

You may change lanes as long as the lines are still broken (dashed).

It is not true that the right lane is reserved for slow vehicles.

266.description_en:
The directional arrows shown in the figure are located within the (pre-selection) lanes, before an intersection.

They indicate to drivers the directions permitted at the intersection:

- lane A allows the driver only to turn left

- lane B allows the driver to go straight ahead and to turn left

- lane C allows turning right and going straight ahead

You may enter the chosen lane when the lines are still broken (dashed), while it is mandatory to follow the direction indicated by the arrow if the lane lines are solid.

They may be supplemented by markings on the road surface indicating the destinations reachable.

They may be combined arrows, for example straight-right for lanes intended for those who must go straight ahead or turn right.



It is not true that lanes A, B and C shown in the figure are two-way traffic lanes.

267.description_en:
The directional arrows shown in the figure are located within the (pre-selection) lanes, before an intersection.

They indicate to drivers the directions permitted at the intersection.

You may enter the chosen lane when the lines are still broken (dashed), while it is mandatory to follow the direction indicated by the arrow if the lane lines are solid.

They may be supplemented by markings on the road surface indicating the destinations reachable.

They may be combined arrows, for example straight-right for lanes intended for those who must go straight ahead or turn right.



It is not true that they are yellow on roads where parking is prohibited, or blue on motorways.

269.description_en: This marking indicates, both inside and outside built-up areas, a pedestrian crossing, where pedestrians have right-of-way over vehicles. It may be supplemented by the specific vertical sign for PEDESTRIAN CROSSING. On secondary rural roads it must be preceded by the DANGER – PEDESTRIAN CROSSING sign. It may also be oblique. It obliges drivers to stop and yield to pedestrians crossing the carriageway.

270.description_en:
This marking indicates, both inside and outside built-up areas, a pedestrian crossing, where pedestrians have right-of-way over vehicles.

It may be supplemented by the specific vertical sign for PEDESTRIAN CROSSING.

On secondary rural roads it must be preceded by the DANGER – PEDESTRIAN CROSSING sign.

It may also be oblique.

It obliges drivers to stop and yield to pedestrians crossing the carriageway.

A pedestrian crossing may be preceded on the right by a yellow zig-zag stripe, as in the figure, to improve its visibility.

272.title_en: Signage near a railway level crossing
272.description_en:
The signage shown in the figure warns drivers that they are close to a railway level crossing (with barriers, without barriers, or with half-barriers).

It indicates to drivers that they must pay attention to the possible approach of trains.

It is not permitted to move into the left-hand part of the carriageway (for example, to overtake).

273.description_en:
The signage in the figure indicates an area for the stop of buses, trolleybuses and articulated buses in scheduled public service. It helps buses carry out the manoeuvre of pulling in to the kerb and pulling away again.

It prohibits parking but not the brief stop of other vehicles, including in sections marked with a yellow zig-zag line (it is still possible to drive over it).

Where road markings are missing, parking is prohibited from 15 metres before to 15 metres after the bus stop sign.

It is not true that the area is also reserved for taxi parking, nor that it prohibits parking 20 metres before the yellow zig-zag line.

275.title_en: Regulatory markings on the road surface
275.description_en:
The following regulatory markings may be found on the road surface:

- STOP: completes the vertical sign requiring drivers to stop and give way

- P L with a painted St Andrew's Cross: indicates a railway level crossing (of any type)

- BUS: yellow, in areas reserved for the stop of scheduled public-service buses

- TAXI: yellow, indicating areas reserved for taxi parking

- the name of a place: completes the direction indication given by directional arrows

- a number: indicates the recommended speed

276.description_en:
These are placed along the vertical part of the kerb and indicate that parking (but not stopping) is prohibited for all vehicles on that side of the road.

It is not true that they allow buses to park, or that they warn pedestrians to watch for the step.

278.title_en: Parking area reserved for disabled persons
278.description_en:
The yellow demarcation lines in the figure identify a parking area reserved for disabled persons.

The yellow diagonal stripes must be kept clear to allow disabled persons to enter and exit the vehicle.

279.description_en: The device shown in the figure is a speed hump installed on the road.

300.description_en:
A traffic light is usually placed at an intersection to regulate the passage of vehicles (including bicycles) through the intersection itself.

The light sequence is green-yellow-red-green... Only one light is on at a time.

A steady green light allows you to enter the intersection with caution, then turn left (giving way to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians), turn right (giving way to pedestrians crossing the road), or go straight ahead.

You may enter the intersection only if you are certain you can clear it before the red light comes on.

When approaching a traffic light that has been green for a long time, proceed with caution, ready to stop if the yellow light comes on before you have entered the intersection.

A steady red light requires vehicles to stop before the transverse stop line. It may be larger than the other lights so that it is easily visible.

On vertically arranged traffic lights, the red light is at the top. On horizontally arranged traffic lights, it is on the left.

A steady yellow light:

- requires you to stop before the stop line, provided you can do so safely without creating a hazard

- allows you to cross the intersection if you have already entered it, but you must clear it as soon as possible (it is not true that it requires you to reverse if you have already passed the transverse stop line).

With a flashing yellow light (which indicates the traffic light is off or malfunctioning), you must enter the intersection with caution, giving way to vehicles coming from the right (unless otherwise signaled).

A flashing yellow light is also used as a general danger signal, inviting you to proceed with particular caution and reduce speed at dangerous points on the road.

Passing a vehicle traffic light is therefore permitted:

- when the green light is on

- when the steady yellow light comes on, but only if you cannot stop safely before the intersection

- when the flashing yellow light is on, or the traffic light is off or malfunctioning, but using maximum caution and reducing speed

301.description_en:
Lane traffic lights are placed at an intersection and apply to vehicles (all types, including bicycles) that must continue in the direction of the arrow.

A lit green arrow indicates the directions in which you may proceed. You may proceed only in the direction of the green arrow.

A lit red arrow indicates that you may not proceed in the indicated directions. It requires vehicles heading in the direction of the arrow to come to a halt.

A steady yellow arrow indicates that you must clear the intersection if you have already entered it, or come to a halt safely if you have not.

If the arrows are off, or a flashing yellow arrow is on, you must cross the intersection with particular caution.

It is not true that these are traffic lights for reversible lanes.

302.description_en:
A pedestrian traffic light regulates the passage of pedestrians at intersections.

It may be equipped with an audible signal for the visually impaired.

- With a red light on, pedestrians must stop before crossing.

- With a steady yellow light on, pedestrians who have already entered the crossing must clear it quickly.

- With a green light on, pedestrians may cross the road, and drivers must give way to pedestrians who are crossing. It is not true that pedestrians must give way to vehicles that are turning.

303.description_en:
A traffic light reserved for bicycles (velocipedes) is located at the exit of a cycle path to regulate crossing the road.

- With a green light on, only cyclists may cross the intersection.

- With a steady yellow light on, cyclists must clear the intersection quickly if they have already entered it.

- With a red light on, cyclists must stop.

It is not true that it applies to all two-wheeled vehicles.

304.title_en: Traffic lights for public transport vehicles
304.description_en:
A traffic light for public transport vehicles applies only to vehicles on scheduled passenger services (buses, trams, taxis), so it is not limited to vehicles running on rails.

These lights are placed at intersections and operate in coordination with the other traffic lights.

- Requires a halt when the white bar at the top is lit

- Allows vehicles to proceed when the white bar at the bottom is lit

- Allows vehicles to proceed right or left when a white bar slanted to the right or to the left is lit

- Indicates an advance stop warning when the yellow triangle in the centre is lit

305.description_en:
This light is placed on a two-way carriageway with at least three lanes (also at motorway toll booths, with red and green lights) to regulate use of the lanes by vehicles (all types of vehicles).

- Allows entry into the lane indicated by the green arrow

- Does not allow occupying the lane indicated by a red X light

- A flashing yellow light obliges the driver to move into the lane indicated by the arrow

It is not true that it also applies to pedestrians; it does apply to cyclists.

It is not true that a lane with a red light lit requires stopping and waiting for the go-ahead signal.

306.description_en:
Green wave traffic lights are synchronised lights installed along routes with multiple intersections.

They advise the driver to maintain the speed indicated by the lit symbol in order to find green at the subsequent traffic lights (taking advantage of the green wave).

Of the three lights of the traffic light, only one is lit at a time.

Attention: they do not require the driver to maintain the indicated speed; they only recommend it.

It is not true that they are placed on motorways, since there are no at-grade intersections there.

307.description_en:
The flashing yellow light, type B or C in the figure, is placed alongside the vehicle traffic light to remind vehicles turning right that they must:

- Give way to cyclists (type C)

- Give way to pedestrians (type B)

Type A, which appears when the traffic light is switched off or faulty, requires caution, reduced speed and giving way to vehicles coming from the right.

A flashing yellow light of type A may also be placed at dangerous points on the road as a general danger signal, inviting drivers to proceed with particular caution and moderate their speed.

308.description_en:
When in operation, these lights come on alternately and prohibit the passage of vehicles and pedestrians. They require drivers to come to a halt and not cross the transverse stop line.

They may be found at a railway level crossing with half-barriers or without barriers, at the access to a ferry boarding pier or a movable bridge, or when aircraft are landing or taking off (supplementing the LOW-FLYING AIRCRAFT danger sign).

As a rule, they are located on the right-hand side of the road and are integrated with an acoustic signalling device.

At level crossings, they are placed in the immediate vicinity of the tracks and come into operation shortly before the train arrives, before the half-barriers begin to lower, and remain lit until the train has fully passed. Therefore, when approaching a level crossing with red lights flashing alternately and the half-barrier still raised, drivers must prepare to stop.

It is not true that they are located near a police checkpoint along railway lines, serving as a signal for train drivers, 150 metres before a level crossing or on the first of the distance panels.

309.title_en: Road service personnel identify themselves by

310.description_en: The officer stands with both arms outstretched toward our direction, as shown in the figure. This is equivalent to a red traffic light, so you must come to a halt before the transverse stop line, and passing is prohibited (you may not turn left, turn right, or go straight ahead).

311.title_en: Traffic officer in AVANTI (GO AHEAD) position
311.description_en: The officer stands side-on with both arms outstretched, as shown in the figure. This is equivalent to a green traffic light: traffic flowing parallel to the officer's arms (coming from their right or left) is permitted to pass, though caution is still required. You may therefore go straight ahead; turn right (giving way to pedestrians crossing the intersecting road); or turn left (giving way to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians).

312.description_en:
The officer has one arm raised, as shown in the figure. This is equivalent to a steady yellow traffic light, so:

- you must stop before the intersection, if it is possible to do so without creating a hazard

- you must clear the intersection quickly, if you have already entered it

313.title_en: Traffic officer with arms extended horizontally at 90 degrees
313.description_en:
The officer stands with arms at right angles, as shown in the figure. This allows vehicles coming from the officer's left to proceed in all directions, meaning they may turn left, turn right, or go straight ahead.

Vehicles approaching from other directions (from the officer's right, from behind the officer, and from in front) are brought to a halt.

315.title_en: Documents to show on request of officers
315.description_en:
Drivers of motor vehicles or motorcycles must show the following documents upon request of law enforcement officers:
- driving licence
- vehicle registration document (carta di circolazione)
- insurance certificate
- portable warning triangle (mobile danger warning sign)

351.description_en:
Indicates that traffic on the road section where it is placed is one-way; in particular, once you have turned, the road is one-way.

Therefore, once you have turned in the direction of the arrow, it is not possible to travel in the opposite direction (for example, U-turns are prohibited).

It is not true that this sign prohibits continuing straight ahead.

352.description_en:
Indicates that traffic on the road section where it is placed is one-way; in particular, it marks the start of a one-way street.

Therefore, after this sign it is not possible to travel in the opposite direction (for example, U-turns are prohibited).

It is not true that this sign requires drivers to continue straight ahead.

354.description_en:
Gives advance notice of an urban junction (white background), showing the names of the places that can be reached.

In this case, it indicates turning right to reach the railway station and the city centre; it indicates continuing straight ahead for Sora and Naples.

355.description_en:
Gives advance notice of an urban junction (white background), showing the names of the places that can be reached.

In this case, it indicates turning right to reach the city centre; it indicates continuing straight ahead for Milan.

356.title_en: Advance warning of closely spaced urban intersections
356.description_en:
Indicates two successive closely spaced urban intersections (white background).

At the first intersection, turning left is prohibited (due to the 'NO ENTRY' sign) and you turn right for Via Gemona.

At the second intersection (further ahead), turn right for the city centre and for Trieste (Grado and Cividale), or turn left for the hospital or for Austria (Tarvisio and Tolmezzo).

357.title_en: Advance warning of urban intersection with roundabout
357.description_en:
This is an advance warning sign for an urban intersection controlled by a roundabout. It shows a diagram of the roundabout and lists the names of the places that can be reached.

Take the first road on the right for Forlì, the second for the ring road (tangenziale), and the third for the city centre.

358.title_en: Advance warning of urban intersection with a vehicle category restriction
358.description_en:
This is an advance warning sign for an urban intersection with a traffic restriction. It warns of a traffic restriction on the road towards Pescara, specifically:

- Trucks with a mass over 3.5 t (not all of them) are prohibited from continuing straight ahead towards the centre of Avezzano.

- Buses and cars are allowed to continue straight ahead.

- Warns to turn left at the urban intersection to reach the Rome-L'Aquila motorway.

359.title_en: Advance warning of rural intersection with a railway level crossing on one branch
359.description_en:
Warns of an intersection on a rural road (blue background).

Indicates the presence of a railway level crossing on the right-hand branch of the intersection (not a railway station), and therefore warns drivers turning right of possible train crossings. Indicates to turn right for S. Giovanni, to turn left for a tourist destination (brown sign), and to continue straight ahead to reach Porto Torres.

360.description_en:
This is an advance warning sign for a motorway junction (not an intersection, as there are no intersections on motorways) (green background), which allows drivers to choose their direction in advance.

Indicates that you should continue straight ahead to reach Bologna, and turn left for Linate Airport.

361.description_en:
It is an advance warning and temporary roadworks sign. It is placed near a junction that comes before a road works site.

It prohibits all vehicles from continuing straight ahead and indicates the alternative route (Novara can still be reached).

When combined with the 'ESTESA' supplementary panel, it indicates that the diversion is 2 km long (it does not indicate the distance from the diversion itself).

363.description_en:
It indicates an urban preselection and is placed in place of the junction advance warning sign. On urban roads (white background) with multiple lanes, it allows drivers to move into the preselection lanes, specifically:

- it indicates to drivers heading to the tourist resort to move into the middle lane
- it indicates to drivers heading to Terni to move into the left lane
- it indicates to drivers heading to the city centre to occupy the right lane

364.description_en:
It is a preselection sign on an extra-urban road (blue background) divided into two lanes.

It gives advance warning of a preselection zone with two destinations:

- it indicates to the driver heading to Bari to move into the left lane

- it indicates to the driver heading to Pescara to move into the right lane

365.description_en:
It is an information sign placed along a motorway (green background):

- the left side shows the progressive distance from the starting point of the motorway (in this case we are at kilometre 54 from the start of the motorway)

- the right side shows the distance to the exit for the indicated locality (in this case there are 4 kilometres left from the exit toll booth for Piacenza)

366.description_en:
Placed on motorways or main extra-urban roads (as in this case), it indicates the distance (the one at the bottom) between the sign and the next exit junction. It then lists the localities reachable by leaving at that junction (in the centre).

In this example, it is on an extra-urban road (as shown by the blue background) and indicates that the junction for Frosinone is 500 m away and that the localities reachable are those listed in the centre on a blue background.

Tourist localities are indicated on a brown background.

It is not correct to read that Frosinone itself is 500 metres away (in fact, at 500 metres there is the exit from the road we are travelling on, which then allows us to reach Frosinone).

367.description_en:
Indicates the start of a built-up area and therefore identifies the locality reached (in this case Taranto).

It is placed at the start of the built-up area, on all the access roads to the indicated locality.

If crossed out by a red stripe, it indicates the end of the built-up area.

It is not true that it indicates the direction to follow to reach Taranto.

368.description_en:
Indicates the end of the built-up area and therefore also the end of the 50 km/h maximum speed limit and of the prohibition on sounding the horn.

The blue panel shows the next localities (built-up areas) reachable, listed in order of distance, and for each locality its distance in kilometres.

It is not true that it is located on main extra-urban roads, since, as stated, it is placed just at the exit of a built-up area, and therefore on secondary extra-urban roads.

369.description_en:
Indicates, on a motorway, the distance (number on the right) to the localities reachable along the route, listed in the order they are reached.

If blue, it is located on extra-urban roads.

It is not true that it indicates that, upon exiting at the first motorway toll booth, all the indicated localities can be reached.

370.description_en:
Identifies the type of road being travelled: in this case, municipal road no. 19 (it has a white background).

It may be found as a complement to direction signs.

It is not true that it indicates a distance or a time, or that it is located at the start of a country road.

371.description_en:
The sign identifies the type of road being travelled: in this case state road no. 2 (an extra-urban road, as shown by its blue background).

It may be found within direction signs or junction signs.

It is not true that it indicates a distance or the length of a stretch of road.

372.description_en:
Identifies the type of road being travelled: in this case motorway no. 25 (it has a green background).

It can be found within a motorway junction advance warning sign.

When combined with an arrow, it indicates the direction to a motorway toll booth.

It is not true that it indicates a distance.

373.description_en:
Identifies the type of road being travelled: in this case international route no. 55. It is placed on roads of international importance and shows their international classification number.

It can be found within a road fork advance warning sign.

It is not true that it indicates a motorway, a distance, or a maximum speed.

374.title_en: State border between European Community countries
374.description_en:
Indicates the border between Italy and a Member State of the European Economic Community.

It does not require stopping at the state border. It is not true that it warns of a police roadblock near the state border.

375.title_en: Advance warning of state border between European Community countries
375.description_en:
Gives advance warning of a state border with a country that is part of the European Union, on roads leading to that border. It also indicates the distance (at the bottom).

It does not require stopping for customs checks at the state border.

It is not true that it is located near a roadblock, or that it is a sign that must be placed on a vehicle.

376.description_en:
Indicates the start of a pedestrian area. The supplementary panel contains particular time restrictions or exceptions (categories authorised to travel).

In this case, vehicles carrying disabled persons, police, ambulances and firefighters (when on urgent emergency duty), and vehicles for loading and unloading goods are permitted.

The same sign crossed by a red transverse stripe indicates the end of the pedestrian area.

It is incorrect to say that the sign indicates a mandatory path for pedestrians or routes for tourist excursions.

377.description_en:
Indicates the start of a restricted traffic zone, i.e. an area where access and circulation of vehicles may be limited in time and/or to particular categories of vehicles.

The supplementary panel indicates the time restrictions or exceptions (categories of vehicles authorised to circulate).

In this case, passage is permitted only to vehicles carrying disabled persons, Police, ambulances and Fire Brigade vehicles (when on urgent emergency duty), and vehicles for loading and unloading goods (only at specific times).

378.title_en: Road open (mountain pass open with snow chains obligation)
378.description_en:
Placed on mountain roads, it signals the road conditions (in this case for the Stelvio Pass).

Indicates that the road is open (so it is possible to reach the Stelvio Pass), but only for vehicles equipped with snow chains or winter tyres (it makes their use mandatory).

It does not merely recommend fitting chains; it requires them (if winter tyres are not fitted).

379.description_en:
Placed on mountain roads, it signals the road conditions (in this case for the Stelvio Pass).

Indicates that the road is closed (so it is not possible to reach the Stelvio Pass), while it is possible to get as far as Trafoi (a locality located before the Stelvio).

The sign advises proceeding with particular caution and attention and recommends (but does not require) the use of snow chains or winter tyres.

380.description_en:
Indicates the entrance to a main extra-urban road (i.e. a road with separate carriageways). If crossed by a red transverse stripe, it indicates the end of the road.

If green, it indicates the start of a motorway.

May appear in a reduced (small) format on advance or pre-selection signs.

It does not indicate the presence of an overpass or require vehicles to travel in parallel lanes.

Not to be confused with the 'U-TURN' sign.

381.description_en:
Placed on a road with separate carriageways, it indicates the presence of a structure (overpass or underpass) where a U-turn (i.e. to turn back) may be made.

If green, it is located on a motorway.

Not to be confused with the 'START OF MAIN EXTRA-URBAN ROAD' sign.

382.description_en:
Posted near the Italian border, visible to drivers coming from the foreign state, it indicates the general maximum speed limits that apply in Italy. From top to bottom:

- 50 km/h on urban roads

- 90 km/h on secondary rural roads

- 110 km/h on main rural roads (for example: expressways, fast roads)

- 130 km/h on motorways

383.description_en:
This is a location sign placed at (at the entrance to) an emergency room (pronto soccorso), indicating the direction to take in order to enter.

It does not indicate a pharmacy.

384.description_en:
This is a location sign placed at a hospital, indicating its entrance or the direction to follow to reach it.

Therefore, it reminds drivers not to make disturbing noises in its vicinity.

385.description_en:
This is a location sign indicating the name of the river near the bridge that crosses it.

In this case, it is located near a bridge crossing the Arno river.

It does not indicate a danger of storm surges or flooding.

386.title_en: Advance tourist and hotel information notice
386.description_en:
Gives advance notice of a tourist and hotel information office, where information about tourist accommodations and services (hotels, motels) can be requested.

The distance is shown below.

387.description_en: Indicates the proximity of an area designated for parking caravans and motorhomes, and for camping.

388.description_en: Indicates an equipped area with facilities that allow vehicles with sanitary services to discharge organic waste and grey and black water.

389.description_en:
Located (directly) at the markings of a pedestrian crossing.

Obliges drivers to stop when pedestrians are crossing at pedestrian crossings.

Outside built-up areas, it is found after the warning sign PEDESTRIAN CROSSING.

It is not true that, if green, it may be placed on a motorway (where there are no pedestrian crossings).

390.description_en:
Located (directly) at the markings of a cycle crossing.

Advises caution and indicates that right-of-way must be given to cyclists crossing on the markings.

It is not true that it indicates a cycle path.

391.description_en:
If placed on the edge of the sidewalk, indicates a school bus stop.

If placed on the outside of a bus, signals that it is carrying schoolchildren.

Warns drivers to pay attention to children who, after getting off the school bus, may suddenly cross the road

392.description_en:
Indicates a stop for extra-urban public transport buses and therefore the place where they can be waited for.

It may be combined with a panel showing the departure times.

It does not indicate a lane reserved for buses or a parking area for buses and trolleybuses.

393.description_en:
Indicates a park-and-ride facility with bus lines, and therefore the possibility of parking the car and taking the bus.

It is located near a bus stop.

The sign shown indicates that after parking the car, it is possible to take bus no. 8 or no. 45.

It does not indicate a bus bay.

394.description_en: Indicates the presence of a call device to be used in case of a request for roadside assistance and help, which operates 24 hours a day.

395.description_en:
This is an indication sign placed at the entrance of a dead-end street for vehicles; it also applies to motorcycles.

It does not apply to pedestrians.

396.description_en: This is an indication sign that signals the junction (crossroads) with a street on the right that is a dead end for vehicles (including motorcycles). It nevertheless allows turning right or proceeding straight ahead.

397.description_en:
Indicates the speed that is recommended (WARNING: this is not an obligation) not to exceed in optimal traffic conditions.

It may be combined with a panel indicating the length of the road section where it is recommended not to exceed the indicated speed.

So in this case, it still allows, for example, travelling at 70 km/h.

If crossed out by a red stripe, it indicates the end of its validity.

398.description_en:
This is an information sign. It indicates the start of a road reserved for all motor vehicles (cars, motorcycles, quadricycles, articulated lorries, etc.), while prohibiting traffic from non-motor vehicles (bicycles, carts, etc.).

It therefore replaces the prohibition signs relating to non-motor vehicles.

If crossed out by a red stripe, it indicates the end of its validity.

399.description_en:
Indicates the start of a motorway tunnel and therefore reminds drivers not to park and not to stop in the tunnel, unless otherwise signposted, or in any case to switch off the engine in the event of a prolonged halt in the tunnel.

It reminds drivers to hold the steering wheel firmly to cope with any gusts of wind at the tunnel exit.

It does NOT indicate an unlit tunnel.

400.description_en:
Can be found at the start of a bridge, a viaduct or an overpass.

It may be supplemented by a panel indicating its length.

It reminds drivers to hold the steering wheel firmly to cope with any crosswinds.

It does NOT prohibit overtaking between motor vehicles.

401.description_en:
Indicates that at the next intersection it is not possible to turn left directly, and therefore shows the route to take in order to reach the road on the left indirectly.

It still allows drivers to continue straight ahead or turn right, and it only concerns drivers who intend to turn left.

It does NOT fail to apply to bicycles and mopeds.

402.description_en:
It is located on an extra-urban road and indicates a lay-by beside the carriageway for making a brief stop.

It may be combined with a supplementary panel showing the distance between the sign and the lay-by.

It is not true that parking is allowed only for 3 hours.

403.description_en:
It is an information sign installed on urban roads (white background) and indicates how the lanes must be used, in particular:

- the right-hand lane is reserved for buses of urban public transport services

- the left-hand lanes are intended for the normal traffic of all vehicles

It does not indicate that buses may overtake on the right.

404.description_en:
It is an information sign installed on extra-urban roads (blue background) and indicates how the lanes of a carriageway must be used.

In particular, it indicates that the left-hand lane is prohibited to lorries exceeding a maximum laden mass of 3.5 tonnes, so all other vehicles may travel on both lanes.

It is not true that it is found only on two-way roads.

405.description_en:
It is an information sign installed on motorways (green background) and indicates the minimum speeds (mandatory, not recommended) to be maintained in the indicated lanes.

So the first lane on the right may be used with no minimum speed limit, the middle lane may not be used below 60 km/h, and the left-hand lane may not be used below 90 km/h.

It is not true that it allows driving at 160 km/h in all three lanes, as the general speed limit on motorways is 130 km/h.

406.title_en: Change in number of available lanes (increase)
406.description_en:
It is an information sign placed on extra-urban roads (blue colour) and indicates a change in the number of available lanes (in this case from one to two).

It may be combined with a supplementary panel showing the distance from the point where the lane increase occurs.

It is not true that it indicates that overtaking on the right is permitted.

407.description_en:
This is an information sign placed on motorways (green background). It indicates a reduction in the number of available lanes (in this case from three to two).

It therefore advises drivers to slow down because the carriageway is narrowing.

It may be combined with a supplementary panel showing the distance to the lane narrowing.

408.description_en:
This is an information sign (so it is not a mandatory requirement), usually placed at the entrance to built-up areas. It recommends that the vehicles shown on the panel follow the indicated direction in order to avoid driving through the built-up area.

In this case, it recommends that road trains and articulated lorries (goods vehicles with a gross mass over 3.5 t) follow the road to the right.

409.title_en: Mandatory direction for road trains and articulated lorries
409.description_en:
This is a mandatory sign placed near a roadworks site for the duration of the road works.

It indicates a mandatory direction (not a recommended or optional one) for certain categories of vehicles (road trains and articulated lorries).

The sign does not apply to all other types of vehicles.

410.description_en: This sign is placed along an extra-urban road and indicates that a vehicle repair workshop is located nearby.

411.description_en: This sign is placed along an extra-urban road and indicates that a public telephone is located nearby.

412.description_en:
It is placed along an extra-urban road and indicates a fuel station nearby.

If the background is green, it indicates a fuel station on a motorway.

It is not true that it indicates a fuel station reserved only for vehicles powered by LPG.

413.description_en:
It is placed along an extra-urban road and indicates the proximity of a major railway station offering the possibility of transporting cars accompanying the traveller.

It is located near the access point for cars to be loaded onto trains.

It is not true that it indicates the possibility of remaining in the car during its transport by train, or an area reserved for parking motorhomes.

414.description_en:
It indicates a parking area for the exclusive use of taxis in service, that is, an area marked by yellow stripes with the word TAXI.

It is not true that the sign is equipped with its own light.

415.description_en: The sign shown displays certain details (locality, street, telephone numbers) of the nearest State Road Police command.

451.description_en:
In a series of hairpin bends, it indicates their progressive number (not the total number, which may instead be shown on the supplementary panel 'TORNANTE' in figure 143 - see the chapter on supplementary panels).

It therefore indicates the proximity of a sharp and dangerous bend (hairpin bend).

It is not true that it indicates how many kilometres away the next hairpin bend is.

452.title_en: Normal edge delineators on two-way roads
452.description_en:
These are complementary signs placed at the edges of the carriageway on two-way roads (they are not used on one-way roads).

They indicate the edges of the road from a distance, and therefore the road's alignment. They are especially useful in conditions of poor visibility (not only at night).

It is not true that they are placed 100 metres apart from each other.

453.title_en: Normal edge delineators on one-way roads
453.description_en:
These are complementary signs placed at the edges of the carriageway on one-way roads.

They indicate the edges of the road from a distance, and therefore the road's alignment. They are especially useful in conditions of poor visibility (not only at night).

They may be replaced by reflective elements where walls or railings are present at the edges of the carriageway.

454.description_en:
These are complementary signs used in one-way tunnels to mark the edge of the carriageway. They are mandatory in tunnels with bends.

They may also be found where there are narrowings or permanent diversions of the carriageway.

It is not true that they have their own light source.

455.description_en: This complementary sign is placed at the sides of the carriageway on mountain roads. It is used to make the edges of the carriageway more clearly visible on a snow-covered road.

456.title_en: Delineator for bend, narrowing or hairpin bend
456.description_en:
Used on both urban and extra-urban roads (main and secondary). It indicates the alignment of sharp, dangerous bends where visibility is limited.

It warns the driver to take care when negotiating a bend. The arrows point in the direction of the bend.

When located near a roadworks site, it is white and red; in this case it indicates a temporary diversion with a bend.

It may be preceded by the warning sign 'CURVA PERICOLOSA A SINISTRA' (dangerous bend to the left).

457.description_en:
This supplementary sign is installed in a series of elements to highlight the outer edge of a dangerous bend (improving its visibility).

It is useful for increasing the visibility of the road's layout at a distance.

If it is white and red, it indicates a temporary diversion in the presence of roadworks.

It is not true that it is placed 150 metres before a bend, or that it is only placed if the bend is on a one-way road.

458.description_en:
This sign is placed across the road you are travelling on, at T-junctions, i.e. junctions where it is not possible to continue straight ahead.

The arrows point in the only possible directions, so it indicates the need to turn right or left.

To indicate temporary diversions, it is white and red.

459.description_en:
This is a panel used together with the COMPULSORY PASSAGE or PERMITTED PASSAGE sign, placed within the carriageway in the presence of an obstacle (refuge island, traffic island, central median).

It is retroreflective, for better visibility at night.

It is not true that it has its own light source.

461.description_en:
This sign gives advance warning of works in progress and therefore of the possible presence of workers on or near the carriageway, or of temporary deposits of materials or machinery on the road.

When this sign is present, it is advisable to reduce speed and, if necessary, stop, proceeding with caution.

This sign may be supplemented by the 'ESTESA' panel, which indicates the length of the roadworks.

462.description_en:
Gives advance warning of a traffic light installation in the presence of roadworks (for example, placed before a temporary narrowing of the carriageway due to works in progress). It may be found on both urban and rural roads.

The disc in the centre may show a flashing yellow light.

When this sign is present, it is advisable to reduce speed and, if necessary, stop at the red light.

463.description_en:
Marks an area occupied by a roadworks site and is placed along its edges.
It may also be used at railway level crossings when the barriers are out of order.
It may be supplemented by a fixed red light lantern in case of poor visibility.

464.description_en:
Used to mark short-duration roadworks, temporary diversions, areas affected by accidents, and the temporary separation of traffic directions.

It is not true that it can be used for roadworks lasting more than 10 days (as stated, it is used for short-duration works).

465.description_en:
This sign indicates the recommended (not mandatory) direction for lorries with a maximum laden mass exceeding 3.5 t.

It is generally found near roadworks sites, is placed at the exact point of the diversion, and may be preceded by an 'ADVANCE DIVERSION NOTICE' sign.

It is not true that it indicates a parking area for lorries.

467.title_en: Advance diversion warning for vehicles over 7 t
467.description_en:
It is part of the temporary signs for roadworks. It is placed near an intersection preceding a roadworks site.

It prohibits all vehicles with a maximum laden mass over 7 t from continuing straight ahead and indicates the alternative route (Lucca can still be reached).

All other vehicles may continue straight ahead.

468.description_en:
It is a temporary advance warning sign for roadworks. It is placed near an intersection preceding a roadworks site.

It prohibits all vehicles from continuing straight ahead and indicates the alternative route (Novara can still be reached).

When combined with the 'ESTESA' supplementary panel, it indicates that the diversion is 2 km long (it does not indicate the distance to the diversion).

469.description_en:
Indicates a temporary narrowing of the carriageway for ongoing roadworks, i.e. a reduction from two driving lanes to one (closure of the right-hand lane).

It is placed in the vicinity of a road construction site. It may be supplemented by a panel showing the distance to the point where the lane closes.

It does NOT require giving right-of-way to vehicles coming from the right.

470.description_en:
Placed where roadworks are in progress, it indicates which lanes different categories of vehicles may occupy. In this case, it indicates that lorries with a maximum authorised mass exceeding 3.5 tonnes may only use the right-hand lane.

It does NOT require lorries to drive in parallel lines, nor does it mean that lorries may only overtake on the right.

471.description_en:
It may be mounted on a vehicle to give advance warning of a mobile roadworks site with a narrowing on the left, and to indicate the lanes available for traffic.

It may be supplemented with flashing yellow lights. It is accompanied by the supplementary panel 'DISTANZA' (DISTANCE), which indicates the distance to the roadworks (500 m).

472.title_en: Panel fitted on road maintenance vehicles
472.description_en:
It may be fitted to road maintenance vehicles that are parked or moving slowly on the carriageway. It indicates the side from which the vehicle carrying it must be overtaken.

It warns drivers to reduce speed due to the possible presence of the above-mentioned vehicles.

500.description_en: These are special vertical road signs which, when placed below a sign, complete it with additional information.

501.description_en: Indicates the distance (in metres or kilometres) between the sign below which it is placed and the point where the danger, the requirement (prohibition, obligation or right-of-way) or the indication begins.

502.description_en: Indicates the length (in metres or kilometres) of the stretch of danger or of the requirement (prohibition or obligation).

503.description_en: Indicates, both on public holidays and on working days (feriali), the hours during which the requirement imposed by the sign below which the panel is placed is in force.

504.description_en:
Indicates that the requirement imposed by the sign below which the panel is placed applies on public holidays and during the hours shown.

A public holiday does not only mean Sunday.

505.description_en: Indicates that the requirement imposed by the sign below which the panel is placed applies on working days (feriali) and during the hours shown.

506.description_en: Indicates that the mandatory or prohibition sign to which it is attached applies only to the vehicles shown.

507.description_en: Indicates that the mandatory or prohibition sign to which it is attached applies to all vehicles except those shown.

508.description_en: Indicates the starting point of the danger, the requirement (prohibition, obligation or right-of-way) or the instruction imposed by the sign to which it is attached.

509.description_en: Indicates that the danger, the requirement (prohibition, obligation or right-of-way) or the instruction imposed by the sign to which it is attached continues to apply both before and after the sign itself.

510.description_en: Indicates the end point of the danger, the requirement (prohibition, obligation or right-of-way) or the instruction imposed by the sign to which it is attached.

511.description_en: Positioned overhead on the carriageway together with a sign, it specifies which lane the sign refers to. For example, if placed with a sign indicating a place name, it shows the lane to take to reach that place. It indicates that the sign it is paired with applies only to the lane shown.

512.description_en:
This panel is applied to the 'ALTRI PERICOLI' (OTHER DANGERS) or 'LAVORI IN CORSO' (ROADWORKS) sign and indicates possible work to repaint road markings.
It may therefore indicate a temporary absence of road markings and the presence of temporary roadworks for repainting the road markings.

513.description_en:
This panel is placed below the 'ALTRI PERICOLI' (OTHER DANGERS) sign and indicates the presence of an accident and therefore crashed vehicles on the carriageway.

It is advisable to reduce speed and, where possible, choose an alternative route.

514.description_en:
This panel is applied to the 'ALTRI PERICOLI' (OTHER DANGERS) sign and indicates the presence of a railway track crossing the road.

It calls for reduced speed and particular attention.

It may be found where trains pass infrequently, such as near port sidings, freight yards or industrial plants.

It does not mean there is a railway level crossing.

515.description_en:
This panel is applied to the 'ALTRI PERICOLI' (OTHER DANGERS) sign and indicates the presence of snowploughs working on the road (typically placed on snow-covered roads).

It calls for reduced speed and for keeping a distance of at least 20 metres from snowploughs in operation.

It does not mean that snow chains must be fitted, nor that the road can only be used after the snowplough has passed.

516.description_en:
Indicates the presence of roadworks where earth-moving machinery (excavators, bulldozers, etc.) may be operating on the road.

Invites drivers to reduce speed and pay particular attention.

517.description_en:
Indicates that the stretch of road on which it is placed may be subject to flooding due to heavy rain or storm surges.

It may also be placed below the 'Cunetta' (dip/gutter) sign.

518.description_en:
Indicates the possibility of encountering heavy traffic, with vehicles forming queues.

Invites drivers to proceed with caution, so as not to rear-end vehicles stopped due to traffic congestion. Where possible, it advises choosing an alternative route to avoid the queue.

It may be found, for example, at motorway entrances.

It is not true that it requires vehicles to travel at walking pace.

519.description_en:
Indicates the possibility of encountering icy stretches of road when temperatures are low, or on roads already covered in snow.

When placed below the 'STRADA SDRUCCIOLEVOLE' (slippery road) sign, it indicates a stretch of road that is slippery due to ice forming when temperatures drop.

Invites drivers to reduce speed and pay particular attention.

It does not mean that it indicates an area where it snows often.

520.description_en:
Indicates a stretch of road that is dangerous in rain because it is slippery due to mud or debris.

In rainy conditions, invites drivers to reduce speed and increase the safety distance.

It does not mean that it indicates an area where it rains often.

521.description_en:
Indicates a stretch of uphill road where trucks may be travelling at low speed because the steep climb forces them to slow down.

Indicates that you should drive at a cautious speed to avoid accidents with trucks that may be ahead of you.

It is not true that it signals the possibility of being towed.

522.description_en:
Placed below the 'NO PARKING' sign, it indicates that a vehicle left parked may be taken to a municipal impound lot by a tow truck, or immobilised with a wheel clamp (ganascia) and locking bar.

Vehicles used by persons with disabilities that display the appropriate permit cannot be removed or immobilised.

It is not true that the vehicle is removed or immobilised after three hours.

523.description_en:
Indicates the proximity of one or more sharp bends (hairpin bends), which are particularly dangerous because drivers cannot see far ahead.

It can be found below the CURVE or DOUBLE CURVE sign.

Do not confuse it with the supplementary 'HAIRPIN BEND NUMBER' sign (figure 144), which shows the sequential number of the hairpin bend. The latter is found in the chapter on supplementary signs.

524.description_en:
Placed below the 'NO PARKING' sign, it indicates the day and time slots when the road is mechanically cleaned. The parking ban applies only on the days and hours shown.

It is not true that the panel indicates a parking ban for street-cleaning vehicles.

525.description_en:
Placed below right-of-way signs. Near an intersection (crossroads), they show the layout of the main road (the wider line), distinguishing it from the secondary roads.

They cannot be placed on motorways because motorways have no at-grade intersections.

It is not true that they indicate dangerous bends, underpasses, dead-end roads, or that the crossing roads are temporarily closed.

550.description_en:
At railway level crossings, use the utmost caution and reduce speed to avoid dangerous situations that could result in collision with the crossing barriers or damage to the equipment. Crossing a level crossing without complying with all applicable rules (for example, crossing with a risky maneuver to save time) can endanger many people, such as passengers on a passing train, as well as the driver.



If, at a level crossing, you are still on the tracks with your vehicle when the barriers begin to close, stay calm and clear the railway track by any means necessary, even if it means breaking through the barriers. If your vehicle breaks down, act as quickly as possible to remove it, for example by having other road users tow it or help you push it off the railway track. In any case, make every effort to warn approaching trains of the danger.

If the vehicle cannot be moved, immediately have all passengers on board get out and notify the railway station so that train drivers are informed of the danger in good time.

It is not true that you must empty the fuel tank, abandon any trailer, or avoid moving the vehicle if there are injured people (in the case of a rear-end collision on the tracks).

551.description_en:
If you drive a long downhill stretch in neutral with the engine off, even if you think you are saving fuel, the risk of accidents increases, because the braking distance dangerously lengthens, it becomes difficult to steer if the vehicle has power steering, it becomes difficult to brake if the vehicle has power brakes, and it becomes difficult to turn the steering wheel quickly to avoid an obstacle.

It is not true that this causes an electrical overload, a fault in the differential, or that you should remove the ignition key.

552.description_en:
In a built-up area, if you see a ball rolling onto the roadway, do not swerve sharply or try to avoid it if this means entering the opposite lane.

You must slow down progressively (to avoid being rear-ended by the vehicle behind you) so that you can stop if necessary, also anticipating that a child may run out into the road. It is not true that you must activate the hazard warning lights.

553.title_en: Passing very close to a parked car
553.description_en:
Passing very close to a parked car (even at low speed) can be dangerous:

- if there are still people inside, because a door may be opened carelessly

- it may block the view of a person in a wheelchair or a pedestrian pushing a baby stroller who is about to cross the road

554.description_en:
Speed must be adjusted so that it does not obstruct traffic or cause disorder, and above all so that it does not endanger the safety of people and property (not only of those being transported), and in any case always stays within the maximum permitted limits.

Always maintain an appropriate speed so that you can keep control of the vehicle and bring it to a stop within your field of vision and in safe conditions in the event of unexpected situations.

Speed must be appropriate:
- to your psychophysical condition
- in relation to the characteristics and condition of the vehicle
- in relation to the vehicle's load
- in relation to weather conditions
- in relation to the characteristics and conditions of the road, as well as its state of maintenance and cleanliness (presence of potholes, uneven surfaces, wet leaves)
- in relation to traffic conditions

It is not true that speed must be adjusted based on the time available, the speed of following vehicles (you must instead consider those ahead), the engine's fuel supply, the type of gearbox, driving skill, the tyre brand, or the distance to the destination.

It is necessary/mandatory to adjust (reduce, moderate) speed:
- on stretches of road with limited visibility, for example near curves, crests, or in fog or mist
- near an intersection or when crossing with other vehicles is difficult
- in strong crosswinds
- when the road is covered with water, snow, ice, leaves, or mud
- in case of glare from the sun
- at night
- on steep downhill stretches
- in congested passages and narrow sections
- when driving through built-up areas and on stretches of road lined with buildings
- near schools and places frequented by children
- when there are no sidewalks and pedestrians occupy the roadway
- when you encounter the stopped vehicle sign (portable warning triangle) on the road
- where roadworks are in progress
- in mixed traffic (presence of slow and fast vehicles, or of animals and pedestrians occupying the road)

It is not true that it is necessary to reduce speed on one-way roads, two-way roads, outside built-up areas, on provincial roads, on uphill roads, in the presence of any road sign, near speed cameras, only when traffic police officers are present, or when being followed by a scheduled bus.

You must reduce speed and, if necessary, stop:
- when crossing with other vehicles is difficult
- near pedestrian crossings
- when pedestrians on the route are slow to move aside or show signs of uncertainty
- when animals on the road show signs of fright
- when you are dazzled
- at intersections, to let vehicles that have right-of-way pass. If you cross an intersection at high speed while having right-of-way, in the event of an accident, contributory fault cannot be ruled out.

When traveling in parallel lanes (for example along channelized lanes, or when traffic is channelized), it is possible that vehicles in the right-hand lane travel at a higher speed than those in the left-hand lane.

556.description_en:
In Italy the following maximum limits apply (speed limits are not identical in all European countries).



The general limits valid for motorcycles, cars, cars towing a trailer, and vehicles up to 3.5 t are:

- 50 km/h - built-up areas (urban roads)

- 90 km/h - secondary extra-urban roads

- 110 km/h - main extra-urban roads

- 130 km/h - motorways



The following additional maximum limits apply to certain categories of vehicles:

- 40 km/h - agricultural machinery and work machinery with tyres

- 45 km/h - mopeds

- 80 km/h - motor quadricycles

- 80 km/h - articulated lorries; cars towing trailers (even light ones) or caravans on motorways

- 70 km/h - articulated lorries; cars towing trailers (even light ones) or caravans on extra-urban roads (main and secondary)



On urban roads with particular characteristics, where the appropriate sign is present, the maximum limit may be 70 km/h.



On main extra-urban roads, in case of precipitation (rain, snow), the maximum speed may not exceed 90 km/h.



On motorways, in case of precipitation (rain, snow), the maximum speed may not exceed 110 km/h.

On motorways with three lanes in each direction (plus the emergency lane), the road owners may raise the speed limit up to 150 km/h, provided that particular road characteristics and conditions exist.



On motorways and main extra-urban roads, in case of dense fog with visibility under 100 m, temporary maximum speed limits not exceeding 50 km/h may be imposed.



Newly qualified drivers (those who obtained their licence less than 3 years ago) may not exceed 100 km/h on motorways and 90 km/h on main extra-urban roads.

600.description_en:
Reaction time is the time that elapses from the moment a dangerous situation is perceived until braking begins. Reaction time is usually roughly one second. Therefore, the distance travelled during reaction time is the distance covered from the moment a dangerous situation is perceived until the start of braking. It depends on the speed at which one is travelling. The distance travelled during reaction time (e.g. one second) can be calculated:

- by multiplying the speed by 1000 (metres in a kilometre) and dividing by 3600 (seconds in an hour), which is equivalent to multiplying by 10 and dividing by 36.
- approximately, by dividing the speed by 10 and multiplying by 3

So, for example, in 1 second at a speed of 50 km/h you travel:

- 50x10/36 = 13.889 m using the first method
- 50/10x3 = 15 m using the second (approximate) method

601.description_en:
This is the distance travelled from the start of braking until the vehicle comes to a stop. It depends on speed: the higher the speed, the greater it becomes.

In particular, the relationship is such that:

- if speed doubles, the distance increases 4 times

- if speed triples, the distance increases 9 times

- if speed quadruples, the distance increases 16 times

and so on (that is, if speed increases n times, the distance increases n squared times)



Besides speed, braking distance depends on:

- the grip between tyre and asphalt; it increases if grip is low (e.g. on snow, mud, oil, wet road) or if the wheels lock, or if worn tyres are used

- the gradient of the road; in particular it increases on a downhill and decreases on an uphill

It is not true that it depends on the driver's reflexes (these only influence reaction time).

602.description_en:
The total stopping distance is equal to the distance travelled during reaction time plus the distance covered during braking.

Therefore:

- it increases as speed increases

- it depends on the driver's reflexes

- it increases when tyre grip decreases, and therefore if tyres are worn, if the road is wet, snowy or covered in mud (it decreases if the asphalt is rough)

- it increases if the downhill gradient of the road increases

603.description_en:
The safe following distance is the distance to be kept from the vehicle in front, to allow your vehicle to stop in time in case of danger, avoiding rear-ending the vehicle ahead.

It is not a fixed value, but the minimum must be at least equal to the distance travelled during reaction time (i.e. the metres the vehicle covers in roughly one second).



This distance must be adjusted according to:

- the speed of your own vehicle and that of the vehicle in front

- the readiness of your reflexes and the driver's psychophysical condition (attention, concentration, state of health, etc.)

- traffic conditions

- the horizontal and vertical layout of the road (presence and extent of uphill or downhill sections)

- weather conditions (rain, snow, fog)

- the type of vehicle you are driving and its state of efficiency, for example the condition of the service brakes (not the handbrake), the condition and grip of the tyres, and the amount of load carried.

It does not depend on the number of lanes on the road, its width, the size of the vehicle in front, the speed limit shown on the back of the vehicle ahead, the width of your vehicle, the type of fuel (petrol, diesel, LPG), its engine capacity or power, the gear engaged, the number of gears or wheels, or the presence of power steering.



The safe distance to keep from a snow-clearing or salt-spreading machine in operation is 20 metres.

On an extra-urban road with one lane per direction, the distance between vehicles carrying goods with a total mass over 3.5 tonnes, which have been prohibited from overtaking, must be at least 100 metres.

There are no specific indications on the minimum safe following distance to keep on steep downhill sections in bad weather (heavy rain, snowfall), whether travelling in the emergency lane or on extra-urban roads.



It must always be maintained, including before starting an overtaking manoeuvre or when proceeding at low speed.

It must be increased when driving in a convoy, when it is difficult to assess the behaviour of the driver of the vehicle ahead, or when that vehicle is carrying a protruding or unstable load.





It is not true that:

- the driver is obliged to check that the vehicle behind them keeps a safe following distance

- it must be at least equal to the visibility distance or equal to the braking distance

- it must be at least 100 metres in heavy rain

- it may decrease in tunnels

- if the vehicle ahead is a lorry, it must be reduced

- on motorways it may be reduced



To calculate the minimum safe following distance, remember that it equals the reaction distance.

So, based on what has been explained, calculating the reaction distance gives:

- 9 m at 30 km/h (30x10/36 = 8.33 rounded up = 9)

- 14 m at 50 km/h

- 28 m at 100 km/h

- 36 m at 130 km/h

- 42 m at 150 km/h

604.description_en: Driver distraction is a hazard and can cause accidents (even if it lasts only a few seconds). It can be caused by switching on and using a mobile phone, lighting a cigarette, or looking for the controls of the radio or other electronic devices.

650.description_en:
As a general rule, all vehicles must travel on the right side of the carriageway and close to the right-hand edge (even if the rest of the road is clear).

Vehicles without an engine (animal-drawn vehicles, bicycles, etc.) must keep as close as possible to the right-hand edge of the carriageway.

On two-way roads with two lanes, vehicles must move as close as possible to the right-hand edge of the carriageway when meeting other vehicles or when driving on stretches with limited visibility (such as when climbing a hump). This applies to all types of vehicles.

Motor vehicles may travel in parallel rows near intersections controlled by traffic police or traffic lights.

No vehicle may drive in lanes reserved for other vehicles (lanes reserved for public transport, emergency lanes, cycle paths, etc.), not even in heavy traffic.



It is not true that, to turn left, vehicles must keep to the right-hand edge of the carriageway.

In that case, on a two-way road, drivers must move toward the centre of the carriageway; on a one-way road, they must move toward the left-hand edge.

651.title_en: Correct use of the road and behaviour necessary to avoid creating a hazard or obstruction to traffic
651.description_en:
You must drive in a manner suited to the characteristics of the vehicle, the road, and the traffic, observing not only the traffic rules but also the precautions dictated by common sense, and combining them with a strong sense of civic responsibility. It is not true that you must give way to all vehicles at intersections or always proceed at constant speed.

Correct use of the road means that:
- vehicles proceed at a speed appropriate to road and traffic conditions, respecting the speed limits set by law
- the rules of conduct and those dictated by common prudence are observed
- drivers hurry to clear the intersection when the steady yellow light appears on the traffic light and they are unable to stop the vehicle safely before the stop line
- right-of-way is given to pedestrians crossing at pedestrian crossings
- dipped headlights are used in built-up areas at night
- rear-view mirrors are checked before activating the indicator to change lanes

Drivers of high-performance vehicles are also subject to the rules that apply to all drivers.

Since it constitutes a hazard or obstruction to traffic, it is prohibited to:
- keep to the left-hand edge of the carriageway in order to turn into a road on the right
- park on tram tracks
- make a change of direction without signalling the manoeuvre with sufficient advance notice
- race against speed
- drive at excessively low speed without a justified reason
