It is not true that it is prohibited to temporarily stop a vehicle along the right-hand edge of a one-way carriageway.

It is not true that the driver of a vehicle may fit two-tone horns to be heard more easily and use them only outside built-up areas, or that the horn must be sounded in built-up areas every time one approaches a cycle crossing.

653.description_en: On a two-way road with three lanes, as shown in the figure, the right-hand and left-hand lanes are reserved for normal driving, while the central lane is used only for overtaking in either direction. You may not drive in parallel rows.

656.title_en: Road divided into two separate carriageways (1)
656.description_en:
On a road with two separate carriageways, as shown in the figure, vehicles must drive on the carriageway to the right relative to their direction of travel.

It is not true that the left-hand carriageway must be used for overtaking.

657.title_en: Road divided into two separate carriageways (2)
657.description_en:
On a road with two separate carriageways, as shown in the figure, vehicles must travel on the carriageway to the right with respect to their direction of travel.

It is not true that the carriageway on the left must be used for overtaking.

659.title_en: Road divided into four separate carriageways
659.description_en: On a road with four separate carriageways, it is not true that the central ones are reserved for overtaking, since it is the lanes, not the carriageways, that are designated for overtaking.

660.description_en:
Driving in parallel files is not always permitted.



It is permitted

- when authorised by traffic officers

- on roads with two lanes per direction at an intersection controlled by traffic officers or traffic lights

- in heavy traffic on roads with at least two lanes per direction (therefore also on one-way roads with at least two lanes)



While driving in parallel files:

- it is permitted to change lane to carry out turning manoeuvres

- it is not true that when driving in the left lane, the left turn indicator must be kept on

- motorcycles may not proceed by passing between side-by-side vehicles

661.description_en:
Anyone intending to change lane:

- must check that the line dividing the lanes is dashed

- must check that the lane they wish to enter is clear ahead and behind (no other vehicles approaching) for a sufficient distance

- when overtaking, must check that the vehicle ahead has not signalled the start of the same manoeuvre

- must signal the manoeuvre in advance, using the turn indicator (even if the road is clear)

- must not obstruct or endanger those travelling in the lane they wish to enter

- it is not true that they are obliged to signal the manoeuvre with the horn



It is never permitted to drive straddling lane lines, not even when intending to turn.

662.description_en:
It is possible to change lane only as long as the line dividing the lanes is dashed.

It is not true that it can be done up to the transverse stop line.

663.description_en: When you want to change direction, you must activate the turn signal in advance. Use of audible signals is not mandatory, except in case of danger.

664.description_en:
It must be carried out without creating danger or obstruction to others. You must therefore signal the manoeuvre in advance by activating the turn indicator.

It is performed by moving into the lane that allows this manoeuvre, keeping as close as possible to the right edge of the carriageway and reducing speed as you approach the turning point. Then, leave the centre of the intersection on your left and give right-of-way to pedestrians crossing the road you are entering.

It is not true that you go around the traffic light column possibly placed in the centre of the intersection, nor is it necessary to move close to the centre of the intersection.



If an articulated lorry intends to turn right on a narrow road:

- drivers of other vehicles must keep in mind that it may considerably reduce speed and anticipate that, during the manoeuvre, it will move to the left (swing out)

- do not stay too close to it, so as not to obstruct it, in case a reversing manoeuvre becomes necessary

- you must refrain from overtaking it, because it could block the view of signs or vehicles coming from the side

- it is not true that drivers of following vehicles must activate the hazard warning lights

665.description_en:
It must be carried out without creating danger or obstruction to others:

- check in the rear-view mirror that no following vehicle has started to overtake

- then signal the manoeuvre in advance by activating the turn indicator

- take care not to enter the road you are turning into on the wrong side

It is performed by moving into the lane that allows this manoeuvre, therefore:

- on a two-way road, move towards the centre of the carriageway

- on a one-way road, move as close as possible to the left edge

Unless otherwise signposted, a left turn gives right-of-way to vehicles coming from the right, from ahead, and to pedestrians.

It is not necessary to stop before completing the manoeuvre if no vehicles are approaching.



At an intersection:

- if there is a ROUNDABOUT sign (fig. 104), occupy the area on the right, leaving the centre of the intersection on your left

- otherwise, occupy the area on the left, leaving the centre of the intersection on your right

666.title_en: Left turn at an intersection without a roundabout
666.description_en: Occupy the area on the left, leaving the centre of the intersection on your right.

667.title_en: Left turn at an intersection with a roundabout sign
667.description_en: Occupy the area on the right, leaving the centre of the intersection on your left (vehicle H).

668.description_en:
The driver intending to make a U-turn with the vehicle must verify that they are not in conditions that prevent it (heavy and continuous traffic, one-way road, solid center line, poor visibility) and must not create danger or obstruction for other road users.

They must therefore activate the turn indicator (which must remain on for the entire duration of the maneuver) and give way to all approaching vehicles.

It is not true that they must activate the hazard warning lights.

It is not permitted:

- on a one-way road

- when the center line is solid

- in all cases of poor visibility

- near or at curves

- near or at intersections

- near or at humps

- on a motorway

It is not true that it can only be performed on wide roads, allowing it to be done in a single maneuver.

It is not true that it cannot be performed in the absence of road markings or when the edge line is solid.

669.title_en: Merging into the flow of traffic
669.description_en:
The driver intending to merge into the flow of traffic must ensure they can perform the maneuver without creating danger or obstruction for other road users, taking into account their position, distance, and direction.

They must therefore activate the turn indicator to signal their intention well in advance (even if no other vehicles are approaching) and give way to vehicles already in transit (all types of vehicles, including bicycles).



Before setting off:

- the driver of a car must fasten the seat belt unless exempt, and make sure the road is clear, also checking the rear-view mirrors

- the driver of a motorcycle must wear and fasten the helmet and switch on the dipped headlight

670.title_en: Merging into the flow of traffic in reverse
670.description_en:
Vehicle S, moving in reverse to merge into traffic, must ensure they can perform the maneuver without creating danger or obstruction for other road users. They must therefore activate the turn indicator and give way to vehicles in transit (both from the right and from the left).

In addition, they must pay attention to any pedestrians passing behind them and give them right-of-way, make sure the road is clear, and carry out the maneuver with particular caution.

It is not true that they must activate the hazard warning lights, switch on the rear fog light, or repeatedly sound the horn during the maneuver.



Failure to comply with the rules prescribed for merging into the flow of traffic entails, among other things, the loss of points from the driving licence.

671.title_en: Stopping on the right edge of the carriageway
671.description_en:
The driver intending to stop on the right edge of the carriageway must avoid creating danger for drivers of approaching vehicles (two or four wheeled), signalling their intention well in advance by activating the turn indicator (even if traffic is light) and avoiding sudden braking.

It is not true that they must flash repeatedly or activate the hazard warning lights.



The loss of points from the driving licence is provided only for failure to comply with the rules prescribed regarding the parking prohibition.

Therefore, it is not true that, when stopping on the right edge of the carriageway without signalling the intention to perform this maneuver well in advance, points are deducted from the driver's licence.

672.description_en:
It is not permitted:

- to drive in a zig-zag manner, even if the directional lanes are marked by dashed lines

- to suddenly change direction of travel

- to make a U-turn

- to occupy the opposite lane of traffic (not even, for example, to overtake a bicycle)

- if outside built-up areas, to make a stop

It is not true that it is not permitted to exceed 60 km/h, to operate sound signalling devices, or that overtaking is not permitted where regulated by traffic lights.



When approaching an intersection:

- you must prepare to observe the right-of-way rules

- use the utmost caution to avoid accidents

- you must move in good time into the lane for the direction you intend to take

- you must signal your intention to turn in good time

- when riding a two-wheeled vehicle, you must queue behind the other vehicles waiting

- it is permitted to enter the intersection only if you have the ability to proceed and clear it

- if you cannot immediately tell who has right-of-way, you must proceed with caution and care

If two vehicles arrive simultaneously from different roads, the obligation to give way generally falls to the driver of the vehicle arriving from the left, but both have the obligation to moderate speed to avoid accidents. One must be prudent and tolerant towards those who, although not having right-of-way, pass first anyway.



When, upon approaching an intersection, we realise we have chosen the wrong pre-selection lane, we must follow the direction permitted by any road markings (giving the due right-of-way).

To avoid confusion, rear-end collisions, and to avoid obstructing other vehicles, one must not change lanes, brake suddenly, or stop to ask for directions (not even from traffic officers).

It is not true that we must pull over to the right and stop until the column of following vehicles has passed, reverse back to the point where the solid lines end, or wait for the light to allow us to change lanes.



If, at the go-ahead signal, the vehicle in front is slow to set off:

- in built-up areas it is prohibited to use the horn to urge the driver of the vehicle in front to resume moving

- it is advisable to wait patiently for the vehicle to move off

- it is advisable to avoid sounding the horn insistently and causing intolerance among other motorists

- it is advisable, if necessary and possible without danger, to assist the motorist who has remained stationary

- one must not overtake it with dangerous manoeuvres

It is not true that it is advisable to try to clear the carriageway as quickly as possible, including by reversing direction or getting out to look for a traffic officer to take the appropriate measures.

673.description_en:
Before entering the roundabout, reduce speed and use maximum caution while monitoring the behavior of other road users.

The general rule is to give way to the right. You must yield to vehicles coming from the left only where the "DARE PRECEDENZA" (Give Way) sign is present. In that case, traffic is regulated so that vehicles entering the roundabout give way to those already circulating on the ring.

Inside the roundabout, reversing and overtaking, from either the right or the left, are not permitted.

Vehicles that do not need to exit at the first right-hand turn are not required to keep to the inner lane.

674.description_en: When leaving a private property (garage, courtyard, etc.) with a vehicle, be careful, proceed slowly (especially when reversing), and give way to all vehicles and pedestrians. There is no obligation to sound the horn.

675.title_en: Right-of-way between vehicles on a narrow, steeply sloping road
675.description_en: If, on a steeply sloping road, two vehicles cannot easily pass each other, the driver travelling downhill generally must stop and, if necessary, reverse. If one of the drivers is near a passing bay, that driver must pull over and let the other driver pass.

676.title_en: If at night you meet a vehicle with high beams on
676.description_en:
When you meet a vehicle with its high beams on at night on a non-urban road, proceed with caution. Use your low beams, look away from the light beam so that you are not dazzled, slow down appropriately and, if necessary, stop.

Also account for reduced visibility in your driving, and avoid sudden maneuvers and lane changes.

It is not true that you must set the interior rear-view mirror to its anti-glare position, stop immediately, try to shield your eyes with your hands, or sound the horns.

677.description_en:
In heavy traffic, the driver must adjust speed as closely as possible to that of the traffic flowing in the lane being used, always keep a safe distance from the vehicle ahead, and avoid sounding the horn to urge the vehicles ahead to speed up.

It is not true that the driver must repeatedly change lanes in order to always use the freest one, occupy lanes reserved for public transport vehicles (even when they are free), or use the simultaneous flashing of all direction indicators.

678.description_en:
When, inside a built-up area, the driver of a vehicle comes across a procession, they cannot interrupt it. They must stop on the right and wait for the carriageway to clear. Before proceeding, they must make sure the procession has fully passed.

They must avoid sounding the horn, and must not reverse or make a U-turn if this obstructs the flow of traffic.

If possible, they may turn into a side street, provided the manoeuvre can be carried out correctly.

679.title_en: If a pedestrian, outside a crosswalk, does not yield to us, you must:
679.description_en: When a pedestrian, outside a crosswalk, does not show any sign of yielding right-of-way to us, you must reduce speed, warn them of immediate danger with a short horn tap and, if necessary, stop so as not to hit them.

680.title_en: In the presence of a police car
680.description_en:
Drivers must follow the hazard warnings or instructions shown on the illuminated displays of police vehicles.

If a police car with its siren on overtakes you and positions itself in front of you, and its roof display shows an illuminated message:

- 'ACCOSTARE' (pull over): you must bring your vehicle to a forced halt

- 'ALT POLIZIA' (police stop): only you are required to come to a halt

- 'INCIDENTE' (accident): you must reduce speed because an accident has occurred ahead

- 'RALLENTARE' (slow down): you must slow down (the obligation applies to all vehicles)

681.description_en:
Cargo must be loaded onto motor vehicles so that it:

- does not exceed the load capacity stated in the vehicle registration document (carta di circolazione)

- does not fall off

- does not compromise the stability of the vehicle

- does not reduce the driver's visibility or restrict freedom of movement while driving

- does not cover lighting and visual signalling devices, number plates, or hand signals given by the arm (this applies to vehicles without an engine, such as bicycles)

- does not project from the rear by more than three tenths of the vehicle's length. In that case, the load must be marked with a reflective panel with white and red stripes.


On motorcycles, the load must be securely fastened and positioned so that it does not project sideways by more than 50 cm. Animals may be transported if kept in a suitable cage.

682.description_en:
Drivers must give way to vehicles on their RIGHT:

- at intersections without signals

- where the sign 'INTERSEZIONE CON PRECEDENZA A DESTRA' (intersection with right-of-way to the right) is posted



Drivers must give way to vehicles on their RIGHT and LEFT:

- where the sign DARE PRECEDENZA (give way) is posted

- where the sign FERMARSI E DARE PRECEDENZA (stop and give way) is posted

- to vehicles running on rails (trams, trains), unless signalled otherwise

- to emergency vehicles (ambulances, police) with their alarm (siren) active; stop if necessary

- when leaving tracks, mule paths, parking areas, or a driveway access

- when reversing or changing direction of travel

- when pulling out into the flow of traffic from a standstill

Giving way to the right and left is not required at an intersection pre-signalled with the sign INCROCIO CON DIRITTO DI PRECEDENZA (intersection with priority road), INCROCIO CON PRECEDENZA A DESTRA (intersection with right-of-way to the right), or where the ROTATORIA (roundabout, fig. 104) sign is present.

The same applies when turning left (in that case, you give way to vehicles coming from the right and from ahead), or at intersections with a yellow traffic light (in that case, generally you give way only to vehicles on the right).

683.description_en:
To drive, mopeds, motor vehicles, and cars must be fitted with rear-view mirrors, which contribute to the driver's panoramic view.

The mirrors must be of an approved type, correctly mounted, and kept in good working order (not cracked or dirty).

Mirrors do not allow the driver to see the entire area of road behind and around the vehicle, so their use must often be combined with a direct look by slightly turning the head.

Mirrors must be adjusted to provide full visibility. This adjustment must be made each time the vehicle is used (it is not true that it only needs adjusting every 1,000 km), and after the driver's seat position has been set. Adjustment should normally be done with the vehicle stationary.



Rear-view mirrors must be used, both inside and outside built-up areas, whenever you need to check the road behind the vehicle. In particular:

- when pulling out into traffic (when setting off from a standstill)

- before changing lane or turning

- before starting and during a reverse parking manoeuvre (even if the vehicle has parking sensors)

- before starting an overtaking manoeuvre, and before moving back to the right to complete it safely, without cutting in front of the overtaken vehicle.

You do not need to use them every time you intend to go straight ahead at an intersection.

It is not true that:

- the size of rear-view mirrors is proportional to the engine displacement of the vehicle

- the interior light of the rear-view mirror turns on when the vehicle's position lights are switched on

- motorhomes may omit rear-view mirrors if these make them too wide

- external rear-view mirrors on cars may be replaced with a different type, provided the surface is larger

- rear-view mirrors on two-wheeled vehicles are fixed and cannot be adjusted



The central rear-view mirror of a car must be adjusted so that it falls within the driver's field of view and provides a view of the entire rear window.

It is generally designed to minimise distortion of the distance of following vehicles.

It has an anti-glare position for use at night, which reduces the discomfort to the eyes caused by the headlights of following vehicles.

It is not true that cars fitted with rear headrests do not have a central rear-view mirror because it is unusable, that the central rear-view mirror of a car may be removed if the vehicle has a left-side mirror, or that the central rear-view mirror may be used as a screen for a satellite navigation device.



The left-side rear-view mirror must be adjusted so that the rear of the vehicle appears in its right third, and so that the driver mainly observes the portion of road alongside the vehicle on the left.

It must be used:

- before changing lane to the left or turning left

- before pulling out into the flow of traffic

- before starting an overtaking manoeuvre

It is advisable that checking the left-side mirror is also accompanied by a quick direct side glance (that is, slightly turning the head).

This is because the left-side mirror has a very wide blind spot and distorts the perception of distance (vehicles appear farther away than they really are) and of the speed of approaching vehicles.

It is not true that the left-side rear-view mirror must be folded away when driving on narrow roads, or that it must be adjusted so that the interior of the vehicle can be checked.

700.description_en:
The driver must give right-of-way to traffic coming from the right:

- at intersections without signals

- where the sign 'INTERSECTION WITH RIGHT-OF-WAY TO THE RIGHT' is present

The driver must give right-of-way to traffic from both the right and the left:

- where the sign 'GIVE WAY' is present

- where the sign 'STOP AND GIVE WAY' is present

- to vehicles running on rails (trams, trains), unless signed otherwise

- to emergency vehicles (ambulances, police) with their siren activated, stopping if necessary

- when leaving tracks, mule paths, parking areas, or driveway access

- when reversing or making a U-turn

- when pulling out from a standstill into the flow of traffic

750.title_en: The danger of overtaking is determined by
750.description_en:
- the risk of colliding with other vehicles that intend to make the same manoeuvre

- the risk of collision with the vehicle being overtaken during the approach, side-by-side phase, and pull-in

- the risk of a head-on collision with a vehicle coming from the opposite direction

- the reduced width of the carriageway

751.title_en: A driver who intends to overtake must:
751.description_en:
- make sure visibility is sufficient to carry out the manoeuvre safely

- make sure the manoeuvre can be completed without obstructing others

- make sure the road is clear enough to allow the overtaking to be completed in full

- make sure the width of the carriageway allows it

- make sure no vehicle is coming from the opposite direction

- make sure that vehicles behind or ahead have not begun or signalled an intention to make a similar manoeuvre

- make sure there are no signs prohibiting it

- assess the space needed for the manoeuvre, including the difference in speed between their vehicle and the one being overtaken, and the length of both vehicles

Then:

- signal the manoeuvre to drivers behind by activating the left turn indicator. Drivers ahead may be warned with the horn (where permitted) or by flashing the high beams, so that they do not start the same manoeuvre

- adjust speed to that of the vehicle being overtaken and keep an adequate lateral distance from it

- after completing the overtaking, return to the right as soon as possible (signalling with the right turn indicator) without creating danger or obstruction, checking the position of the overtaken vehicle in the rear-view mirrors. Do not cut in on or obstruct the overtaken vehicle, and leave a safe distance proportional to its speed.

After completing a first overtaking manoeuvre, on roads with at least two lanes per direction, it is possible to carry out another one without returning to the right, provided this does not cause obstruction.

752.title_en: The driver of the vehicle being overtaken must
752.description_en:
- assist the overtaking manoeuvre and not accelerate

- on roads with one lane per direction, keep as close as possible to the right edge

- not race the overtaking vehicle

- if driving a very slow vehicle, stop as soon as possible to let traffic pass

- if being overtaken while a vehicle is approaching from the opposite direction, it is advisable to reduce speed and move as close as possible to the right edge of the carriageway

If you are overtaken and a collision occurs, you may bear some responsibility if you did not do everything possible to facilitate the overtaking manoeuvre.

It is not true that the driver must always reduce speed or shift to a lower gear to facilitate overtaking.

753.title_en: The space needed for an overtaking manoeuvre
753.description_en:
- is important for road safety

- increases when overtaking a column of vehicles

- increases as the length of either vehicle (overtaking or overtaken) increases

- increases if the vehicle being overtaken accelerates

- depends on the difference in speed between the overtaking and overtaken vehicles: it is greater when the speed difference is small

The safe following distance must also be respected when beginning the overtaking manoeuvre.

754.description_en:
- when signs prohibit it

- when there is not enough free space or sufficient visibility

- when the vehicle behind or the vehicle ahead has already started the overtaking manoeuvre

- if it requires crossing a solid white longitudinal line, single or double

- near bends and humps (on the uphill section) on two-lane, two-way roads

- at railway level crossings without barriers (except where traffic is controlled by traffic lights)

- at uncontrolled intersections

- on acceleration or deceleration lanes

- in all cases of poor visibility

- of a vehicle that is overtaking another vehicle, if this requires moving onto the lane reserved for the opposite direction of travel

- of stationary or slow-moving vehicles at railway level crossings or traffic lights, if it requires entering the opposite half of the carriageway

- of vehicles moving slowly due to traffic congestion, when this requires moving onto the lane reserved for the opposite direction of travel

- of a vehicle that has slowed down or stopped at a pedestrian crossing to allow pedestrians to cross

- if the vehicle to be overtaken has stopped to give way to pedestrians, including outside pedestrian crossings

- of police, fire brigade or ambulance vehicles, but only when they are on an emergency call

- on the right of a stationary tram if there is no safety island



It is permitted to overtake a police car if it is not on an emergency call and there are no other obstacles.

It is not true that overtaking is prohibited at night, in urban areas with insufficient public lighting, at the exit of a public car park, near hospitals, or near filling stations.

756.title_en: Overtaking near a hump is permitted
756.description_en:
- on one-way roads

- on two-way roads with at least two lanes per direction of travel

- on roads with separate carriageways

- on two-way roads with two lanes, only on the downhill section of the hump

757.title_en: Overtaking on the right is permitted
757.description_en:
- when the driver of the vehicle ahead has signalled the intention to turn left or pull over to the left on a one-way road

- when overtaking a trolleybus (or tram) that is travelling in the centre of the road, or that is stopped for passengers to board and alight, but only where there is a safety island

- at traffic-light-controlled intersections, if the vehicle to be overtaken has signalled its intention to turn left and has started the manoeuvre

758.description_en:
During an overtaking manoeuvre on a motorway, the following can cause an accident:

- insufficient attention paid to vehicles behind

- insufficient safe following distance

- sudden movement into the overtaking lane by one of the vehicles ahead

- staying too long in the overtaking lane

- strong crosswind that compromises vehicle stability

- overtaking by queuing behind a vehicle that is already overtaking

800.description_en:
Before starting to drive a vehicle (car, motorcycle, etc.), you should always:

- adjust the seat and head restraint to your height

- adjust the interior and exterior rear-view mirrors

- make sure your licence category allows you to drive the vehicle

- make sure the vehicle is in perfect working order

- make sure carried objects are secured so they cannot fall or scatter

- check that rear and side visibility is not compromised by passengers or badly positioned cargo

- identify the controls (levers and buttons) needed for driving and understand how they work

- if driving a car, check that passengers have properly fastened their seat belts

It is not true that you should:

- reset the trip odometer

- disable the driver's side airbag

- check that the seat belts are fitted with pretensioners



When driving a motor vehicle, you must carry all the documents required for driving (vehicle registration document, insurance certificate, driving licence, etc.), and they must be valid.

801.description_en: Stopping (arresto) is the interruption of the vehicle's movement due to traffic requirements, such as at a red traffic light.

802.description_en:
A brief stop (fermata) of a vehicle is the temporary suspension of movement for very short-term needs, such as asking information from traffic officers or allowing people to get in or out.

During a brief stop the driver must always remain present and ready to resume driving.

A brief stop is not permitted if it obstructs traffic.

The driver must take appropriate precautions so as not to create a danger for other road users and not to cause accidents.



Where a brief stop may be made:

- where there is no raised sidewalk, the driver must leave a space of at least one metre for pedestrians to pass

- outside built-up areas, the driver must, if possible, place the vehicle outside the carriageway (but not on cycle paths), otherwise as close as possible to the right edge of the carriageway



A brief stop is prohibited:

- where the specific 'No Stopping' sign is present and in all places where it obstructs traffic

- outside built-up areas, at and near intersection areas

- within built-up areas at intersection areas (junctions and level crossings) and within 5 metres of them, unless otherwise indicated

- at or near level crossings

- on railway or tramway tracks, or so close to them as to obstruct the movement of rail vehicles

- in tunnels, unless otherwise indicated

- in underpasses, under overpasses, under arches and porticoes, unless otherwise indicated

- near speed humps

- on bends and, outside built-up areas and on urban arterial roads, also near them

- near and at vertical and/or traffic light road signs if the view of the sign is obstructed

- on motorways, except in emergencies

- on pedestrian and cycle crossings, on cycle paths (and their exits) and on sidewalks (on the latter unless otherwise indicated)

- at horizontal pre-selection markings and along channelling lanes

Stopping in front of urban waste bins is, however, permitted.



It is NOT true that stopping is prohibited:

- along the left edge of a one-way carriageway

- at the exit of driveways or near them

- on areas designated for markets or for loading and unloading goods

- in any case in double parking

- in any case at night



In all cases where a brief stop is prohibited, parking is also prohibited (but not vice versa).

803.description_en:
Parking (sosta) is the suspension of the vehicle's movement for an extended period, with the driver being able to leave the vehicle.

While parked, the driver must prevent use of the vehicle without their consent and take appropriate precautions to avoid accidents.

It is NOT true that during parking at night the driver must always leave the position lights on.



When parked, it is advisable for the driver to switch off the engine, apply the parking brake and engage the lowest gear; on roads with steep gradients, it is also advisable to leave the vehicle with the wheels turned towards the sidewalk.

It is NOT true that the driver of a car may leave the engine running if parking for a short time.



Unless otherwise indicated, the driver parking within built-up areas must place the vehicle as close as possible to the right edge of the carriageway, parallel to it and in the direction of travel, provided that a raised sidewalk exists. Where none exists, they must leave a space of at least one metre for pedestrians to pass.

On one-way urban roads, parking is also permitted along the left edge of the carriageway, provided that sufficient space (at least three metres) remains for at least one line of vehicles to pass.

It is NOT true that parking cars or motorcycles within built-up areas is prohibited when no marked bays exist.



Outside built-up areas, the driver who needs to park must, where possible, place the vehicle outside the carriageway, but not on cycle paths and not on road shoulders, unless otherwise indicated. If it is impossible to place the vehicle outside the carriageway, they must park as close as possible to the right edge of the carriageway.



In zones set aside for parking, the driver must position the vehicle as prescribed by the signage, placing their vehicle within one of the designated spaces (bays) without encroaching on adjacent ones.



In a zone where parking is regulated by a parking meter, the meter must be used even for short-term parking; it should not be used in case of a mere stop, for example to let a passenger out.

When parking in a zone regulated by a parking meter, the appropriate ticket must be displayed so that it is clearly visible.

To park in a zone regulated by a parking disc, the arrival time (not the end-of-parking time) must be displayed clearly. The time cannot be updated without having moved the vehicle.

In time-limited parking areas, vehicles serving disabled persons are not required to comply with the time limit set for parking.



Parking is prohibited in all cases where a brief stop is prohibited, and also:

- during the hours and on the days when the signs prohibiting it are in effect (where 'No Parking' is present, within built-up areas from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m., and on extra-urban roads 24 hours a day)

- always where the 'No Stopping' sign is present

- at the exit of driveways

- if it prevents access to or movement of other parked vehicles

- in double parking, except for two-wheeled vehicles (it is NOT true that it is permitted for a few minutes by switching on the hazard lights)

- in spaces reserved for the parking and stopping of buses, trolleybuses and rail-borne vehicles

- within 15 metres of a bus, trolleybus or rail-vehicle stop sign, where parking spaces are not demarcated

- in spaces reserved for the parking of taxis and hire vehicles

- on areas designated for markets and for vehicles loading and unloading goods, during the specified hours

- on road shoulders, unless otherwise indicated

- in spaces reserved for stopping or parking vehicles for disabled persons

- at ramps or kerb transitions between the sidewalk and the carriageway used by vehicles for disabled persons

- in bus lanes or carriageways reserved for public transport (it is NOT true that it is permitted in certain time slots)

- in pedestrian areas within urban zones

- in limited traffic zones for unauthorised vehicles

- in spaces designated for emergency or public hygiene services indicated by the specific signage

- during opening hours, at fuel stations and within 5 metres before and after them

In none of these cases is it possible to park even 'for a few minutes'.

Where parking is expressly prohibited by a provision of the Highway Code, compliance with that prohibition is not conditional on the presence of signs.



Within built-up areas, the driver must not leave a trailer detached from the towing vehicle parked, unless otherwise indicated.



Failure to comply with the prescribed rules on parking prohibitions results, in addition to a fine, in the loss of points from the driving licence.

It is NOT true that it results in suspension of the driving licence.

804.description_en:
When opening a vehicle's doors, you must ensure that this does not create danger or obstruction for other road users.

The driver must also check, using the rear-view mirror, that no other vehicles are approaching.

In addition to paying attention personally, the driver must also alert their passengers.

If the door is opened on the side facing the centre of the road, you must ensure that no other vehicles are approaching.

If a road is narrow, it is necessary to check that no vehicles are approaching either from the front or from behind.

If the door is opened on the side facing the sidewalk, you must ensure that no pedestrians are approaching.

805.description_en:
An emergency stop (sosta di emergenza) is the interruption of movement when the vehicle cannot be used due to a breakdown, or in the case of physical illness of the driver or a passenger.

It is NOT true that it is the temporary suspension of movement to allow a disabled person to get in or out.

850.title_en: Traffic rules on motorways and main rural roads
850.description_en:
On motorways and main rural roads, the following are prohibited:
- pedestrians and animals, except in service areas and parking areas (animals only if properly restrained), and on emergency lanes, where pedestrians may enter only to reach emergency call points
- pedal cycles
- mopeds
- motorcycles with an engine capacity below 150 cm3
- cars that cannot, by design, reach at least 80 km/h on a level road
- agricultural machinery
- vehicles with an untidy load that is not securely fastened or that protrudes beyond the permitted limits
- vehicles that are not watertight and carry an open load, if the load consists of materials that could scatter
- vehicles whose condition of use, equipment or tyres could pose a danger to traffic
- vehicles that do not have a valid periodic technical inspection

On motorways and main rural roads (that is, on carriageways, ramps, interchanges, service areas or parking areas):
- asking for or giving lifts is prohibited
- helping a broken-down vehicle is prohibited. Instead, keep driving and, if useful, stop at the next service area or exit toll booth to report the breakdown
- only authorized emergency vehicles may tow broken-down vehicles
- commercial activities are allowed only if authorized by the road owner
- camping is allowed only in designated areas and for the period set by the road owner
- in service areas, drivers must not leave their vehicle parked for more than 24 hours
- use of dipped-beam headlights is mandatory, including during the day
- reversing direction and crossing the central median, including at the crossover gaps, are prohibited
- driving on the carriageway, or any part of it, against the permitted direction of travel is prohibited
- reversing is prohibited
- driving on the emergency parking lane is permitted only to come to a halt because of a vehicle breakdown
- a driver using the acceleration lane must give way to vehicles travelling in the traffic lanes
- drivers must move into the right-hand lane in good time, and then enter the deceleration lane from its start
- drivers must signal lane changes in good time using their indicators
- in a traffic jam, if the emergency lane is missing or too narrow for police or rescue vehicles to pass, the driver in the first right-hand lane must position the vehicle as close as possible to the left-hand edge line
- in a traffic jam, drivers may use the emergency parking lane only to leave the motorway, starting from the exit advance sign placed 500 metres before the junction
- parking on the emergency lane is allowed only in emergencies caused by the driver or passengers feeling unwell, or by a vehicle fault. The stop must not exceed the time strictly necessary and must never last more than three hours.

854.description_en:
The number of people a vehicle may carry is shown on the vehicle registration document (the number is indicated for the front and rear seats).

Passenger cars may carry a maximum of nine people, including the driver. Trucks may carry a maximum of three people, including the driver. Motorcycles may carry a maximum of two people, including the driver.

All passengers in motor vehicles must take a seat in a way that does not restrict the driver's freedom of movement or block the driver's view.

Vehicles may carry one pet, provided it is kept in a way that does not obstruct or endanger the driving. Carrying more than one pet is also allowed, provided they are kept in a cage or in a rear compartment separated by a mesh partition.



Motorcycles may carry a passenger only if the driver is an adult and the vehicle registration document provides a seat for the passenger.

Motorcycles may not carry children under 5 years old.

855.description_en:
The load on vehicles must be secured in such a way that:

- it cannot fall or be scattered

- it does not compromise the stability of the vehicle

- it does not mask lighting and visual signalling devices, registration plates, or hand signals

- it does not reduce the driver's visibility or prevent free movement while driving

The load:

- must not exceed the outline limit (sagoma) set for each type of vehicle

- may not project longitudinally from the front of the vehicle

- may project longitudinally from the rear if it consists of indivisible items, up to 3/10 of the length of the motor vehicle (the longitudinal projection must be marked with one or two dedicated square panels)

- may project laterally beyond the vehicle's outline by no more than 30 cm from the front and rear position lights (in any case within the maximum outline limits)

If the load projects beyond the vehicle's outline, the driver must take all appropriate precautions to avoid endangering other road users.

It is forbidden to carry or tow items that drag along the ground, even if partly supported by wheels.

When driving behind a vehicle with a projecting load, it may be difficult to tell that it intends to turn, if its direction indicators are hidden by the hanging cargo.

When driving behind a vehicle carrying a load at risk of falling:

- it is advisable to increase the safety distance, especially when going uphill

- it is advisable to increase the safety distance and overtake as soon as possible

- it is advisable to warn the driver of the potential danger

- it is better not to follow too closely, so you can stop in time if the cargo falls

- be careful, especially when it brakes or turns, due to the possible fall of the cargo

On motorcycles it is forbidden to carry objects that are not securely fastened, or that in any way prevent or limit the driver's visibility.

On motorcycles the load must be well secured and positioned so that it does not project laterally by more than 50 cm. Animals may be carried if kept in an appropriate cage.

It is not true that carrying objects that project longitudinally beyond the vehicle's outline is forbidden.

857.description_en:
To tow a vehicle with a trailer, the driver must hold one of the following licence categories:

- B (if the vehicle combination does not exceed 3.5 t),

- B with harmonised code 96

- BE.

It is not true that a holder of a BE licence who later obtains a category C licence may also drive vehicles of category CE.

Before setting off, make the electrical connection between the towing vehicle and the trailer (including for light trailers). Make sure the lighting and signalling systems work properly. Also check that the external rear-view mirrors on the towing vehicle give adequate visibility.

When towing a trailer, be aware that:

- fuel consumption increases, even at moderate speeds

- acceleration (pick-up) is noticeably reduced, especially if the trailer is loaded;

- on roads with steep climbs, the temperature of the engine coolant rises

- braking distance increases

- on steep descents, account for the pushing force the trailer exerts on the towing vehicle

- when driving straight ahead, the load tends to shift forward during braking and backward during sharp acceleration;

- the overturning force exerted by the wind increases

- liquid moving inside a tank fixed to a trailer (tanker, bonza, etc.) during changes of direction, braking and acceleration is the main cause of instability in vehicle combinations;

- in turns, the swept path (the space needed to turn) of the vehicle combination is larger, and the trailer tends to cut the corner because it follows a circular path with a smaller radius than the towing vehicle. For example, when turning right, take care not to mount the sidewalk with the rear wheel.

Trailers must be registered and carry their own number plate, even if they are light. It is not true, therefore, that you must remove the plate from the towing vehicle and fit it to the rear of the trailer. Drawbar trailers (carrelli appendice) do not have their own plate. They carry a repeater plate identical to the towing vehicle's plate.

Trailers intended for carrying goods with a maximum laden mass over 3.5 tonnes must be marked with rear and side retroreflective strips and the appropriate rear panels (fig. 305). In addition, the rear of vehicle combinations (articulated lorry, car towing a trailer or caravan, etc.) must display the speed limit markings that apply to them (fig. 301).

The towing capacity of a vehicle is stated in the vehicle registration document (carta di circolazione). This value, called the 'towing ratio', is the ratio between the laden mass of the trailer and the laden mass of the towing vehicle.

It must not exceed:

- 1: for trailers fitted with a service brake and a mass up to 3.5 tonnes

- 0.5: for trailers without any braking device

In practice, with a towing ratio of 1, the trailer's mass can equal the towing vehicle's mass. With 0.5, it can reach half of that mass.

There is no required ratio between the width of the trailer and the width of the towing vehicle.

Mirrors must not project more than 20 centimetres beyond the outline of the vehicle (towing vehicle or trailer), measured at its widest point.

Goods carried in the trailer must be secured so that they cannot shift, overturn, fall or rub during travel.

It is also advisable to load the trailer so that heavy items sit as close as possible to the axle (centre) of the trailer, not above the towing hitch.

The maximum vertical load on the towing hitch must not exceed the limit stated by the manufacturer on the plate fixed to the towing vehicle's hitch. It must also not alter the vehicle's trim or the aim of the headlights.

The load on a trailer (even a light one), as with motor vehicles, may not overhang the front. It may only overhang the rear, up to 3/10 (three tenths, or 30%) of the trailer's length. Any overhanging load must be marked with the appropriate panel (fig. 302).

A load may overhang sideways (so it is not true that the trailer's width must not exceed that of the towing vehicle), provided the overhang on each side does not extend more than 30 cm beyond the front and rear position lights.

Before making any manoeuvre with the trailer coupled, make sure there are no objects or people within the manoeuvring area of the combination.

On motorways with three or more lanes per carriageway, drivers of vehicle combinations longer than 7 metres in total may only use the two lanes nearest the right edge of the carriageway.

Drivers of motor vehicles towing a trailer, when the laden mass of the combination exceeds 3.5 tonnes, are considered to be under the influence of alcohol if a blood alcohol level above zero grams per litre of blood is found.

It is not true that:

- a trailer with a mass up to 3.5 tonnes is considered part of the vehicle (this applies only to drawbar trailers)

- the tyre inflation pressure of the towing vehicle must equal that of the trailer's tyres

- a trailer cannot be coupled to other vehicles

- cars fitted with ABS cannot tow a trailer without a braking system

- parking sensors prevent a trailer from being towed

- if the towing capacity is missing from the vehicle registration document, the vehicle may tow trailers of any mass

- while driving, the trailer's jockey wheel must be lowered (resting on the ground). This swivel wheel can move in any direction and is used for manoeuvring the trailer when it is uncoupled from the towing vehicle.

T.A.T.S. trailers are trailers for transporting leisure and sports equipment (Trasporto di Attrezzature Turistiche e Sportive). They are fitted with specific equipment for carrying tourist and sports gear (such as boats, gliders, etc.). This equipment must not be sold, and must be used only for leisure. The general rules for other trailer types apply to them.

So it is not true that a right-hand rear-view mirror is optional on the towing vehicle, or that boats carried may project up to 50 centimetres on each side.

The general rules for trailers apply to trailers carrying live animals. It is not true that the hazard warning lights must be kept on, or that horse trailers (vans) may not travel on motorways.

Car-towed trailers are usually fitted with an overrun brake (freno ad inerzia). This brake engages when the trailer moves closer to the towing vehicle and pushes against it. The trailer's braking therefore does not happen at the same time as the towing vehicle's braking, but a fraction of a second later.

The driver must remember that an overrun brake can lose effectiveness after a long period of disuse. Rust can damage its components and the braking elements on each wheel.

The trailer has a safety device (steel cable) that automatically applies the parking brake if the trailer accidentally detaches. When leaving a trailer parked, you must still engage the parking brake lever. On a slope, it is advisable to place wheel chocks against the wheels.

The towing devices on the vehicle must be type-approved (regardless of the trailer's mass). They must be kept clean and properly lubricated.

It is therefore not true that they should be degreased with detergents or petrol.

They must allow enough vertical movement between the towing vehicle and the trailer to compensate for differences in inclination caused by uneven roads. However, they must not show play, deformation or cracks. If they break, they cannot be repaired by welding. They must be replaced.

When the towing hitch is not in use, because no trailer is being towed, the part that projects beyond the rear outline of the vehicle must be slid out, removed or folded away.

If a trailer stands unused for a long time, it is advisable, where possible, to keep its tyres off the ground by placing supports under the chassis. If it cannot be lifted off the ground, increase the tyre inflation pressure and change the contact patch of the tyres periodically, to prevent them from going out of round (deformation).

While in use, trailers must be insured under the same policy as the towing vehicle. When detached from the towing vehicle, they must have separate insurance cover for static risk (when stationary). In built-up areas, the driver must not park a trailer detached from the towing vehicle, unless signs indicate otherwise.

Trailers with a mass over 3.5 tonnes must undergo an annual technical inspection. It is not true that trailers must undergo periodic technical inspection together with the towing vehicle. On the contrary, a drawbar trailer's periodic inspection must be carried out at the same time as the vehicle it is registered with on the vehicle registration document, as an integral part of that vehicle.

858.description_en: A caravan is a trailer that can be used as accommodation when the vehicle is stationary. It is not true that people may stay inside while the vehicle is moving, even if all passengers fasten their seat belts. To reduce the risk of overturning on bends, load a caravan as evenly as possible between the right and left sides, and keep the centre of gravity as low as possible by placing heavy items at the bottom.

860.title_en: Portable hazard warning triangle, reflective high-visibility vest and reflective braces
860.description_en:
The portable hazard warning triangle is part of the mandatory equipment of motor vehicles.

It must be used by all motor vehicles, and only outside built-up areas, to warn of vehicles that must remain stopped on the carriageway and of any fallen load that cannot be moved immediately.

It must be used:

- at night, when the rear position lights or hazard lights of a vehicle stopped on the carriageway are not working, or in case of a fallen load or dangerous substances

- for dangerous substances spilled on an extra-urban road

- if the stopped vehicle or fallen load cannot be seen from at least 100 metres away.

The triangle must be placed:

- at least 50 metres from the stopped vehicle or obstacle, so that it is visible from at least 100 m to approaching traffic

- on the lane occupied by the load or vehicle, at least one metre from the outer edge of the carriageway

- stably supported by its dedicated stand so that it does not fall over.


Where an intersection is less than 50 m away, the hazard warning triangle must be placed behind the vehicle in the position where it is most easily seen.


When carrying out advance warning with the hazard triangle, the driver must make themselves visible by wearing an approved high-visibility reflective vest or reflective braces. This also applies when standing on emergency lanes or in parking bays.

Their use is not necessary within built-up areas.


It is NOT true that:

- the high-visibility reflective vest or braces can in every case replace the hazard warning triangle

- they can only be yellow

- the high-visibility reflective vest protects the driver also from chemical risks, heat, fire and electricity

- inside the vehicle you must keep high-visibility reflective vests or braces in a number equal to the available seats

- the obligation to wear a high-visibility vest applies when parking outside built-up areas, while reflective braces must be worn in urban areas

861.title_en: Obstruction of the carriageway and spillage of slippery, flammable or otherwise dangerous materials
861.description_en:
In the event of an obstruction of the carriageway (fallen load, stopped vehicles, spilled substances), the driver must, among other things:

- inform the body that owns the road or a police body

- where required, give advance warning of the obstacle using the hazard warning triangle (vehicle stopped warning)

- give manual signals to prevent traffic from passing on the side where the hazard warning triangle has not been placed.



In the event of an obstruction of the carriageway due to an accidental fall of load, the driver must, if possible, remove the load so that traffic can pass freely.



In the event of an obstruction of the carriageway due to vehicle breakdown, the driver must try to clear the way for oncoming traffic by pushing the vehicle, if possible, off the carriageway, or at most onto the right-hand sidewalk.



Anyone who could not avoid dropping or spilling slippery, flammable or otherwise dangerous materials must, among other things, remove them or, if possible, spread sand, earth, sawdust or other suitable material on the ground to restore grip.



It is NOT true that the driver must divert traffic while waiting for the body that owns the road to intervene and restore optimal conditions.

862.title_en: Risks posed by cyclists, moped riders, bicycles, heavy vehicles and SUVs
862.description_en:
The driver of a passenger car must be aware of the risks posed by slow vehicles, bicycles, mopeds and heavy vehicles (such as lorries, articulated lorries, road trains, buses and SUVs).

The driver must adapt their driving to these risks.



Slow vehicles: agricultural machinery, mopeds and work machines, especially on extra-urban roads. It can be difficult to judge approach times because of the difference in speed between them and the vehicle being driven.



Bicycles: vehicles with modest mass, characterised by low speeds and possible sideways wobbling. A cyclist about to carry out a manoeuvre finds it very difficult to judge the approach speed of motor vehicles in traffic (for example when turning left), especially if they are very young, inexperienced or elderly (as is often the case).



Mopeds: often ridden by young people with limited driving experience, who may make sudden manoeuvres (such as weaving between other vehicles).

When cyclists or moped riders are present, you must keep a safe lateral distance and avoid any sideways deviation, even a slight one, so as not to endanger their balance and avoid a possible fall.

The left-turn manoeuvre is particularly dangerous for a moped, which must cross the path of one or more lines of faster vehicles approaching in the same direction.



Lorries, road trains, articulated lorries, buses and SUVs: because of their greater mass, they can pose a considerable danger to other road users, especially if they do not respect speed limits.

In general, collisions between vehicles are more dangerous when their masses are very different.



SUVs: the driver of an off-road vehicle (SUV):

- must drive with the utmost caution, aware that the height and mass of their vehicle represent a potential danger to pedestrians, cyclists and smaller cars.

- must consider the serious damage that the protruding, reinforced bumpers of their vehicle can cause in a collision with smaller vehicles

- must remember that driving such a vehicle is particularly demanding in town and requires special care, especially during emergency manoeuvres.

863.description_en:
Although the design of the vehicle allows an adequate field of vision, while driving the driver must carefully observe the area ahead and alongside.

The driver's field of vision can be reduced both by one of the head restraints and by bodywork elements of their own car, which can accidentally block the view of other road users. For this reason it is forbidden to apply adhesive films to the windscreen and front side windows of vehicles.

Pedestrians (especially children) or cyclists risk being outside the visual field of drivers of lorries or SUVs because of the height and shape of such vehicles (limited view through the windscreen). Drivers of these vehicles, especially before setting off, for example at traffic lights, must anticipate their presence in front of the vehicle.

For the same reasons, stopping such vehicles in a queue is particularly dangerous when pedestrians or two-wheeled vehicles are present.

901.description_en:
Use of dipped-beam headlights is mandatory:

- in built-up areas from half an hour after sunset to half an hour before sunrise

- outside built-up areas (on motorways and extra-urban roads) even during the day (or, alternatively, daytime running lights may be switched on during the day)

- in conditions of poor visibility due to weather (snow, rain, fog)

- when driving through tunnels (even if they are lit)

- when transporting seriously injured or sick people

- outside built-up areas when public lighting is sufficient (thus in place of main-beam headlights)

- outside built-up areas with insufficient lighting when passing other vehicles, in place of main-beam headlights.



Dipped-beam headlights may dazzle others or reduce the driver's own visibility:

- if the bulbs are fitted incorrectly or are not approved

- if the headlights are aimed too high.

902.description_en:
Using high beams is mandatory outside built-up areas when public lighting is absent or insufficient. It is prohibited on urban roads.

High beams must be replaced with low beams:

- when meeting other vehicles

- when following a vehicle at a short distance

- when there is a risk of dazzling drivers on other roads or pedestrians.

Intermittent use of high beams in place of the horn is allowed to give useful warnings and avoid accidents (overtaking, immediate danger). This applies by day and by night, in built-up areas and outside them.

903.description_en:
Direction indicators must be operated well in advance whenever:

- a turn, a lane change or a reversing manoeuvre is carried out

- entering a carriageway from an acceleration lane

- signalling the intention to move into a deceleration lane

- leaving the carriageway to make a brief stop

- pulling out from the edge of the carriageway into traffic

- starting an overtaking manoeuvre (left indicator to occupy the lane on the left) and when finishing it (right indicator to return to your own lane).

It is not true that their use is required when driving in parallel lanes without changing lanes, or for at least 500 metres after overtaking.

905.description_en: It makes the rear number plate of vehicles, trailers and tractor units readable from at least 20 metres away. It works when the position lights are on and the green light indicator on the dashboard is lit.

907.description_en:
Reflectors are plastic devices that use reflected light to show the presence and size of the vehicles they are fitted to.

When illuminated, they make vehicles and trailers parked (or broken down) on the road more visible, especially at night, even with the lights off.

They can be:

- white if at the front (including on trailers or semi-trailers)

- red if at the rear, mandatory for all vehicles and trailers

- triangular in shape, only at the rear of trailers, semi-trailers and light trailers

- yellow if at the sides, to mark trailers, semi-trailers, light trailers and vehicles of considerable length, meaning those exceeding 6 metres.

912.description_en:
The following warning lights are red:

- simultaneous flashing of the direction indicators (hazard lights)

- engine coolant temperature

- engine oil pressure

- seat belt

- parking brake (handbrake).

913.description_en: It is located on the control for switching on the high beams (driving headlights) and on the related blue indicator light, which shows that the high beams are on.

914.description_en: It is shown on the control for switching on the low-beam headlights and is placed on the related green indicator light, which shows that they are on.

915.description_en: It identifies the turn signal control and is placed on a green indicator light, which may be paired with an audible signal. The light flashes when the turn indicators are operating.

916.description_en:
It identifies the hazard warning control, or hazard warning light. It is placed on a flashing red indicator light and on the switch that turns on all turn indicators at the same time. It identifies the control of a device to be used in emergencies.

Note that simply turning on the four hazard lights cannot replace the warning triangle for a stopped vehicle, which must still be placed in case of a vehicle breakdown.

921.description_en: It is placed on a red indicator light showing that the coolant temperature exceeds the limits set by the manufacturer. It therefore signals that the water and, consequently, the engine is overheating. It complements the water temperature gauge.

922.description_en: Located on a red warning light. When the light is on, it indicates that the generator, alternator or dynamo is not charging the battery, so the battery is not recharging.

923.description_en:
It is placed on a red warning light that shows the pressure of the lubricating oil in the engine.

When the light is on, it indicates insufficient engine oil pressure. If the light stays on while driving, stop immediately to avoid serious damage.

929.description_en:
It is shown on a red warning light that signals a malfunction in part of the braking system.

It may indicate:

- low brake fluid level,

- excessive wear of the brake pads on disc brakes,

- excessive wear of the brake shoe linings on drum brakes,

- excessive wear of the braking element linings.

When the light is on, have the braking system checked, serviced or repaired.

930.description_en: The symbol is placed on a red warning light that, if lit while driving, indicates that the driver or a passenger is not wearing a seat belt. In this case, it is accompanied by an audible signal.

950.description_en:
An airbag is a device consisting of an inflatable cushion made of nylon or another synthetic material. In a violent collision, a sensor triggers the airbag, which inflates within a few milliseconds between the occupants and the vehicle structure.

This device can be dangerous if the seat belt is not worn. Therefore, it is not true that if a vehicle has front and side airbags, you can do without fastening the seat belt.

The airbag cannot work when the ignition key is not inserted, and it can sometimes be deactivated.

It is not true that it must be periodically inflated to check its efficiency, or that it can be calibrated.

In vehicles equipped with an airbag with a deactivation control, the airbag must be deactivated before placing a child seat on the front seat with its backrest facing the windscreen.



If a car is fitted with an airbag, children may be carried in the front seat, secured in a suitable child seat, only if the vehicle has a control to deactivate the airbag.

BUT BE CAREFUL, THIS QUIZ STATEMENT IS ALSO TRUE:

In vehicles that do not have a control to deactivate the passenger-side airbag, the child seat must not be placed on the front seat with its backrest facing the road.

951.description_en:
Passengers under 12 years of age and under 1.5 m in height must use restraint systems, child seats or cushions suitable for their height and weight.

Restraint systems must be of an approved type and always kept in good working order.

Children under 3 years of age may not travel in cars that are not fitted with suitable restraint systems.

Children over 3 years of age may travel:

- in the front seats of a car not fitted with restraint systems, only if their height exceeds 1.50 metres and they wear the seat belts

- in the rear seats of a car not fitted with restraint systems, only if accompanied by an adult

Child restraint systems are classified into groups according to the weight of the child they can accommodate.

952.description_en:
In the event of an accident, seat belts keep the body fastened to the seat, preventing it from striking the interior parts of the vehicle or, worse, being thrown out of the car in a violent impact. They therefore limit injuries to the driver and passengers in an accident.

They must be worn by both the driver and the passengers of cars that are equipped with them, in any driving situation (including at low speeds).

Seat belts must be of an approved and type-certified design.

The driver is required to ensure that the seat belts are always in good working order, by frequently checking their state of wear and replacing them when they have been subjected to a violent strain in a collision.

The following are NOT required to wear seat belts:

- driving instructors while carrying out their activity

- pregnant women, with a certificate issued by the A.S.L. (Local Health Authority) confirming particular risk conditions

- persons suffering from certain medical conditions, with a certificate issued by the A.S.L. (Local Health Authority).

The following statements are NOT true:

- using seat belts allows children to be carried in the front seats on an adult's lap without danger

- the seat belt retractor may be modified or disabled if it is uncomfortable

- obese persons may use special devices that prevent the seat belt from fitting tightly against the body

- the warning light indicating that the seat belts are not fastened can be disabled by the driver using a dedicated control on the dashboard.

953.description_en:
A helmet is intended to prevent the head from striking hard objects directly, limiting injuries in an accident; however, it is not capable of fully absorbing violent impacts.

A full-face helmet also protects the face from trauma and injuries.

It is advisable for the helmet to have a visor, which protects the face and eyes from impacts with insects, but it must ensure perfect visibility in any light or lighting conditions; the visor must be replaced if scratched or damaged. The helmet's ventilation system helps limit the risk of the visor fogging up.

It must be of an approved type and the right size for the person.

It may only be used if intact and must be properly fastened so that it is not lost in a collision. Wearing it incorrectly or without fastening it correctly can cause serious health risks in the event of a fall or accident.

The helmet undergoes an ageing process due to light and heat.

It must be cleaned with non-corrosive detergents, not with solvents that could compromise the strength of the outer shell.

The helmet must be replaced after suffering a strong impact, even if no deformation is visible on the outer shell.

Stickers of any kind are not permitted.

Wearing a helmet is compulsory for the drivers of two-wheeled mopeds of any age, and for all drivers and passengers of motorcycles.

It is not compulsory for drivers of enclosed-body motor tricycles (motocarri) or of motorcycles fitted with a suitable safety cell.

It must also be worn on motor quadricycles without a bodywork (quads).

The helmet must be worn even for short trips and at low speeds.

A driver who does not wear a helmet is subject to a deduction of points from the driving licence.

954.description_en:
Motorcycle boots provide adequate protection for the feet and ankles when riding a two-wheeled vehicle.

They:

- reduce the effects of sprains in the event of an imprecise foot placement

- protect the ankle joints from the cold

- protect the feet from abrasion on the asphalt in the event of a fall

They have no loose straps or laces, to prevent them from catching on the motorcycle's footrests, and they are designed so that they do not come off in a fall.

Motorcycle boots are approved to international standards.

The following statements are NOT true:

- they can be replaced by trekking shoes for high-altitude mountaineering

- they cover the leg up above the knee

- they are made of flame-retardant rubber

- they have a steel sole.

955.description_en:
When riding mopeds or motorcycles, it is advisable to wear protective gloves for the hands, regardless of the season:

- they protect in particular the back of the hand in case of impact with hard objects

- they protect the palm of the hand in the event of a fall with sliding along the asphalt

- they ensure the right sensitivity during riding and a more secure grip on the controls

They may have different padding depending on the season.

They have special fastening systems to prevent them from slipping off in a fall.

The following statements are NOT true:

- without gloves you can operate the controls more quickly

- they can be replaced by ski gloves

- they also cover the elbow.

956.description_en:
They provide adequate abrasion protection if you slide on asphalt, because they have rigid protective inserts at the joints.

Type-approved motorcycle clothing is tested for cut resistance and impact abrasion.

It is not true that:
- they are not intended for summer use
- they must be black to be approved
- they are tested for resistance and washing

1000.description_en:
It is forbidden to use a motor vehicle on public roads when:

- the vehicle is not covered by third-party liability insurance

- you do not hold the driving licence required for that type of vehicle

- it is not registered

It is not true that it is forbidden to use a motor vehicle on public roads if you do not have the proof of payment receipt, if it has a trial plate, if the vehicle registration document is in the name of a person other than the driver, or if you do not have the certificate of ownership.



Driving a vehicle by a person who has not obtained the corresponding licence is considered a criminal offence



In order to circulate, a motor vehicle must be equipped with:

- number plates

- the vehicle registration document (carta di circolazione)

- the insurance certificate and corresponding sticker, certifying payment of the insurance coverage

- the mobile warning triangle (segnale mobile di pericolo)



Vehicle number plates must be firmly affixed in the correct position. They must always be legible and not dirty. They must not be counterfeit or tampered with. They must not be bent.

Motor vehicles used for driving lessons must be fitted, both at the front and at the rear, with special retroreflective panels bearing the letter 'P' (principiante, meaning learner)

1003.description_en:
Driving licences of categories AM, A1, A2, A, B1, B, BE and BS are valid:
- for ten years if issued or renewed for people under 50
- for 5 years for people aged 50 to 70
- for 3 years for people aged 70 to 80
- for 2 years for people over 80

In no case may you continue to drive a vehicle with an expired driving licence.

The Ministry of Infrastructure and Transport renews the driving licence after a psychophysical fitness assessment carried out by an authorised doctor.

That is, the assessment verifies that the holder still meets the required physical and mental requirements.

1004.title_en: Immediate seizure of the driving licence
1004.description_en:
Police officers order an immediate seizure when they find minor irregularities, for example:
- when it is established that the driver is driving with an expired driving licence
- when driving while intoxicated (this also leads to suspension)
- when the driver fails to give way to rail vehicles or other vehicles that have the right-of-way
- when the driver does not properly secure an improperly loaded load after being instructed by the police (this also leads to suspension)
- when an accident causes injuries to people (this also leads to suspension)
- when the driver, required to take a periodic technical inspection, does not undergo it within the prescribed time limits

It is not true that the licence is seized immediately when:
- the driver travels in Italy with a licence issued by a foreign state in which they are resident
- the driver carries an intoxicated passenger
- the vehicle is driven on tyres of different sizes from those listed on the vehicle registration document
- the driver commits any offence that results in a deduction of points from the licence
- the driver drives without carrying the vehicle registration document or the certificate of ownership

1005.description_en:
The Prefect, the Motor Vehicle Registry (Motorizzazione Civile) and the judicial authority order a suspension of the driving licence. It prohibits the driver from driving vehicles for a set period.

Suspension is an additional penalty that results from breaking certain articles of the Highway Code. Sometimes it applies not after the first offence, but when the driver repeats the same offence twice within 2 years.

For example:
- when a novice driver drives without respecting the restrictions on vehicles and speeds
- when speed exceeds the maximum limit by more than 40 km/h
- when a vehicle uses the emergency lane on a motorway in cases not permitted by the Highway Code
- when the driver drives under the influence of narcotic substances or while intoxicated by alcohol
- when the driver refuses to undergo tests for possible alcohol intoxication
- when the driver flees without giving aid to a person they have hit
- when the driver illegally drives a vehicle under seizure
- if the documents relating to the vehicle's insurance are falsified or forged
- in case of a temporary loss of physical or mental fitness
- if the holder drives with a licence category different from the one required for the vehicle driven

It is not true that suspension is ordered:
- when the driver drives with a suspended licence
- when the holder permanently loses physical fitness
- when doubts arise about whether the required requirements still apply
- together with notice that the points have been reset to zero
- when driving without carrying the driving licence
- when driving with an illegible or damaged licence
- when, at the request of officers, the driver cannot show the portable hazard warning triangle
- when the holder no longer meets the moral requirements
- when a vehicle is parked in spaces reserved for disabled people
- when the road tax for the car is not paid within the deadline

1006.description_en:
The Prefect and the Motor Vehicle Registry (Motorizzazione Civile) order a driving licence review.

The review may require the driver to undergo a medical examination and/or a technical fitness test. These check whether the driver still meets the physical and mental requirements (eyesight, hearing, reflexes) and the technical skills, meaning knowledge of road signs and the ability to drive correctly, needed to keep the licence.

A failed medical examination or fitness test results in the permanent revocation of the driving licence.

If the driver temporarily lacks the required psychophysical fitness, the licence is suspended until the requirements are regained.

A review may be ordered:
- after a serious accident that caused injuries to people
- following driving while intoxicated or under the influence of narcotic substances
- following a reset of the licence's points to zero

1007.description_en:
Revocation is ordered by the Prefect, the Motorizzazione Civile (motor vehicle authority), or a judge. It consists of the permanent cancellation of the driving licence.

Revocation is ordered:

- if the driver drives while a licence suspension is in force

- when the driver, on a motorway, reverses direction or drives on the carriageway against the flow of traffic

- for permanent loss of physical or mental fitness

- when the holder no longer meets the moral requirements

- when the licence is replaced by one issued by a foreign state

- when the holder, subject to a re-examination, is found no longer fit


Revocation is NOT ordered:

- when the driver drives with a licence that has expired

- when the driver does not carry the licence with them

- when the driver drives without prescribed corrective lenses

1009.description_en:
The points licence system gives every driving licence an initial allocation of 20 points.

If a driver breaks certain rules of the Highway Code (note: not all of them), points are deducted from the licence.

The number of points deducted is set by law and depends on how serious the offence is.

When a driver has used up all their points, they must undergo a re-examination of their licence.

To recover points, it is enough to attend a specific course at a driving school.

Attending the course allows a holder of a category A or B licence to recover 6 points, up to a maximum of 20 points.

Drivers with at least 20 points who commit no offences involving point loss are entitled, after two years, to 2 'bonus' points (3 if they are considered newly qualified).

Drivers with fewer than 20 points return to the full initial total of 20 two years after their last offence.

With bonuses, a driver can reach a maximum of 30 points in total.

Newly qualified drivers (category B licence held for no more than three years) have twice the usual number of points deducted.

If several violations involving point loss are committed at the same time, a maximum of 15 points can be deducted, unless one of the violations results in licence suspension.



Points are lost, for example:

- when speed limits are exceeded by more than 10 km/h

- for failing to comply with certain rules on overtaking

- for using a mobile phone without a hands-free earpiece or speaker

- when riding without a helmet where one is required, or with a helmet that is not properly fastened

- for failing to keep a safe following distance, where this leads to an accident

- for not using lights, or using them improperly, while driving
