- for carrying an overloaded vehicle or too many passengers while driving

- for not wearing prescribed corrective lenses while driving

- when racing on public roads

- when driving on the emergency lane of a motorway outside the permitted cases

- when driving under the influence of narcotic substances



Points are NOT lost:

- when racing on private tracks

- for leaving a vehicle parked in front of a driveway access

- when driving without carrying the licence, the vehicle registration document (carta di circolazione) or the certificate of ownership

1010.description_en:
The AM licence allows you to drive:

- two-wheeled mopeds (L1e) with a maximum speed of 45 km/h and a maximum engine capacity of 50 cm3 (combustion engine) or power of 4 kW (electric motor)

- three-wheeled mopeds (L2e) with a maximum speed of 45 km/h and an engine capacity of 50 cm3 or power of 4 kW

- light quadricycles (L6e) with an unladen mass of 350 kg or less, a maximum speed of 45 km/h, and an engine capacity of 50 cm3 or power not exceeding 6 kW

To obtain an AM licence, you must be 14 years old. Until age 16, you may not drive outside Italy, in any European Union country.

Carrying passengers is allowed only from age 18, and only if the vehicle's registration document (carta di circolazione) permits it.

1011.description_en:
The A1 licence allows you to drive:

- light motorcycles with an engine capacity not exceeding 125 cm3, power not exceeding 11 kW, and a power-to-weight ratio not exceeding 0.1 kW/kg

- motor tricycles with power not exceeding 15 kW

- quadricycles: for carrying people, with an unladen mass up to 400 kg (for carrying goods, up to 550 kg), and power up to 15 kW

- agricultural machines that do not exceed the mass and size limits of motorcycles, with a maximum speed of 40 km/h, provided they carry no one other than the driver

To obtain an A1 licence, you must be 16 years old.

The A1 licence also allows you to drive the vehicles that can be driven with an AM licence.

It allows one passenger to be carried, but only if the driver is at least 16 years old and the vehicle's registration document (carta di circolazione) states that passengers may be carried.

1012.description_en:
The A2 licence allows you to drive:

- motorcycles with power not exceeding 35 kW and a maximum power-to-weight ratio of 0.2 kW/kg, provided they are not derived from a version of the same model that develops more than twice that maximum power

- agricultural machines that do not exceed the mass and size limits of motorcycles, with a maximum speed of 40 km/h, provided they carry no one other than the driver

- motor tricycles and quadricycles (quadricycles for carrying goods with an unladen mass up to 550 kg and power up to 15 kW) with an engine capacity above 50 cm3 and a speed above 45 km/h

To ride motorcycles of any power, a holder of an A2 licence must pass a new practical exam on a 600 cm3 motorcycle with power above 40 kW, after at least two years from obtaining the A2 licence.

To obtain an A2 licence, you must be 18 years old.

The A2 licence also allows you to drive the vehicles that can be driven with A1 and AM licences.

A holder of an A2 licence for at least two years can obtain an A licence, which allows driving all motorcycles, even if they are under 24 years old.

It allows one passenger to be carried, if the vehicle's registration document (carta di circolazione) states that passengers may be carried.

1013.title_en: Category A license, also called A without limits or A3
1013.description_en:
The A license without limits (A3) allows you to drive:

- motorcycles of any type (with or without a sidecar)

- agricultural machinery that does not exceed the mass and size limits of motor vehicles, with a maximum speed of 40 km/h, provided it carries no passengers other than the driver

- light motor tricycles and quadricycles. Tricycles with power above 15 kW may also be driven, but only if the driver is at least 21 years old

The category A license also allows you to drive the vehicles that can be driven with the A1, A2 and AM licenses.

You may obtain the A license through direct access if you have reached your twenty-fourth year of age.

The minimum age may drop to 20 if you have held an A2 license for at least 2 years (gradual access).

It allows you to carry one passenger if the vehicle's registration document (carta di circolazione) states that this is permitted.

1014.description_en:
The category B1 license allows you to drive non-light quadricycles with an unladen mass not exceeding 400 kilograms (550 kilograms for vehicles intended for goods transport), excluding the mass of batteries for electric vehicles, and with a maximum power not exceeding 15 kW.

It allows you to drive non-light quadricycles with handlebar steering (quads).

You may obtain the B1 license at age 16.

You may carry one passenger only if the driver is at least 18 years old and the vehicle's registration document (carta di circolazione) permits it.

The license must be renewed every 10 years. The renewal period is 5 years for holders aged 50 to 70, and 3 years for holders over 70.

1015.description_en:
Allows you to drive:

- motor vehicles (tricycles, quadricycles and motorcycles, the latter only up to 125 cm3 and 11 kW, and only in Italy).

- motor vehicles for transporting people and goods (including trucks and motorhomes) carrying no more than eight people besides the driver, with a maximum laden mass of up to 3.5 tonnes, also towing a light trailer (up to 750 kg). Non-light trailers may also be towed, provided the entire combination does not exceed 3.5 tonnes.

- emergency service vehicles with a maximum laden mass of up to 3.5 tonnes

- agricultural machinery, including exceptional machinery

- non-exceptional work machinery that must not exceed 3.5 tonnes.

It also allows you to drive the vehicles that can be driven with the AM and B1 licenses.

It allows you to drive, but only within national territory (Italy), the vehicles that can be driven with the A1 license.

You may obtain the B license at age 18.

The category B license carries speed and driving restrictions for the first three years from the date you pass the exam (limits of 100 km/h on motorways and 90 km/h on main extra-urban roads, and double the points deduction).

The license is valid for 10 years for holders under 50, 5 years for holders aged 50 to 70, and 3 years for holders over 70.

It is renewed by the Motorizzazione Civile (motor vehicle registry office), provided the holder still meets the required physical and mental fitness criteria.

1016.title_en: Category B license with harmonized code 96
1016.description_en:
The category B license with harmonized code 96 allows you to drive cars towing a non-light trailer (over 750 kilograms), provided the maximum authorized mass of the combination does not exceed 4,250 kilograms.

It may be obtained either at the same time as the category B license or after it, in both cases by passing a driving test on a specific vehicle.

1017.description_en:
The category BE license allows you to drive vehicle combinations made up of a car with a maximum authorized mass of up to 3,500 kilograms and a trailer with a mass of up to 3,500 kilograms, even if the mass of the vehicle combination exceeds 4,250 kilograms (a limitation of the category B license with harmonized code 96).

It therefore also allows you to drive the vehicles that can be driven with the AM, B1, B and B harmonized code 96 licenses.

1050.title_en: Probable causes of accidents due to road structure
1050.description_en:
- narrowness of the road

- failure to signpost junctions

- lack of road markings

- deformed or slippery road surface

- presence of unsignposted bottlenecks

1051.title_en: When it is raining, you must
1051.description_en:
- reduce speed and increase the safety distance from the vehicle ahead

- steer carefully and avoid braking suddenly or with excessive force

- prevent the windows from fogging up and keep the windscreen wipers running

- if the rain is heavy, switch on the dipped headlights.

1052.title_en: On roads covered with snow, you must
1052.description_en:
- moderate your speed

- increase the safety distance

- avoid abrupt manoeuvres, acceleration and braking

1053.title_en: When there are icy stretches of road, it is advisable to
1053.description_en:
- keep away from the path of oncoming vehicles

- when going downhill, use low gears

- increase the safety distance

- proceed at a moderate speed

- avoid abrupt manoeuvres, acceleration and braking

- take extra care when driving through shaded areas

- if your vehicle has it, engage four-wheel drive

It is not true that you must use studded tyres rather than snow chains on the front tyres.

Grip on an icy road is lower than on a snow-covered road.

1054.title_en: In dense fog, it is advisable to
1054.description_en:
- proceed at a speed suited to the visibility, with the utmost caution and concentration

- stop, if necessary, outside the carriageway

- if you are forced to stop on the carriageway, use the hazard warning lights (four flashing indicators)

- switch on the fog lights (front and rear) or, if you do not have them, the dipped headlights

It is not true that you must have the turn indicators or position lights on, nor sound the horn continuously, nor unfasten your seat belt.

1055.title_en: In case of getting stuck in snow or sand
1055.description_en:
- if you cannot move off in first gear, it is advisable to engage a higher gear

- if you cannot move the vehicle, it is advisable to place something that provides grip under the wheel that is spinning

1056.description_en:
A phenomenon in which the wheels lift off or slide on wet road surfaces, causing the tyres to lose grip.

The vehicle floats on the water because the tread grooves do not drain the water sufficiently.

It depends on the thickness and pattern of the tread.

It is more likely to occur:

- with light vehicles;

- at high speeds;

- with heavily worn tyres, in which case also at low speeds.

It is not true that it increases on carriageways with a steep lateral slope.

1057.title_en: The driver involved in a road accident
1057.description_en:
- must stop and provide assistance to any injured persons

- must provide their personal details and the details of their driving licence, the vehicle's registration plate and insurance to the persons who were damaged

- must avoid allowing the traces to be altered, if it is necessary to reconstruct how the accident happened

- may use the pre-printed forms provided by their insurance company to report the accident to the insurer

1059.title_en: When a passenger needs to get in or out
1059.description_en:
- it is advisable to do so from the sidewalk side or, if there is none, from the side away from traffic

- open the door only when this does not endanger other road users

- have the passenger wait until the vehicle has come to a complete stop

- if it is a child, it is advisable for an adult to supervise

- pay particular attention to two-wheeled motor vehicles, as they are less visible

1060.description_en:
- due to high speed

- when the safe following distance is not respected

- due to driver inattention

1062.description_en: Located inside a tunnel, this sign indicates the presence of an escape route. It does not mean that you must turn back to the tunnel entrance.

1063.description_en: Located inside a tunnel, this sign indicates the presence of a fire extinguisher.

1065.title_en: Various safety guidelines for two-wheeled vehicles
1065.description_en:
Drivers of motor vehicles must, in general, pay particular attention to two-wheeled motor vehicles, as they are less easily visible due to their small profile.

While on the road, to make themselves more visible, motorcycles must keep their dipped headlights on even during the day.

When crossing intersections, always consider the possibility that a two-wheeled motor vehicle that has passed the stationary vehicles may approach without being visible from a distance.

In heavy traffic with queuing vehicles, before opening the doors to get out of your parked vehicle, always consider the possibility that a two-wheeled motor vehicle may be passing the stationary vehicles in the queue on the right.

When overtaking a two-wheeled motor vehicle, especially at high speed, maintain a good lateral safety distance.

It is not true that motorcyclists may use the horn in all cases when approaching intersections.

Motorcyclists' clothing affects their visibility in traffic, but it is not true that at night they are required to ride wearing a yellow reflective vest.

Tram rails, painted pedestrian crossings on the carriageway and manholes are road features that can be dangerous for two-wheeled vehicles when the road surface is wet.

Riding at speed over manholes or tram rails on a two-wheeled vehicle can cause loss of grip and steering control, leading to skidding or falls.

It is not true that, if you must ride a two-wheeled vehicle on a carriageway shared by vehicles and trams, it is advisable, where possible, to ride with both wheels in the groove of the tram rail.

1100.description_en:
Fitness to drive can be compromised if:

- you take certain sedative or antidepressant medications

- you use drugs: hallucinogens (LSD, ecstasy, etc.), amphetamines, hashish, marijuana, cocaine, heroin

- you consume alcoholic beverages

Alcohol can cause a state of euphoria, leading to underestimation of danger, longer reaction times (slowing reflexes) and drowsiness, and can also dangerously impair concentration and attention.

Anyone driving under the influence of alcohol (blood alcohol concentration above the legal limit) risks arrest.

It is necessary to wait several hours for a driver who has consumed an excessive amount of alcoholic beverages to recover fitness to drive, especially if they have also taken medication.

It is inadvisable to drive when your emotional state is disturbed.

If the driver shows signs of tiredness, it is advisable to reduce speed, reach the nearest rest/parking bay and rest; it is not true that you should move closer to the vehicle ahead.

Eating heavy, excessive or hard-to-digest food can cause reduced attention and longer reaction times, so it is not recommended for anyone who must drive.

1101.description_en:
Helping an injured person in a road accident is both a legal and a moral duty; it can save their life or prevent further physical harm.

The aim of first aid is to assist and, where possible, keep the injured person alive with simple, immediate measures while waiting for more appropriate help, without taking on actions that require specific medical expertise.

In addition, as far as possible, you must avoid the injured person suffering further harm and avoid incorrect or harmful interventions by others.

You must immediately report the accident and call qualified emergency services.

1102.description_en:
If the victim has a bleeding wound:

- if possible, place the injured person in a seated or lying position while waiting for the emergency services

- cover/dab the wound with sterile or, as far as possible, clean material, applying pressure to stop the bleeding

- wash the wound with water only if it is dirty with soil, to avoid a possible infection

- avoid any manipulation of the injury

- do not remove any foreign objects embedded in the wound, because removing them could worsen the bleeding; take great care not to push them deeper into the wound while bandaging

1103.description_en:
If the victim has a foreign body in an eye (a shard of glass, wood or other material), cover the eye with a bandage without carrying out any other procedure (do not remove the object).

Then prevent the victim from touching the injured eye, and do not massage the eyelid to avoid more serious injury.

Wait for a specialist to intervene.

It is not true that the victim must be forced to keep their eyes open.

1104.description_en:
A state of shock (very similar to a faint) is caused by a drop in blood pressure that reduces the blood flow, with serious damage to the brain and heart.

It can be caused by: severe physical pain, serious trauma, strong emotions, heavy blood loss.

It can manifest through several symptoms: shivering, very pale skin, cold sweat on the forehead, a faster heartbeat, sudden utterance of meaningless phrases and words.

The injured person in a state of shock must be laid on the ground and covered to prevent heat loss.

If possible, keep the legs raised (by about 20-30 cm) relative to the body, to promote blood flow to the heart and brain.

1105.description_en:
If a road casualty is in a state of unconsciousness:

- they do not react to simple stimuli

- they are unable to perform movements

- they are unable to answer a question

Since they are not able to look after themselves, you must keep watch over their condition and take care of them until medical personnel arrive.

Move them only if you are certain they have no spinal injuries.

Check whether they are still breathing by placing your hand on the lower side of the chest or on the abdomen:

- if they are breathing with difficulty, clear the nose and mouth of any obstructions

- if they are breathing spontaneously, place them in the 'recovery position' with great care (lying on one side with the head tilted back to promote good breathing, one leg bent, one arm bent so as to support the head, mouth open and facing the ground to allow fluids to drain out).

1106.description_en:
It may cause fractures of the ribs or sternum, complicated by possible lung injuries.

The injured person is breathing with great difficulty, so you should:

- try to ease their breathing by placing them in a semi-seated position

- forbid them to drink or eat, and assist them until medical help arrives

If there is a visible and deep wound, apply firm pressure at once with a clean cloth, without cleaning, disinfecting or dressing the wound.

1107.description_en:
A fracture is the break of a bone. If the bone protrudes through the skin, the fracture is called 'open' (exposed).

The main signs of a fracture are very severe pain, even with the slightest movement of the limb, and swelling and/or deformity of the injured area.

The fracture must be immobilized in the position in which it is found, to avoid damage to nerves and vessels and to minimize severe pain, which can lead to shock.

Immediately afterwards, if necessary, apply the normal anti-shock measures.

In case of an open fracture, where the bone protrudes through the skin, do not push the bone in an attempt to make it go back in. Instead, before immobilizing the limb, cover the wound and the bone with sterile material or a clean cloth to prevent infection.

Always wait for the emergency services.

It is not true that the victim must be asked to move their limbs or walk in order to reduce the pain.

1108.description_en:
If an injured person has burns:

- if flames are still present, put them out by smothering them, for example with a blanket

- avoid removing clothing that remains stuck to the burned skin

- immerse the limbs in cold water to relieve the pain

- it is advisable to cover the burns with clean material, preferably sterile

- do not disinfect the burned parts or apply ointments or alcohol to them

1109.description_en: While driving, you must wear eyeglasses or contact lenses if this requirement is stated on your licence, either in full or in the form of a code (harmonized code '01').

1150.description_en: Anyone who drives a vehicle is subject to liability for their driving conduct: civil, criminal and administrative.

1151.description_en:
Civil liability arising from a road accident is based on the principle that any damage caused must be compensated. It consists of the obligation to reimburse the damage caused to people, property and animals as a result of the accident.

It obliges the person responsible, or whoever acts on their behalf (the insurance company), to compensate the damage caused, by paying money.

It falls on the driver and the owner of the vehicle.

It does not fall on the owner if they prove that the vehicle was used against their will, for example in case of theft.

It is independent of criminal and administrative liability.

It is not true that it is excluded in case of the death of the injured party, that it is aggravated by lack of insurance coverage, or that it in some way falls on the insurance company.

A person who is civilly obliged to compensate the damage caused by a road accident:

- is released from the obligation if they compensate the damage. They may therefore agree with the injured party on the amount of compensation without involving the insurance company

- may have their own vehicle repaired

- may be assisted by a road accident consultant

- is not required to call the police if there is no injury to people

It is not true that they can request revocation of their licence as an alternative, or that they are freed from all forms of criminal liability by paying a sum of money.

1152.description_en:
Criminal liability arising from a road accident is personal, so it falls only on the driver. It arises:

- if provisions of the Criminal Code are violated

- if the accident causes serious injuries to persons

- in cases of manslaughter (involuntary homicide)

It is not true that it arises for the owner of the vehicle if the driver has not been identified.

Criminal liability is excluded:

- when the act is not considered a crime

- when the act is due to force majeure

- when there is only involuntary damage to property

It is not true that it is excluded when damages have been compensated or when assistance has been given to the victim.

Whoever is criminally and civilly liable for a road accident:

- is subject to the penalties set out in the Criminal Code

- is required to compensate the damages

- if they have violated the Highway Code, is also subject to administrative liability and the related sanctions

- may face suspension, revocation or review of the driving licence

It is not true that they are always subject to precautionary arrest and cannot continue to drive vehicles of the same category.

1154.description_en:
Direct compensation for road accidents applies if the vehicle is damaged and the driver suffers minor injuries.

The direct compensation procedure does not apply if more than two vehicles are involved.

It is not true that direct compensation is excluded if a motorcycle is involved, or that in the case of an accident with vehicle damage, the claim must mandatorily be accompanied by photographs.

1155.description_en:
The law makes insurance for motor vehicles compulsory for civil liability toward third parties (borne by both the driver and the owner) when driving on public roads.

The insurance covers:

- risks arising from the circulation of motor vehicles, even when they are not driven by the owner.

- damage suffered by persons and/or property located in public areas or areas open to the public.

- damage suffered by third parties carried in the vehicle, if the vehicle is authorized to carry passengers.

- monetary damage only up to the maximum amount (massimale) set by the insurance policy.

It is forbidden to use a vehicle without insurance coverage on public roads.

When the R.C.A. (motor vehicle civil liability) insurance has expired:

- a penalty is incurred if the vehicle is driven or left parked on public roads

- the vehicle may be confiscated

It is not true that the vehicle may be left parked on public roads, that it may only be used within Italian territory, or that the vehicle must undergo a technical test before being returned to circulation.

It is also valid for accidents occurring in European Union countries.

After signing the R.C.A. (motor vehicle civil liability) insurance contract, the insurer must issue the customer a insurance certificate, which must always be kept on board the vehicle. It is not true that it must issue a list of partner body shops, a first-aid booklet, or a manual on how to avoid accidents.

Every year the insurer must issue its customer a risk certificate (attestato di rischio).

When the annual premium is paid, the insurer must issue the customer an insurance certificate.

The maximum amounts (massimali) of the R.C.A. policy are the highest sums the insurer agrees to pay in the event of an accident.

The minimum amount of the R.C.A. (motor vehicle civil liability) policy limits is set by law, and the customer may increase them by paying a higher sum of money (insurance premium). It is not true that they increase every year.

A contract with the 'bonus malus' formula involves an annual change in the insurance premium, based on the number of accidents caused.

It is not true that the contract is set by a judge, that it does not apply to motorcycles, or that it is cancelled if more than two accidents are caused.

1157.title_en: Policies covering theft, fire, vandalism and natural events
1157.description_en:
Insurance policies taken out to cover damage from theft, fire, vandalism, natural events, or damage to one's own vehicle (kasko policy) are not mandatory.

Insurance policies against the risk of vehicle fire cover only damage caused by accidental (chance) fires.

In an insurance policy against the risk of theft or fire, the compensation due cannot exceed the value the vehicle had at the moment it was stolen or caught fire.

If the vehicle is stolen in a foreign state, the insurance can be activated only by filing the report again in Italy.

It is not true that to take out an insurance policy against the risk of fire, the vehicle must be fitted with an automatic battery disconnect switch.

It is not true that to take out an insurance policy against the risk of theft, the vehicle must be fitted with an anti-theft device.

It is not true that they guarantee forms of life annuity.

1200.description_en:
To reduce fuel consumption, reduce driving speed and keep it as constant as possible, and reduce the number and intensity of accelerations and braking.

Whenever possible, choose flat and smoother roads, reduce unnecessary loads, and keep the windows closed (especially when travelling at medium to high speeds, because turbulence inside the cabin can slow the vehicle).

Keep in mind that the following increase fuel consumption:

- the weight of the vehicle

- luggage placed on the roof (it is therefore better to store luggage inside the vehicle rather than on the roof rack)

- use of the air conditioning

- appliances and devices that run on electricity (radio, lights, rear-window defroster, etc.)

- insufficient tyre inflation pressure.

It is not true that hybrid vehicles (combustion engine plus electric motor) pollute more because they are powered by two engines.

1201.description_en:
Noise increases if audible warning devices (horn, horns) are used excessively.

To avoid annoying noise while driving, i.e. to reduce the noise emitted by vehicles:

- have the silencer (exhaust muffler) checked to make sure it is in good working order and of an approved type

- do not brake harshly unless strictly necessary

- check and, if necessary, replace the brakes if they make noise when braking; brake checks also increase safety

- do not rev the engine unnecessarily and repeatedly while the vehicle is stationary

- avoid keeping a low gear engaged for longer than necessary

- use the horn only for road safety reasons (transporting injured or sick people, immediate danger)

- do not slam the car doors

It is not true that the horn must be replaced with flashing lights (neither by day nor by night).

The noise produced by motor vehicles increases as the silencer deteriorates, and it is not true that noise is caused only by the engine.

When cornering at high speed, tyre scrubbing increases the noise of the vehicle.

Empty trailers that bounce excessively can be a cause of noise.

1202.description_en:
Air pollution caused by vehicles is due mostly to exhaust gases generated by combustion inside the engine. It:

- can cause damage to the respiratory tract and eye irritation.

- increases smog, acid rain and the greenhouse effect

Air pollution can be reduced:

- by adopting a driving style that limits fuel consumption

- by replacing the catalytic converter when it is deteriorated or worn out

- by periodically replacing the air filter

- by checking that the vehicle is always in optimal condition for consumption and performance

- by checking that the air filter is not dirty or clogged

- by using the air conditioner as little as possible, only when needed

- by reducing the weight of the vehicle

- by choosing vehicles powered by electricity, methane or LPG

- by avoiding using the vehicle for short trips

- by turning off the engine during a prolonged stop

It is not true that to reduce pollution it is necessary to check the clutch, differential and suspension, reduce tyre inflation pressure, rev the engine from standstill to keep it warm, or leave the air conditioner running.



Air pollution is greater if:

- the injectors are faulty

- the exhaust smoke is dark in colour

It may be due to irregular engine operation: greater exhaust smoke emission is a sign of greater pollution caused by the engine.

It is not true that pollution is lower right after starting, when the temperature is still low.



Driving a vehicle that emits excessive polluting exhaust gases may result in an administrative fine and the withdrawal of the vehicle registration document (carta di circolazione).

Driving a vehicle whose engine and silencer have been modified may result in heavy administrative fines.



It is not true that, during a prolonged stop in a tunnel caused by a queue of vehicles, activating air recirculation inside the vehicle is harmful to health.

It is not true that air pollution is zero for vehicles that comply with the 'Euro 0' anti-pollution standard.

It is not true that vehicles complying with the 'Euro 4' anti-pollution standard emit a greater quantity of polluting gases than vehicles type-approved under the 'Euro 0' standard.

1204.description_en:
- it is forbidden to discharge antifreeze into the sewer, as it may not be biodegradable

- abandoning a car battery on the road or on the ground can cause serious damage to the environment and to the underlying aquifers; when you buy a battery, the spent battery can be handed to your dealer, who will collect it without any additional cost

- the owner of a vehicle who intends to demolish or scrap it must deliver it to a collection centre for safe disposal (authorised scrapyard)

- when disposing of engine oil, avoid prolonged contact with the skin

- the discharge of organic residues and dirty water from motorhomes must take place at the appropriate sanitary disposal facilities

- abandoning hazardous or toxic waste (oils, liquids, residues from repairs or replacements) on the ground is penalised

- it is forbidden to damage road structures and installations

- it is forbidden to throw objects and waste from moving vehicles

- it is forbidden to dirty the carriageway by leaving waste on it

- it is forbidden to enter roads with vehicle wheels dirty with mud

1250.description_en:
- allows the vehicle to move, making it possible to follow the intended path

- depends on the type of road surface

- opposes sliding towards the outside and the inside of a bend

- opposes sliding of the tyre on the asphalt

- opposes sliding caused by crosswind

- increases if the asphalt is rough

- decreases if the asphalt is wet, covered with leaves, mud, ice or oil-soiled

- is greatest on dry and clean asphalt

- decreases on rails, especially in rain

- decreases on road markings (painted road lines) in rain

1251.description_en:
- if it decreases, the driven wheels may spin

- if it decreases, the braking distance increases

- if it is low, speed must be reduced, for example to take a bend safely (with a low coefficient of adhesion, skidding in bends increases)

- if it decreases, the braking distance increases and sudden braking becomes dangerous

1252.title_en: When the vehicle goes around a bend
1252.description_en:
- It is subject to a force that tends to push it outward

- Excessive speed can cause it to skid or overturn

1253.description_en:
- It is more likely when the load is placed high up or is not securely fixed

- It is more likely when the distance between wheels on the same axle is short (narrow carriageway)

- It is more likely when the road has a tight radius of curvature (sharp bend)

The overturning force also increases as speed increases.

1255.description_en:
- It must be adjusted to the vehicle's load conditions (cargo and number of passengers)

- It must be checked periodically, including on spare tyres

- It must be checked when the tyres are cold (before setting the vehicle in motion)

- If it is too low, it increases friction and fuel consumption

An automatic tyre pressure monitoring system increases vehicle safety.

It is not true that the pressure must be the same for a towing vehicle and its trailer.

1256.description_en:
The minimum tread depth of a car's tyres must be 1.6 millimeters.

It is advisable to replace tyres after a few years, even if they are not worn.

Tubeless tyres, when punctured, deflate slowly (unlike tyres with an inner tube), and it is possible to keep driving with due caution, stopping as soon as possible.

It is not true that they can only be repaired with special sealant cans that seal the hole from the inside.

It is not true that tyres inflated with nitrogen must be kept at a lower pressure than those inflated with air.

Studded tyres may only be used during a certain period of the year, and it is advisable to fit them on all wheels.

It is advisable to fit winter tyres on all wheels.

It is not true that vehicles fitted with winter tyres must observe lower speed limits than ordinary ones.

Anyone using non-approved snow chains is liable to the same penalty as if they had none.

Using chains on stretches without snow damages the suspension components.

It is not true that on four-wheel-drive (4x4) vehicles the chains must be fitted to the rear wheels.

For greater safety:

- Use only tyres of the sizes specified in the vehicle's type approval

- Fit identical tyres on the wheels of the same axle

- Check the condition of the tyres on the sidewalls as well, to prevent sudden blowouts or deflation

To ensure grip and vehicle stability, check that the tyre inflation pressure is the one recommended by the manufacturer.

Too low an inflation pressure causes abnormal wear on the edges of the tyre (not the center).

It is not true that reducing the inflation pressure improves tyre cooling.

It is possible to swap the front tyres with the rear tyres, since the front ones are more subject to wear.

1257.description_en:
It is best to park the vehicle on level, stable ground.

Before proceeding, engage the parking brake and select first gear or reverse. Then have any passengers get out and stand outside the carriageway.

Before lifting the vehicle, it is advisable to slightly loosen the wheel bolts.

After replacing the wheel, tighten the bolts slightly with the vehicle raised, and tighten them fully once the vehicle is lowered.

The jack must not be placed just anywhere. It must be positioned at the point indicated for that specific vehicle.

On vehicles fitted with a temporary spare wheel, speeds above 80 km/h must not be exceeded. Passengers may still be carried.

1258.description_en:
Braking systems of light vehicles are often fitted with a brake servo. The vacuum brake servo cannot work with the engine off.

The braking effect from the engine is at its maximum when first gear is engaged.

Prolonged and repeated use of the brakes overheats them and reduces braking efficiency. When driving down long, steep descents, engage a low gear to avoid overheating the brakes. It is not true that excessive grip causes the brakes to overheat.

After washing the vehicle, it is advisable to carry out a brake test.

The parking brake must be used to hold the vehicle when parked or in an emergency. It should not be used while driving, or to brake or bring the vehicle to a halt. Not all vehicles have a manually operated parking brake. It must be able to hold the parked vehicle even on slopes.

In braking systems, the kinetic energy of the car is converted into heat through friction. The parts of the braking system most stressed by high temperatures are the friction linings.

It is not true that in an emergency stop the driver must engage reverse gear or press the brake and clutch at the same time.

Replacing brake pads is not routine maintenance and cannot be done by just anyone.

The brake hydraulic fluid level must be checked periodically.

It is not true that the braking circuit of light vehicles is a sealed circuit, so periodic checks of the hydraulic fluid level are unnecessary.

Inefficient or unbalanced braking can be caused by:

- air or vapour in the hydraulic braking circuit
- excessive wear of the brake linings
- irregular wear of the drums or discs
- different tyre inflation pressures on the same axle
- excessive heating of the brake linings
- excessive or poorly distributed load
- excessive and repeated braking

With unbalanced brakes, tread wear is generally irregular and uneven, and during braking the vehicle may swerve toward the side of the wheel that locks first.

1259.description_en:
The suspension of a motor vehicle:

- is located between the chassis and the wheels (both front and rear)
- helps make driving more comfortable and safer
- contributes to the steerability of the vehicle
- keeps the wheels in contact with the road surface
- absorbs shocks transmitted by unevenness in the road

Suspension can become ineffective through wear or after suffering excessively strong impacts.

A vehicle with ineffective suspension has problems with road holding.

Overloading the vehicle can cause the suspension to wear, break, or temporarily lose effectiveness.

A vehicle with ineffective suspension increases driver fatigue and may cause the low-beam headlights to be misaligned.

It is not true that suspension does not operate on straight roads.

It is not true that if the vehicle is overloaded, simply increasing the tyre pressure is enough to prevent suspension problems.

1260.title_en: Shock absorbers of a motor vehicle
1260.description_en:
Shock absorbers of a motor vehicle reduce the oscillations of the suspension and help the vehicle hold the road.

Overloading the vehicle can make shock absorbers ineffective or cause them to wear out early.

It is not true that the driver can adjust the stiffness of the shock absorbers themselves. To do so, the driver must go to a specialist workshop.

Worn-out shock absorbers:

- cause abnormal behaviour during braking, especially in bends
- cause uneven tread wear on the tyres
- increase the risk of suspension spring breakage
- reduce passenger ride comfort
- worsen road holding

It is not true that sealed-circuit shock absorbers need no maintenance.

It is not true that if the vehicle is overloaded, simply increasing the tyre pressure is enough to prevent shock absorber problems.

1261.description_en:
The steering wheel can be adjusted for height.

If the power steering malfunctions, the steering becomes 'heavy'.

If a tyre punctures, the steering pulls toward the side of the punctured wheel.

To ensure road safety, check periodically that there is no abnormal play in the steering.

Excessive play in the steering makes the vehicle's path imprecise.

'Hard' steering can indicate insufficient tyre pressure.

Hydraulic power steering does not work when the engine is off.

Wheel toe-in affects steering precision.

If the steering vibrates, have the front wheel balance checked.

Power steering helps control the vehicle's path if a tyre punctures.

Steering precision is affected by poor condition of the suspension and shock absorbers. It is not affected by low lubricating oil pressure or excessive coolant temperature.

1263.description_en:
It is inadvisable to place objects under the driver's seat, because they may slide while driving and get in the way of the driver's movements.

Using a mobile phone without a hands-free kit or earpiece is prohibited while driving.

Satellite navigation systems must be programmed before setting off.

When transporting children, it is advisable to engage the child safety lock, which prevents the doors from being opened from inside the vehicle.

The air conditioning can be usefully used in winter as well, to quickly defrost the windscreen.

Stickers, hanging charms, or other objects attached to the vehicle's windows can reduce the driver's visibility.

Clean, transparent windows give better visibility outside the vehicle.

Check the wiper blades and replace them if they are worn.

Check that the washer fluid reservoir always contains fluid to clean the windows.

It is not true that if the windscreen is covered in dust, the demisting system must be used.

Damage to the front windscreen must not be repaired with emergency solutions such as transparent adhesive tape.

Variable message panels give warnings of danger and may be mandatory (obligation, prohibition).

1264.description_en:
The exhaust system is designed to channel exhaust gases outward after reducing their toxicity, pressure and temperature, as well as to reduce the noise of the vehicle and reduce air pollution caused by exhaust gases.

A deteriorated silencer increases the noise pollution produced by motor vehicles. It must be replaced with another silencer of a type approved for that vehicle.

To replace the exhaust pipe, contact an authorized workshop.

Tampering with the exhaust system results in administrative penalties.



It is not true that:

- the exhaust system of electric vehicles requires more frequent maintenance than that of vehicles with internal combustion engines

- outside built-up areas, vehicles may be driven without a silencer

- the exhaust system must be entirely replaced at every lubricant change

- if the silencer's exhaust pipe develops a hole and you do not intend to replace it soon, it can be repaired by wrapping it with glass wool and insulating tape

1265.description_en:
- engine oil and brake fluid levels must be checked periodically

- the brake fluid level is checked by inspecting the dedicated transparent reservoir

- on some engines, the engine oil level can be checked through a dedicated sight window on the oil sump

- the lubricant level must be checked with the vehicle on level ground and after the engine has been switched off for several minutes

It is not true that:

- the engine oil level must be checked with the engine running

- they are not fitted with a brake fluid reservoir because braking is purely mechanical

- on air-cooled models, the coolant level can be checked through a dedicated window positioned between the engine's cooling fins

- no fluids need level checks because the reservoirs are sealed

1267.title_en: Drive chain in two-wheeled motor vehicles
1267.description_en:
- it connects the engine sprocket to the wheel sprocket

- its wear, lubrication and correct tension should be checked periodically

- if not lubricated, it may break

- if it shows signs of wear, it must be replaced, and the engine sprocket and wheel sprocket may also need to be replaced

- its sudden breakage can cause the rear wheel to lock, resulting in loss of control of the vehicle
